P01-007.remedy: boundary_rationale: retype the MT 2:9 element as the lawsuit's contention announcement rather than a verdict, and re-cut the rib-element list so no element is named that the span's bytes do not carry; replace the sentence denying any fresh imperative or formula with the per-term disposition the cut rule requires - the verse-initial messenger formula at oshb:Jer.2.5 relayed in the same divine mouth with no frame-owner change, and the witness-summons imperatives at oshb:Jer.2.10 and oshb:Jer.2.12 sounding inside the lawsuit rather than opening a fresh discourse frame. device_notes: add the paseq segs at MT 2:5 and MT 2:13 as count-only single-witness disclosure with no intra-verse position claim. P01-008.challenge_claim: The entry seam at Jer.2.14 rests on a rhetorical-mode observation rather than one of the book's tier-1 seam classes and the closer formula-adjacent rival close is never weighed; and six ketiv/qere verses fall inside the span undisclosed while the blanket denial of any discourse imperative or addressee shift is refuted by the bytes, with a title-stack sentence that blends two distinct objects and quotes neither.
P01-008.grounds: Disclosure, upheld and unconditional: six of the book's variant verses, carrying six notes, fall inside Jer.2.14-Jer.2.30 - MT 2:15, 2:16, 2:20, 2:24, 2:25, 2:27 - and none is disclosed. Two of them carry clauses the row argues and lists as evidence: נפשו נַפְשָׁהּ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.24, byte tier) and ילדתני יְלִדְתָּ֔נוּ (oshb:Jer.2.27, byte tier), unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere in each. One refinement: the row's engagement with those two verses is a bare motif label rather than a reading of the disputed forms, so the omission stands on the symmetry duty rather than on any mis-glossed variant. One paseq seg (MT 2:24) is undisclosed in the same class - a new finding. Denial, upheld on two of its four terms: no word-event formula falls inside the span (the formula's sites in these chapters are MT 1:4, 1:11, 1:13 and 2:1) and the chapter's only two messenger-formula verses both fall outside it, so those two terms hold; but addressee shifts stand. The span opens in the third person about Israel at MT 2:14, turns to feminine singular by עָזְבֵךְ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Jer.2.17, byte tier) and holds it to MT 2:25, turns to masculine singular with a vocative at וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ ... יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.28, byte tier), then to plural at כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.29, byte tier) and again at MT 2:30. Participant shift is a licensed cut class, and the second of these turns falls exactly at the setumah the row disclosed and then dismissed as accompanied by nothing. Imperative forms also stand inside the span at וּדְעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ (oshb:Jer.2.19), רְאִ֤י דַרְכֵּךְ֙ בַּגַּ֔יְא דְּעִ֖י (oshb:Jer.2.23) and מִנְעִ֤י רַגְלֵךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.25), all byte tier - content imperatives inside the address rather than fresh discourse frames, so the tier-1 class name the row uses is defensible while the sentence as written is not. Onset warrant, upheld: the row's own stated ground is a shift into a run of rhetorical questions, which is not a member of the tier-1 signal set, so a seventeen-verse span opens with no named tier-1 device. One refinement to the rival: closing at MT 2:29 on its closure formula is weaker than framed, because closure corroboration operates only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows and MT 2:30 supplies none; the gap in the rejected-alternative field is nonetheless real, and the stronger unweighed rival is the participant-shift seam at MT 2:28 / MT 2:29. Title stack, upheld: the bytes give נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.2.19, byte tier; sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) but נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Jer.2.22, byte tier; sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier) without the hosts element, so the later site is the lone member of the four-site object lacking it; the row's single parenthesised label covers both sites, drops the postpositive element that makes the shape a closure formula, and supplies no splice for either - a blended count object.
P01-008.remedy: device_notes: add variant-note disclosure for MT 2:15, 2:16, 2:20, 2:24, 2:25 and 2:27 (single-witness), and the paseq seg at MT 2:24 as count-only; split the title-stack sentence into its two objects, each with its own byte-tier splice from source under its own oshb: ref, the postpositive element retained, and each with its own digit and tier. boundary_rationale: replace the blanket denial with the per-term disposition the bytes support - no word-event formula and no messenger formula inside the span; imperative forms present at MT 2:19, 2:23 and 2:25 but not discourse frames; participant shifts present at MT 2:28 and MT 2:29 and dispositioned - and state the onset's warrant class explicitly as a non-tier-1 rhetorical-mode shift. strongest_rejected_alternative: add the participant-shift rival at MT 2:28 / MT 2:29, noting the coinciding setumah and the closure formula at MT 2:29, in place of or beside the metaphor-shift rivals. confidence: with no tier-1 device at the onset over a seventeen-verse span, hold at medium_low. Any change to the span itself is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption and is not author work. P01-009.challenge_claim: The row's stated warrant for its close improperly leans on the chapter division, which is never boundary evidence; and the onset warrant turns on an unquoted original-language shape-parallel, the variant note inside the span goes undisclosed, and a byte-true device crosses the rear seam undisclosed.
P01-009.grounds: The tier-4 item is upheld outright: the rationale says the close relies on the chapter boundary together with the topic shift, and the notes field repeats that the boundaries are argued from the imperative and the chapter close alone. Chapter division is tier-4 metadata and is never boundary evidence in either direction, so a field that makes it a co-warrant is defective irrespective of where the seam falls. The disclosure item is upheld: MT 2:33 carries a variant note, למדתי לִמַּ֖דְתְּ (oshb:Jer.2.33, byte tier), unpointed beside pointed, and the row argues that verse in prose and lists it as evidence with no disclosure; the row's parashah statement is otherwise exactly right - the layer is silent across MT 2:30-2:37 and the absence is correctly not read as counterevidence. The cross-seam item is upheld in substance and its digit refuted: שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ (oshb:Jer.2.35, byte tier) carries the return root two verses before this unit's close, on a seam whose next unit is built on that root, and the sentence saying the inventories carry nothing further leaves it undisclosed - a device straddling the seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed. But no single contiguous consonantal object returns the two verses the challenge claims for its anger-turning idiom: that pair stands at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) and the comparandum clause at MT 4:8 stands at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier); a two-verse count across two different spellings is a semantic-class count presented as a skeleton sweep, which the count discipline bars. The shape-parallel item is refined rather than upheld: the row does not claim one lexeme - it names a see-imperative and a hear-imperative and claims the same discourse-frame shape, imperative plus the word-of-YHWH as object, which is byte-true at both sites, שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier) and רְא֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier). What is defective is that this original-language construction claim, and the rejected alternative resting on it, cite the comparandum only under a translation ref with no witness splice and no tier, and name no swept object or digit; swept separately the hear-construction stands at 10 verses and the see-construction at 1 verse, skeleton tier, and both of those digits reproduce for the objects named.
P01-009.remedy: boundary_rationale: strike the chapter boundary from the close warrant and either re-warrant the close on content alone or state plainly that no content warrant closes the unit and carry the reduced confidence on that basis; add a byte-tier splice under oshb:Jer.2.4 for the comparandum and re-cut the shape claim so it names its object (imperative plus the word-of-YHWH as object) with per-lexeme digits and tier. device_notes: strike the appeal to the chapter close; add variant-note disclosure at oshb:Jer.2.33 (single-witness); add the cross-seam disclosure of the return-root form at oshb:Jer.2.35 with its own named object and digit, and do not carry a two-verse idiom count. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the renewed-onset argument so it names the swept construction and its digit. Any respan is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption. Test the cure must pass: no tier-4 appeal survives in any field; every original-language shape claim carries a byte-tier splice under its own witness ref; every digit reproduces for the object its own sentence names; the mark-disclosure sweep is clean for variants across Jer.2.31-Jer.2.37 - the four tests that killed the original.

P01-010.challenge_claim: The notes field drifts into process register with an unanchored positional row-count reference and an editorial-methodology statement; and a spelling-bound substring digit is presented as a root count carrying a book-wide earliest claim the bytes refute, while the onset argument leaves the verse's opening word and its closing formula unengaged and three of the span's five verses carry undisclosed variant notes.
P01-010.grounds: The count-object defect is upheld and is the heaviest item. The digit reproduces exactly for the contiguous consonantal run of the plene spelling (sweep: 41 verses, skeleton tier, earliest at Jer.3.1), but the sentence carrying it names its object as the return root, and that needle is spelling-bound: the root stands earlier in the immediately preceding material at וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.19, byte tier), יְשִׁיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Jer.2.24, byte tier) and שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ (oshb:Jer.2.35, byte tier). The earliest-in-the-book claim is therefore false at the level asserted, and an exclusivity claim is never dampened by naming a tier. Support-audit note: the same digit is reproducible for that needle, so reproducing it is not a check of the object - the object is what fails. The onset item is upheld: MT 3:1 opens on לֵאמֹ֡ר (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier), a bound speech-frame infinitive with no governing verb of speaking anywhere in the verse, and the same verse closes נְאֻם יְהֹוָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier). A verse-initial bound speech frame with no governing verb is a byte-true element sitting exactly at the seam and arguing dependence on what precedes, and the closing formula is a closure shape at the end of the span's opening verse; the row engages neither while resting its onset on the absence of a formula of its own. The disclosure item is upheld: MT 3:2, MT 3:4 and MT 3:5 each carry a variant note and none is disclosed, although the parashah layer was plainly read at MT 3:5, where the petuchah citation is correct as to type and verse and the layer is indeed silent inside MT 3:1-3:4 and at the front seam; no paseq seg falls anywhere in this chapter, so nothing is owed there. The register items are upheld: naming the following three units is a bare positional and count-based cross-row reference where the rule requires verse anchors, and the appeal to a held posture on the cluster's edges narrates an editorial stance rather than a feature of the text. New finding in the same sentence: it also places the cluster's close at Jer.4.4 and calls that this span's close, while this unit's span closes at Jer.3.5 - the self-reference is factually wrong as well as positional. The extent item is refined: the observation behind it is byte-true, since return-root forms stand at MT 2:35 before the claimed cluster and at MT 4:8 after it, but the two-verse skeleton digit offered for it does not reproduce for any single object.
P01-010.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the return-root sentence so it names the swept object exactly (the contiguous consonantal run of the plene spelling, skeleton tier, 41 verses, earliest at Jer.3.1) and either drop the root-level earliest claim or replace it with per-form sweeps, each naming its attested spelling and carrying its own digit; add byte-tier splices under oshb:Jer.3.1 for the verse-initial bound speech frame and for the closing formula, and disposition both against the no-formula warrant, disclosing the speech frame as a cross-seam dependence signal. device_notes: add variant-note disclosure for MT 3:2, MT 3:4 and MT 3:5 (single-witness); delete the reference to the following three units and replace it with verse anchors; delete the held-posture clause; correct the cluster-extent sentence so this unit's own close is named correctly and any extent claim carries a per-form object and digit. Test the cure must pass: every earliest or exclusivity claim reproduces for the object its own sentence names, swept per attested spelling; the register sweep returns clean on the positional, cross-part and editorial-narration arms; the mark-disclosure sweep is clean for variants across Jer.3.1-Jer.3.5 - the three tests that killed the original.

P01-011.challenge_claim: One item challenges (low) that the declared false positive on the missing ketiv/qere disclosure is wrong: the note at oshb:Jer.3.7 is live, stands immediately before the clause the entry argues in prose, and carries the reading both witnesses render; secondarily, that filing the reign anchor under a date-frame signal key overstates it. The paired item supports the entry and confirms the same omission as a heuristic false positive, on the ground that the entry only paraphrases that verse's content and cuts no boundary there.
P01-011.grounds: Same object, opposite dispositions; the bytes decide for the challenge and refute the declared false positive. The variant inventory carries exactly one note at MT 3:7, and the bytes show the unpointed ketiv beside the pointed qere, ותראה וַתֵּ֛רֶא (oshb:Jer.3.7, byte tier), standing immediately before בָּגוֹדָ֥ה אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.7, byte tier) - the clause boundary_rationale quotes in the second witness and lists at web:Jer.3.7 among its evidence refs. A rendered quotation covering a variant verse with no variant disclosure in any field of the entry is the condition this book's citation discipline warns on, and that machine warn fires here, on this entry alone among the four adjudicated in this attempt; so the omission is a live disclosure gap, not a heuristic artifact, and the narrower test the supporting item applies - disclosure owed only where the disputed word is quoted verbatim or a boundary is cut at that verse - is not the disclosure symmetry this book runs. Severity holds at low on the bytes: both readings are the same narrative verb, the ketiv differing by a final he alone, so no sense the entry relies on turns on the choice, and this unit's seams stand at Jer.3.6 and Jer.3.11, not at Jer.3.7. The secondary point holds as well: the anchor reads בִּימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.3.6, byte tier), an in-the-days-of construction naming a single reign, not the year-formula or bet-plus-cardinal shape that defines this book's byte-derived date-header object, whose 19 candidate sites do not include this verse - so both halves of the date_frame.reign_sequence key overstate the signal. The seam warrant is untouched: the fresh speech-introduction verb with the addressee turn to the prophet is byte-true and remains the driver.
P01-011.remedy: device_notes: add the ketiv/qere disclosure for the one note at MT 3:7 (single-witness), naming the qere as the reading both witnesses carry and stating that this unit's seams do not turn on it; keep the existing petuchah disclosure unchanged. observed_substrate_signals: drop date_frame.reign_sequence - the byte-derived date-header object does not carry this site and the verse names one reign, not a sequence - and leave the reign anchor in boundary_rationale prose only; narrative_frame.addressee_shift stays, so this is not a driver swap and unit_type, confidence, and strongest_rejected_alternative do not re-open. Tests the cure must pass: the entry must no longer carry a rendered quotation covering a variant verse with no variant disclosure in any field (the condition that raised the original warn), and every retained substrate key must name a signal the byte-derived inventories carry at this site.

P01-012.challenge_claim: One item challenges (high) that the one-unit warrant rests on a blanket no-imperative and no-addressee-shift statement the pointed bytes contradict twice inside the span; that the doubled ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.3.19, the verse the rejected rival turns on, is undisclosed; that the rival is dismissed on a translation-side ground with its Hebrew pivot unquoted; and that splice and gloss extents part company at oshb:Jer.3.12. The paired item supports the same entry, holding that neither the imperative at Jer.3.12 nor the call at Jer.3.14 carries a fresh addressee, formula, or scene change, and that the Jer.3.19 rival was correctly declined.
P01-012.grounds: Same object, opposite dispositions, and the bytes decide for the challenge. boundary_rationale claims that no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides the restoration promise and the reflection from the invitation that opens the unit; two of its three terms are byte-false. אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier) is a fresh feminine-singular imperative, and שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) is a fresh plural imperative with a fresh plural vocative against the feminine-singular addressee of שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier). The plural second person in fact already stands inside the earlier verse's own tail, וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier) - one verse earlier than the challenge locates the shift - and the second witness renders all of it number-blind. The third term holds: no word-event formula and no messenger-formula onset falls inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20, so the cure is a re-cut of the negative, not its reversal. The variant point holds too: the inventory carries two notes at MT 3:19, one of this book's twelve doubled-note verses, and the bytes give תקראו תִּקְרְאִי and תשובו תָשֽׁוּבִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) - two second-person number alternations sitting on exactly the addressee question the cohesion sentence gets wrong, in the one verse the rejected alternative is built on, disclosed in no field. No count, slice, or rendered quotation covers that verse, so the mechanical disclosure arms stay silent there; the omission is material on content, not on the machine. The rival is raised on the rendering's fresh quotation mark, a tier-4 signal that is never evidence, while the Hebrew pivot at that verse, וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) - the emphatic independent pronoun the entry names but never quotes - goes unweighed. Extent: the Jer.3.12 splice stops on the bound noun of נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), severing it from the divine name, while the rendering beside it runs to the end of the verse; a second extent miss, named in neither item, runs the other way at the onset, where the splice carries the speech-introduction frame וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) that its rendering omits. High severity is proportionate: the failed sentence is this unit's own cohesion warrant, and every further leg lands on the same addressee question.
P01-012.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the blanket negative with a positive cohesion warrant - the single divine speech opened at Jer.3.11 runs on with no onset formula anywhere inside the span - and state the imperative at Jer.3.13, the imperative-with-vocative at Jer.3.14, and the singular-to-plural addressee turn explicitly, with the disposition that keeps them inside the unit. device_notes: disclose the two variant notes at MT 3:19 (single-witness; a doubled-note verse), naming both as second-person number alternations, since the contested addressee reading and the rejected rival both stand on that verse. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-argue the Jer.3.19 rival from its emphatic pronoun-plus-perfect pivot rather than from the rendering's quotation mark, and name the closer rival at Jer.3.14; one sentence plus the mandated rival-disclosure sentence only. Splices: re-cut the Jer.3.12 pair so the rendering opens and closes where the splice does and no splice terminates on a construct severed from its nomen rectum, and extend the Jer.3.11 rendering to cover the speech-introduction frame the splice already carries. Tests the cure must pass: no negative claim about imperatives or addressee inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20 survives that the pointed bytes contradict (the test that killed the original); every variant verse the entry argues from carries its disclosure; each splice and its rendering share their opening and closing words. A re-span at Jer.3.14 is a PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit boss adoption - it is not author work.

P01-013.challenge_claim: One item challenges (medium) that the renewed-call claim at oshb:Jer.3.22 is unanchored and untiered, since the same three-word call stands at oshb:Jer.3.14 on the far side of this unit's own front seam, leaving a byte-true device straddling that seam undisclosed; and, second, that the bare-heights noun is quoted here in its plene spelling while the same imagery earlier in the chapter is defective, with neither spelling named. The paired item supports the entry, holding the front seam a licensed speaker-and-scene shift with its mark statements exact.
P01-013.grounds: The first leg is upheld, the second refuted. Upheld: שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) and שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) are identical at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier - the noun's dagesh and the accents differ - and a skeleton-tier sweep of the three-word run returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, those two. The prior site stands inside the block this unit's front seam separates it from, so a byte-true device straddles that seam and argues continuity against it; calling the later site renewed names the recurrence without its prior verse and without a tier, and the byte-tier label carried by the splice proves the quotation, not the recurrence. Refuted: the spelling leg identifies no defect in this entry. Both forms are attested - the plene at Jer.3.21 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) against the defective at Jer.3.2 (skeleton sweep: 4 verses) - but no field of this entry makes a count, recurrence, or exclusivity claim about that noun; the per-spelling discipline binds sweeps and recurrence claims, and the only claim attached to the word here is a verse quotation that collates at byte tier against its own cited ref. Severity stays medium on the surviving leg, which lands on the completeness of the front-seam warrant rather than on prose hygiene. The seam itself survives: the turn from first-person divine promise at Jer.3.20 to third-person narrated report at Jer.3.21 is byte-true, the setumah at MT 3:25 is the correct type, and the parashah and variant inventories are genuinely empty across Jer.3.21-Jer.3.25, exactly as disclosed.
P01-013.remedy: boundary_rationale (or device_notes, if the disclosure is grouped there): replace the bare renewed with a verse-anchored, tier-labelled recurrence statement - the same call stands at Jer.3.14, identical at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses) - and state its disposition: the shared call argues continuity across this unit's front seam, which is carried instead by the speaker turn at Jer.3.21. Tests the cure must pass: no recurrence adjective survives without its prior verse and its tier (the test that killed the original), and the front-seam warrant must still stand on the page once the counter-signal is disclosed beside it. No boundary change is proposed, and the spelling observation needs no field change.

P02-001.challenge_claim: Two distinct items. One challenges (medium) a register lapse: pipeline part-and-row vocabulary standing in place of the literary self-reference, said to repeat across all four prose fields. The other challenges (medium) the parenthesis denying any address or formula shift at Jer.4.7 - holding that the second person turns from plural to feminine singular there and the speaking voice moves with it, while the entry keeps high confidence on that denial - and adds that the variant note at oshb:Jer.4.5 is placed on this unit's opening imperative when it sits on the verse's third imperative.
P02-001.grounds: Distinct defects, not one: register on the one side, byte claims on the other. Both are real, and each item's own count-object needs correcting. Byte leg, upheld: the summons commands a plural throughout - הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier) and שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס צִיּ֔וֹנָה הָעִ֖יזוּ אַֽל תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) - while Jer.4.7 turns to feminine-singular suffixes, אַרְצֵךְ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרַ֥יִךְ (oshb:Jer.4.7, byte tier), a change consonantally certain in the final kaf where a plural addressee would carry mem; and the voice moves with it, from divine first person at כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִצָּפ֖וֹן (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) through third-person description to a first-person-plural speaker naming YHWH in the third person at כִּ֥י לֹא שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ (oshb:Jer.4.8, byte tier), before the divine formula returns at Jer.4.9. The formula half of the denial holds - no onset formula stands at Jer.4.7 - so the parenthesis fails on address, not on formula, and it survives only in the second witness, which is number-blind there and is tier-4 ground that is never evidence. The variant locative in device_notes is byte-false as well: the note at MT 4:5 rides on ותקעו תִּקְע֥וּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier), not on the verse-opening imperative that carries this unit's own warrant, while boundary_rationale states the same note correctly - so the entry contradicts itself across two fields. Correcting that item's own object: the qere sits on the fourth imperative form of the verse, third only under a bare-imperative object the item did not name. Register leg, upheld in substance with its object corrected: the pipeline vocabulary stands in three prose fields, not four - boundary_rationale (a writer part named as the thing that opens, and a following unit called a fresh row), strongest_rejected_alternative (a candidate split called its own row), and device_notes (three further uses) - while literature_type_guess is clean. P02-017.challenge_claim: No byte claim in the row is false and the seam stands, but three defects: the English gloss set beside the Jer.6.6 splice covers neither end of what was spliced, dropping the four-word formula that opens it and adding a mound clause the splice does not contain; the formula the warrant rests on is a subordinated shape opening on a causal connective, quoted but not engaged, against the bare verse-initial formula at Jer.6.9, and the two are separate objects book-wide (29 verses against 153); and the frame-owner change that actually makes Jer.6.6 an onset, the besiegers' cry giving way to divine speech, is left implicit when a formula warrant owes the mouth.
P02-017.grounds: Re-derived from the source bytes. The row's splice is the first seven words of MT 6:6 and re-collates at byte tier (oshb:Jer.6.6). Limb one is upheld and is the load-bearing defect: the English set beside that splice covers neither end of it. The splice opens on כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), five words the gloss renders not at all, while the gloss's tail, “and cast up a mound against Jerusalem” (web:Jer.6.6), answers וְשִׁפְכ֥וּ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סֹלְלָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), four words that stand later in the verse and are not inside the splice. Fidelity is not the problem - the English is verbatim against the staged receiving text and carries its ref in the same field - the problem is extent, in both directions, and the unglossed head is exactly the formula the warrant rests on. Limb two is REFUTED on the bytes: the connective-plus-formula shape is attested at 29 verses book-wide (sweep: 29 verses, MT keys) and stands verse-initial at 28 of them, the one non-initial site being MT 24:8, so at MT 6:6 it is the book's standard subordinated-onset shape and not a buried subordinate clause; and the 29-verse shape is a strict subset of the 153-verse formula census (sweep: 153 verses, MT keys), a shape within its superset rather than a separate object. MT 6:6 also carries the plain armies title, a member of the 50-verse formula-plus-title set (sweep: 50 verses, MT keys), so both recorded substrate-signal keys are byte-correct here; the bare verse-initial כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.6.9, byte tier) is a second onset three verses on, not a standard the seam fails. Limb three REFINES: the incoming mouth is in fact given - the splice carries the divine name and title and the prose calls the speech divine - so what is missing is the OUTGOING frame owner, the attacking force's own summons at ק֖וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה (oshb:Jer.6.4, byte tier) and ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַלָּ֔יְלָה וְנַשְׁחִ֖יתָה (oshb:Jer.6.5, byte tier), which both witnesses render in the first person plural as the attackers' own speech; the ruled granularity licenses this cut on a frame-owner CHANGE, and the change is asserted without the party being changed from ever being named. NEW FINDING, raised by neither item: the ground given for rejecting the strongest rival is byte-inexact at the exact verse the rival would cut. The rival is answered by saying the closing imperative is addressed to the same city already under address, but at MT 6:6 the city is governed by a preposition and is then spoken OF in the third person at הִ֚יא הָעִ֣יר הָפְקַ֔ד (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), the verse closing on בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), and MT 6:7 continues third-person of her, whereas MT 6:8 names her as the vocative of a directly addressed imperative, הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier), with second-person suffixes at מִמֵּ֑ךְ and אֲשִׂימֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier) that both witnesses render as address to the city. The addressee therefore CHANGES at MT 6:8, which is the ruled tier-1 explicit-addressee-shift class - the rival's live ground, and the one the row never answers. Verified sound and not disturbed: the setumah at MT 6:5 on the front seam and the petuchah at MT 6:8 on the row's own close are both correctly typed, kept apart, and held tier-3 single-witness non-driving; the inventory records exactly 1 variant note at MT 6:7 and the bytes bear it out, the unpointed reading standing immediately before the pointed one, disclosed without being quoted; and span-relevant disclosure symmetry is complete - the chapter's paseq segs stand at MT 6:1, 6:11, 6:14 and 6:16 (inventory: 4 segs in the chapter, 0 in span), and the inventories carry 0 special letters and 0 exegesis notes anywhere in MT 6:6-6:8. The seam stands; nothing here moves it.
P02-017.remedy: Three field edits, no respan. (1) boundary_rationale - bring quote and gloss to one extent at MT 6:6: extend the Hebrew splice through the mound clause so it covers the English already offered, and add the receiving text's own rendering of the formula as its own balanced curly run in the same field, “For Yahweh of Armies said,” (web:Jer.6.6). CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): run the Hebrew word-run against the English word-run at MT 6:6 - every spliced word must have English beside it and every English word Hebrew behind it, with 0 words unmatched at either end; the extended splice must still return byte tier on re-collation; each curly run must be balanced and verbatim against the staged folded receiving text with a web: ref in the same field. CURE TEST: the outgoing mouth is named, not implied, and every verse argued in prose outside Jer.6.6-Jer.6.8 appears in boundary_evidence_refs. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative - replace the ground: the present sentence asserts the closing imperative addresses the same city already under address, which the bytes contradict (third-person reference to the city at Jer.6.6-Jer.6.7 against direct vocative address at Jer.6.8). Re-ground on what survives the shift - the mouth is unchanged, no fresh speech formula intervenes, and the Masoretic paragraph layer brackets Jer.6.6-Jer.6.8 as one segment (tier-3, single-witness, non-driving). CURE TEST: the sentence no longer asserts continuous address to the city, the ground given survives an explicit addressee shift at Jer.6.8, and the field stays within one sentence plus at most the mandated rival-disclosure second sentence. Then re-check confidence, presently high: if the rival is answered only by the unchanged mouth plus tier-3 paragraph corroboration, high is not carried and medium is the supported posture. P02-019.challenge_claim: The stated ground that no tier-1 marker stands inside web:Jer.6.10-Jer.6.15 is byte-false at three points, and the rival-rejection sentence turns the modern English paragraph division into an affirmative reason for keeping the material together.
P02-019.grounds: All three sites re-derive from the bytes. oshb:Jer.6.12 closes נְאֻם יְהוָֽה at byte tier, the chapter's only postpositive divine formula (sweep: 162 verses book-wide; 1 in this chapter, at oshb:Jer.6.12); oshb:Jer.6.15 closes אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה at byte tier; oshb:Jer.6.11 carries the imperative שְׁפֹ֤ךְ at byte tier. The tier-4 leg is upheld without narrowing: a modern paragraph division is never-evidence in either direction, and here it is carrying affirmative weight.
P02-019.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace both negative-existence phrases with the byte-true statement - the span carries the imperative at oshb:Jer.6.11, the postpositive divine formula closing oshb:Jer.6.12, and the amar-YHWH close at oshb:Jer.6.15 - and state why none of them cuts (closure corroboration with no fresh tier-1 onset at oshb:Jer.6.13). P02-021.challenge_claim: Two items. (a) unit_type judgment_oracle is an undisclosed operative-category deviation because the span pronounces no judgment of its own and matches the closed vocabulary's trial_speech instead. (b) An addressee turn of exactly the class used to cut the front seam falls inside the span at oshb:Jer.6.20, which addresses the offerers and not the witnesses summoned at oshb:Jer.6.18-Jer.6.19, while the backward force of the consequence particle opening oshb:Jer.6.18 goes unweighed at high confidence.
P02-021.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defect claims and they do not both survive. Item (a) is REFUTED on the bytes: oshb:Jer.6.19 carries הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה at byte tier, rendered “Behold, I will bring evil on this people, even the fruit of their thoughts” (web:Jer.6.19) - a first-person divine announcement of coming disaster standing inside the span - so the premise that no judgment content is pronounced anywhere in the span is byte-false, judgment_oracle is a defensible per-bytes typing of a summons-plus-announcement-plus-indictment shape, no closed-vocabulary deviation arises, and no disclosure is owed. Item (b) is UPHELD. oshb:Jer.6.18 summons שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם and, under its own imperative, וּדְעִ֥י עֵדָ֖ה; oshb:Jer.6.19 summons שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ while its body speaks of הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה in the third person; oshb:Jer.6.20 then turns to second-person-plural possessors עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ and וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם, rendered “Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices are not pleasing to me.” (web:Jer.6.20). The same addressee-shift class is what cuts this unit's front seam, so the criterion is applied inconsistently and the internal turn is disclosed nowhere. The consequence particle opening oshb:Jer.6.18 (sweep: 55 verses book-wide; 3 in this chapter, at oshb:Jer.6.15, oshb:Jer.6.18, oshb:Jer.6.21) binds the summons back to the refusal reported at oshb:Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17 and, unlike oshb:Jer.6.21, carries no formula overriding it; with neither weight weighed, high confidence is not calibrated. P02-024.challenge_claim: The unifying ground, a communal first-person-plural voice across the span, is carried by 1 of the span's 2 verses: oshb:Jer.6.25 has no first-person forms, and its two variant notes fall precisely on the addressee number that the unit label and the back seam both rest on.

The seam warrant therefore survives; what fails is the discriminating clause and the undisclosed continuity, and the severity attaches to the disclosure defect, not to the boundary.
P02-025.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete or re-cut the clause declaring the verse distinct from the communal first-person-plural voice of Jer.6.24-Jer.6.25, and disclose instead that the verse's own closing first-person-plural suffix at oshb:Jer.6.26 continues the communal voice of oshb:Jer.6.24 across the front seam while the vocative-plus-imperative onset carries the cut. P03-002.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the claim that the closing verse keeps the same referent as the prohibition and replace it with the byte-true referents - this people at oshb:Jer.7.16 against this place at oshb:Jer.7.20 - resting retention on the consequence connective and the unchanged divine speaker. device_notes: disclose that the place-noun catchword reaches back across the front seam to oshb:Jer.7.14 and is argued against rather than ignored, and disclose that oshb:Jer.7.20 is the book's single koh-amar adonai-YHWH stack site with a digit-bearing sweep count naming the object and unit; add count-only single-witness paseq disclosure for MT 7:16 and MT 7:20 (2 segs; no intra-verse position claim). P03-004.challenge_claim: The row names the feminine-singular addressee at its onset as personified Zion, a name absent from the chapter's bytes; and the judgment formula at oshb:Jer.7.32 is called recurring with a tier label but no count.
P03-004.grounds: Both confirmed. The form claim itself is byte-true: גָּזִּ֤י נִזְרֵךְ֙ וְֽהַשְׁלִ֔יכִי וּשְׂאִ֥י at oshb:Jer.7.29, byte tier, carries three feminine-singular imperatives and a feminine-singular suffix, so the address change at the onset is real. P03-004.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the named referent with the byte-attested description - an unnamed feminine-singular addressee - or, if an identification is retained, mark it as inference and cite the sweep showing the name is absent from the chapter. Attach a digit-bearing sweep count in the sanctioned form to the recurrence claim for the formula at oshb:Jer.7.32, naming the swept object and its unit. device_notes: add count-only single-witness paseq disclosure for MT 7:34, MT 8:1 and MT 8:2 (3 segs; no intra-verse position claim).
