P03-007.challenge_claim: The stated reason for ending the unit at web:Jer.9.2 is contradicted by the unit's own closing verse, because the third-person accusation placed after the seam already begins inside it; the seam-adjacent parashah evidence is disclosed on only one of the two sides, the mark at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 going unmentioned while the mark at oshb:Jer.8.17 is disclosed; and two prose coordinates inside the numbering zone are left bare of any dual or qualifier.
P03-007.grounds: Re-derived from bytes; three legs, and they do not fall together. LEG 1 (real, but narrower than claimed). The accusation is byte-true inside the closing verse: כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2, “For they are all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.” (web:Jer.9.2). But it stands as a subordinate causal clause under the first-person wish frame that opens that same verse, מִֽי יִתְּנֵ֣נִי (byte tier), the frame that also opens oshb:Jer.8.23 = web:Jer.9.1 with מִֽי יִתֵּ֤ן (byte tier); the contiguous interrogative-plus-yiqtol wish family stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide, those two adjacent sites and no other (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys oshb:Jer.8.23 and oshb:Jer.9.1). The verse after the seam is a different thing again: oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 opens verse-initially with וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ (byte tier), a third-person main clause carrying no wish frame at all, and closes וְאֹתִ֥י לֹֽא יָדָ֖עוּ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte tier), where the first person has become Yahweh's own and is sealed by the postpositive divine formula. So the discriminator has to be cut at the speaker-frame level, not at the presence of third-person description: what changes at the cut is who speaks, a tier-1 participant and speaker change, and it falls exactly there. Two byte facts leave that the only warrant available: across oshb:Jer.8.18-oshb:Jer.9.1 there is no speech formula and no postpositive divine formula (sweep: 152 verses carry the koh-amar-YHWH skeleton book-wide, 0 of them in this span, the nearest after it four verses past the seam at oshb:Jer.9.6 = web:Jer.9.7; sweep: 162 verses carry the neum-YHWH skeleton book-wide, 0 of them in this span, the formula standing at oshb:Jer.8.17 immediately before it and at oshb:Jer.9.2 immediately after it). What survives of the challenge is therefore this: the stated warrant names a feature the unit's own closing clause contains, and that straddling accusation goes undisclosed as cross-seam continuity. What does not survive is the word contradicted — the seam is tier-1 grounded on the speaker change and is not disturbed. LEG 2 (refuted on bytes). The two marks are not a symmetric pair and cannot be read as two sides of one disclosure. The setumah at oshb:Jer.8.17 closes the verse immediately preceding the unit, so it is seam-coincident with the front cut. The unit's closing verse, oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2, carries 0 parashah marks, so there is no back-seam mark to disclose; the setumah at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 closes the verse after the unit and is span-relevant to the unit beginning at web:Jer.9.3, which does disclose it. Inside oshb:Jer.8.18-oshb:Jer.9.1 the single-witness layers are empty: 0 parashah marks, 0 paseq segs, 0 variant notes, so the span-relevant disclosure set is already complete, and the mark cited is corroboration, not a driver (tier-3, single-witness, petuchah and setumah kept distinct; absence is not counterevidence). LEG 3 (real, low, not the breach implied). The two bare coordinates exist and both resolve on the WEB side inside the zone. But the unit carries 3 dual-cited zone pairs, web:Jer.9.3 = oshb:Jer.9.2, oshb:Jer.8.23 = web:Jer.9.1 and oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2, each arithmetically right on the injective crosswalk, and it clears the zone-disclosure enforcement under a live-arm control check (a control copy with those duals stripped fails on 3 refs; a control copy with 1 dual mis-set fails on its arithmetic), structured references being the object the Tier-0 zone rule governs. The bare prose digits are an ambiguity residue below that threshold, cheap to cure and inconsistent with the dual practice used two sentences earlier, not a Tier-0 failure. FURTHER DEFECT, not raised in the challenge: the rival-alternative sentence weighs 1 rival, the chapter-division rival at web:Jer.8.22, while the live rival at the contested seam is the other one, closing at web:Jer.9.1 = oshb:Jer.8.23 so the wayfarers' lodge wish travels with the indictment its own subordinate clause introduces. That rival is what the bytes make available here, and it goes unweighed.
P03-007.remedy: boundary_rationale — replace the closing sentence. State that the unit ends at web:Jer.9.2 = oshb:Jer.9.1 because the first-person wish frame governing oshb:Jer.8.18-oshb:Jer.9.1 stops there and web:Jer.9.3 = oshb:Jer.9.2 opens a verse-initial third-person main clause whose own first person is Yahweh's, closed by the postpositive divine formula (tier-1; splice the pointed run from the source, never re-key it), not because third-person description of the people begins there. In the same sentence disclose that the third-person accusation already stands, subordinated, in the unit's own closing clause and so straddles the seam. TEST (the test that killed the original): read the corrected sentence against the bytes of oshb:Jer.9.1 and oshb:Jer.9.2 side by side — it must name no feature that oshb:Jer.9.1 itself contains, and the straddling accusation must be disclosed; the original fails both arms. strongest_rejected_alternative — re-aim it at the back-seam rival (closing at web:Jer.9.1 = oshb:Jer.8.23, the wayfarers' lodge wish going with the indictment it introduces), within the existing one-sentence limit. TEST: the rival named must be the one the bytes make live at the contested seam, not the chapter-division rival at web:Jer.8.22. boundary_rationale and device_notes — give the two bare in-zone coordinates their qualifier: web:Jer.9.3 = oshb:Jer.9.2 in the rationale, web:Jer.9.2 = oshb:Jer.9.1 in the device note. TEST: no coordinate touching WEB ch 9 or MT 8:23 / MT ch 9 stands in any field without a witness prefix or dual, and each dual's arithmetic checks on the crosswalk. NO RESPAN IS ORDERED — web:Jer.8.18-web:Jer.9.2 stands on this evidence; any boundary change is a proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work. device_notes keeps its existing setumah disclosure at oshb:Jer.8.17 unchanged (correct and seam-coincident) and adds nothing about oshb:Jer.9.2, which lies outside this span. observed_substrate_signals needs no edit unless the corrected warrant is recorded as a new signal key, in which case it changes in the same edit.

P03-008.challenge_claim: Two items on one row. First: the rejected-alternative sentence names a neighbouring unit by its position rather than by verse, a register violation, while the seam itself is otherwise byte-warranted. Second: the front-seam warrant is contradicted by the bytes the row itself quotes -- third-person description already runs in the immediately preceding verse and the row's opening word is a consecutive form binding it to that clause -- and the parashah seg called the opening mark sits at the wrong seam.
P03-008.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one, and they do not stand at the same strength. (a) The register item stands exactly as filed and needs no reframing: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'kept together as the row before this one', a cross-unit reference by position where the standing rule requires verse anchoring. (b) The mark-position item stands exactly as filed, and the keying convention it rests on is provable from the inventory itself: a seg is recorded against the verse it FOLLOWS. At the book's eleven parent-frame seams the frame-final verse carries a seg 11 times out of 11 (oshb:Jer.1.3, oshb:Jer.6.30, oshb:Jer.10.25, oshb:Jer.17.27, oshb:Jer.20.18, oshb:Jer.24.10, oshb:Jer.29.32, oshb:Jer.33.26, oshb:Jer.39.18, oshb:Jer.45.5, oshb:Jer.51.64) and the frame-initial verse 0 times out of 11 (parashah tier-3, single-witness). Under that keying the SAMEKH at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 falls after the span's FIRST verse -- inside the row -- while the front seam itself carries no seg (inventory: 0 segs at oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2; absence is never counterevidence). The closing SAMEKH at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 does stand at the back seam. Both span segs are SAMEKH; no PE is in play here. device_notes' claim that setumot open and close the row is therefore half wrong, and the same key is carried in boundary_evidence_refs as front-seam corroboration. (c) The seam-warrant item is REFINED rather than upheld as framed. Both byte facts are true: oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2 closes in third-person plural description, כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים (byte tier), and the row's own opening word וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 (byte tier) carries the pointed vav plus patah with a doubled following consonant, the consecutive prefix pattern. But the third-person material before the seam sits inside that verse's subordinate causal clause serving the first-person wish, whereas oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 opens a fresh MAIN clause in third-person description. The warrant is therefore under-specified, not contradicted; what is genuinely absent is the disclosure, since a byte-true consecutive form straddling the row's own front seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and no field discloses it. (d) NEW, raised by neither item: the row's prose carries bare in-zone coordinates -- the seam 'could instead sit at 9.2 rather than 9.3', and 'a fresh koh-amar onset at 9.7'. Inside the offset zone a bare coordinate resolves to two different verses: read on the web side, 9.7 is the koh-amar onset (web:Jer.9.7 = oshb:Jer.9.6); read on the MT side it is the arrow verse carrying the zone's single ketiv/qere note (oshb:Jer.9.7 = web:Jer.9.8) and no koh-amar at all. The zone-disclosure arm is machine-enforced only on witness-prefixed refs, so prose coordinates of this shape pass unseen; the class recurs at P03-010, P03-011 and P03-013.
P03-008.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'kept together as the row before this one' with a verse-anchored formulation naming the two wish-cries at web:Jer.9.1 = oshb:Jer.8.23 and web:Jer.9.2 = oshb:Jer.9.1; no positional cross-unit reference may survive in any field. (2) device_notes AND boundary_evidence_refs: stop presenting oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 as this row's OPENING mark -- under the inventory's follow-the-verse keying that seg stands inside the span; say instead that the front seam carries no seg (absence is never counterevidence) and keep oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 as closing-seam corroboration, both SAMEKH, single-witness, tier-3. (3) boundary_rationale: scope the third-person warrant to the fresh main clause, and disclose the straddling consecutive form at the front seam with its tier. The span is NOT to be moved by this remedy: any respan (e.g. opening after the seg and the neum-YHWH tag at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3) is a proposal for boss adoption, never author work. (4) Add an explicit dual or numeric qualifier to every bare in-zone coordinate in this row's prose. TESTS the cure must pass: no positional or administrative cross-unit reference anywhere in the row; every parashah citation states which seam it stands at under the follow-the-verse keying; the front-seam warrant survives a full re-read of oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2 including its causal clause -- the read that killed the original; and no bare chapter.verse coordinate touching web ch 9 or MT 8:23 / MT ch 9 remains without a dual or numeric qualifier.

P03-010.challenge_claim: Both edges of the seam warrant lean on translation poetry-line layout, which is not evidence from either witness, while the Hebrew that would actually carry the prose-register claim is left unquoted.
P03-010.grounds: The layout digits are right and the objection to relying on them is right in principle: the translation carries 0 poetry lines across web:Jer.9.12 = oshb:Jer.9.11 through web:Jer.9.16 = oshb:Jer.9.15, against 3 at web:Jer.9.11 = oshb:Jer.9.10 and 2 at web:Jer.9.17 = oshb:Jer.9.16; poetry-line breaks are tier-4 translation formatting, never evidence in either direction, and the staged MT extract carries no layout layer, so nothing on the witness side underwrites a register contrast. But 'both edges lean on' it overstates the defect. The opening edge names a byte-spliced unformulaic interrogative onset, מִֽי הָאִ֤ישׁ הֶֽחָכָם֙ (oshb:Jer.9.11 = web:Jer.9.12, byte tier) -- a discourse-frame onset, tier-1. The closing edge names, in the same sentence as the layout remark, the next verse's own title-stack formula with a plural imperative, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ (oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, byte tier) -- tier-1 and wholly independent of layout. Both edges therefore already stand on witness signals; the layout is an impermissible CO-citation, not the load-bearing driver, and the boundary is not in question. The sharper locus, named by neither item, is a different field: observed_substrate_signals records narrative_frame.prose_interlude_in_poetic_context, which files a translation-layout fact into the substrate-signal register where tier-4 formatting can never sit; device_notes then repeats the same fact a third time.
P03-010.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the two layout clauses ('set in prose where the oracles on either side run in poetry'; 'returns to poetry'), retaining the opening interrogative onset at oshb:Jer.9.11 = web:Jer.9.12 and, at the close, the koh-amar-plus-imperative onset at oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, each with its splice and tier named. (2) observed_substrate_signals: drop narrative_frame.prose_interlude_in_poetic_context. oss is a dependent field of the driver set, so re-check the remaining keys, unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative after the edit. (3) device_notes: drop the poetry-line sentence, or restate it explicitly as translation formatting carrying no evidential weight in either direction. (4) Add the zone qualifier to the bare coordinates 9.16 and 9.17 in the prose. TEST the cure must pass: delete every layout sentence and the row's two edge warrants must still stand, each naming a byte-spliced witness signal with its tier -- the deletion that killed the original; and no field, prose or oss, may rest a boundary claim on poetry lines, paragraph breaks or verse numbering.

P03-011.challenge_claim: The addressee analysis is byte-wrong at the row's opening, the summons imperatives being plural forms addressed to the summoners rather than to the mourning women; the transliteration erases the feminine-plural morpheme that actually marks the turn to the women; and the closing splice runs past its gloss.
P03-011.grounds: The opening component is REFUTED on the row's own words. boundary_rationale glosses הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ וְקִרְא֥וּ לַמְקוֹנְנ֖וֹת (oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, byte tier) as 'consider, and call for the mourning women', treating the mourning-women noun as the OBJECT of the two plural imperatives -- which is exactly what the bytes carry. The row does not address the women at its opening and does not say it does. The defect the item is reaching for is real but sits one field away, in strongest_rejected_alternative, which speaks of 'the women of 9.17-21'. The women are spoken OF in the third person at oshb:Jer.9.17 = web:Jer.9.18, וּתְמַהֵ֕רְנָה (byte tier), with the benefit accruing to a first-person plural group, and oshb:Jer.9.18 = web:Jer.9.19 is a quoted cry from Zion; the address to the women themselves begins only at oshb:Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.20 with the feminine-plural imperative שְׁמַ֤עְנָה (byte tier). The rejected alternative therefore assigns three verses to an addressee the bytes withhold, and it contradicts the row's own rationale, which locates the turn correctly. The transliteration defect is real as filed: that same form is rendered 'shim'ah', dropping the ending that carries the feminine-plural addressee the argument depends on -- a byte-checkable form claim held to the same discipline as a digit. The gloss-extent defect is real as filed: the closing splice runs one preposition past its gloss and stops inside a construct chain, where the bytes read כְּדֹ֖מֶן עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה (oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, byte tier). Verified and left standing: the variant-formula disclosure is exact -- the bare-imperative-plus-neum consonantal run stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier), oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, against 152 verses for the koh-amar-YHWH shape (sweep: 152 verses, skeleton tier); and all three parashah citations are correctly positioned under the follow-the-verse keying (PE after oshb:Jer.9.15 = web:Jer.9.16 at the front seam, SAMEKH after oshb:Jer.9.18 = web:Jer.9.19 inside, SAMEKH after oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22 at the close; tier-3, single-witness).
P03-011.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the addressee description to the bytes -- the women are addressed from web:Jer.9.20 = oshb:Jer.9.19, not from web:Jer.9.17 = oshb:Jer.9.16 -- or drop the addressee contrast and rest the alternative on the continuity of the death image alone; the field must not contradict boundary_rationale. (2) boundary_rationale: re-transliterate the feminine-plural imperative at oshb:Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.20 with its full ending. (3) boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing pair so gloss extent equals splice extent -- either extend the splice through the whole prepositional phrase at oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22 and gloss it whole, or shorten the splice to the dung noun. (4) Add the zone qualifier to the bare coordinates 9.17-21, 9.21, 9.22 and 9.23 in the prose. TESTS the cure must pass: every transliteration reproduces the ending of the form it names; no splice extends past its gloss or terminates inside a construct chain; and the addressee claim in EVERY field survives a re-read of oshb:Jer.9.16-Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.17-Jer.9.20 -- the read that killed the original.

P03-013.challenge_claim: Two items on one row. First: boundary_rationale names the production plan's own segmentation of the book alongside the unit's own edge, a register violation, though the formula-driven boundaries and the nations-list disclosure are otherwise sound. Second: the cross-reference propping the opening warrant is an untiered recurrence claim carrying no sweep digit, and the two sites are not the same shape in the bytes, differing precisely in the verse-initial property the warrant rests on.
P03-013.grounds: Both items stand, and they are DISTINCT defects in two different sentences of the same field. (a) Register: boundary_rationale closes 'The row and the part both end at 9.26' -- an administrative division of the book, barred from row prose in every field. The sentence carries no textual content, so removing it costs the warrant nothing. (b) Recurrence: the row's opener הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים at oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25 (byte tier) is verse-initial. The site called the same shape reads לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ at oshb:Jer.7.32 = web:Jer.7.32 (byte tier): there the formula is prefixed by the therefore-particle and is NOT verse-initial, so the two sites differ in the one property the onset warrant leans on; the Hebrew is quoted at only one of them; and the claim carries neither a tier label nor a digit. The consonantal run stands in 15 verses book-wide (sweep: 15 verses, skeleton tier), 14 of them with the neum-YHWH tag attached (sweep: 14 verses, skeleton tier) -- a dense formula rather than a distinguishing onset marker, which the row does not say. The boundary itself is untouched by either item and holds independently: the preceding verse closes on its own neum-YHWH tag at oshb:Jer.9.23 = web:Jer.9.24 with a seg following it (parashah tier-3, single-witness) -- the closure-then-fresh-onset configuration the ruled granularity licenses -- and the roster and its verdict at oshb:Jer.9.25 = web:Jer.9.26 are one grammatical sentence. The same bare in-zone coordinate class flagged elsewhere in this cluster is live here too, in the very sentence at (a).
P03-013.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the closing sentence naming the row and the part; nothing textual is lost, and the bare in-zone coordinate goes with it. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the cross-reference -- either splice oshb:Jer.7.32 = web:Jer.7.32 alongside the opener and state the difference (therefore-particle prefix; not verse-initial) with the tier at which the two DO match, or drop the cross-reference and rest the onset on the verse-initial formula plus the neum-YHWH closure at oshb:Jer.9.23 = web:Jer.9.24. Any retained recurrence sentence carries a tier label and an adjacent digit naming the swept object and unit (the consonantal run: 15 verses). (3) If any in-zone coordinate survives anywhere in the prose, give it a dual or numeric qualifier. TESTS the cure must pass: the recurrence claim survives a side-by-side byte read of BOTH sites including the verse-initial property -- the read that killed the original; every recurrence or count sentence carries a tier and a digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit; and a register sweep finds no administrative, positional or file-order reference in any field.

P04-001.challenge_claim: The no-internal-seam warrant is falsified by the bytes the row itself quotes, a sustained singular address to Yahweh interrupting the plural addressees; the same warrant assigns the whole span to one speaker's mouth that the bytes contradict; and the Aramaic island's opening verb is mislabelled an imperative.
P04-001.grounds: The item stands. Form class: כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן at oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 (byte tier, Aramaic) carries the tav prefix and the paragogic nun of a prefix-conjugation form, and the translation renders it as a modal future, “You shall say this to them” (web:Jer.10.11); no morphology layer is staged, so the label stands or falls on the pointed bytes plus the two renderings, and neither supports 'citation imperative'. That label is also the sharper locus of the contradiction the item names, since the same rationale asserts that no additional discourse imperative interrupts the span while calling this form one: correcting the form class cures both at a single edit. Frame ownership: the row places the mockery in one mouth on the strength of the onset formula at oshb:Jer.10.2 (byte tier), but the span carries at least two further speaker positions the bytes will not put in that mouth -- second-person praise addressed TO Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.6, גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ (byte tier), continued at oshb:Jer.10.7, and third-person predication ABOUT Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.10, וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת (byte tier). A koh-amar claim that does not name which mouth carries which stretch is the one claim this book's formula census will not support. One qualification on the addressee half: the rationale DOES disclose the praise turn before denying an 'additional' one, so this is a self-contradictory criterion rather than a suppressed fact -- still a defect, and the return to the plural addressees at oshb:Jer.10.11 is a further undisclosed turn. The holding is not disturbed: a thematic register alternation is not a tier-1 seam, the default for frame-plus-speech is the larger unit, and the island disclosure is present and correct (inventory: 15 Aramaic-coded morphs, all in that one verse). NEW, raised by neither lens: observed_substrate_signals files the hear-the-word plural imperative of oshb:Jer.10.1 (byte tier) under a word-event key, although the word-event system is a closed set of three shapes that are never blended and a discourse-frame imperative is not one of them; across the book's candidate rows the discourse-imperative signal element appears in 31 oss entries, 28 of them under narrative_frame or speech_formula keys and 3 under a word-event key. Second new item: device_notes places the seg at oshb:Jer.10.11 'inside the span', where under the follow-the-verse keying it stands at the span's CLOSING seam.
P04-001.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-label the Aramaic opener at oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 as a prefix-conjugation (modal) form, not an imperative, and re-read the criterion sentence so it no longer denies a signal the same sentence names. (2) boundary_rationale: name the mouth per stretch -- the formula-owned mockery, the second-person praise at oshb:Jer.10.6-Jer.10.7, the third-person predication at oshb:Jer.10.10, and the return to the plural addressees at oshb:Jer.10.11 -- or restate the warrant to claim only that no fresh divine-speech formula, addressee-naming imperative or discourse frame opens a rival unit inside the span. No respan is ordered: the span stands. (3) observed_substrate_signals: re-file the oshb:Jer.10.1 discourse imperative out of the word_event family into the key family the corpus uses for that class, and carry the same order as its own sweep to every row whose oss carries word_event.discourse_imperative_onset (P04-001, P04-003, P04-008). oss is a dependent field, so re-check confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative after the edit. (4) device_notes: state the oshb:Jer.10.11 seg as standing at the closing seam, not inside the span. TESTS the cure must pass: every form-class label in the row is readable off the pointed bytes plus both renderings -- the read that killed the original; no sentence denies a signal the same row names; every koh-amar claim names whose mouth carries which verses; and the oss key set contains no word-event key that is not one of the three attested word-event shapes.

P04-002.challenge_claim: The twin cross-reference is an untiered recurrence claim that the consonantal evidence bears only in part, and the ketiv/qere note is argued from an English rendering that cannot register the variant.
P04-002.grounds: Both halves check out on the bytes. The narrow claim is exact: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ closes oshb:Jer.10.16 and the identical run closes oshb:Jer.51.19 (byte tier, both). The wider designation is not: of the five verse pairs, two are byte-identical (oshb:Jer.10.12 against oshb:Jer.51.15; oshb:Jer.10.15 against oshb:Jer.51.18) and three diverge already at skeleton tier -- oshb:Jer.10.13 carries the ketiv/qere doublet where oshb:Jer.51.16 has a single article-less noun, besides two divergent verb forms; oshb:Jer.10.14 carries the refiner noun plene against the defective spelling at oshb:Jer.51.17; and oshb:Jer.10.16 has the defective Jacob noun with an Israel noun before the tribe noun against the plene Jacob and no Israel noun at oshb:Jer.51.19. No tier is named anywhere on the recurrence claim, where campaign practice requires one on every recurrence sentence, so which of these the row asserts cannot be read off it. The ketiv/qere inference is falsified by the witnesses themselves. The note is inventory-true and both forms stand in the source bytes, מִקְצֵ֣ה ארץ הָאָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Jer.10.13. But the parallel verse carries the article-less מִקְצֵה אָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Jer.51.16 (byte tier), and the translation renders the two identically -- “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.10.13) and “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.51.16) -- so the English cannot register the article and is evidence for neither reading. A witness-internal variant is never adjudicated from a translation. The row's edges are unaffected: the participial opening is verse-initial at oshb:Jer.10.12 and the name-formula verse-final at oshb:Jer.10.16 (byte tier, both), and the seg keyed after oshb:Jer.10.11 stands at the front seam exactly as the row says (parashah tier-3, single-witness).
P04-002.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale and device_notes: tier-label the recurrence and scope it -- the closing name-formula is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.10.16 and oshb:Jer.51.19; if the wider pairing is kept as texture, state the tier at which it holds and that three of the five verse pairs diverge in the consonants. (2) device_notes: delete the inference that the qere supplies the definite reading carried into the English; the same English stands over the article-less parallel at oshb:Jer.51.16 = web:Jer.51.16. Retain the note as a single-witness disclosure of the two forms with no reading preferred. TESTS the cure must pass: every recurrence sentence names its tier and the extent it claims, and survives a byte comparison of all five verse pairs -- the comparison that killed the original; and no ketiv/qere, parashah or other witness-internal claim anywhere in the row is argued from an English rendering.

P04-004.challenge_claim: The unqualified statement that nothing before this verse addresses Yahweh in the second person is refuted by the bytes seventeen verses earlier in the same chapter, and the exclusivity is asserted without a swept object or a sweep count.
P04-004.grounds: The clause is false as written. oshb:Jer.10.6 reads כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ and oshb:Jer.10.7 opens מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ (byte tier, both): a second-person masculine independent pronoun, second-person suffixes on the name-noun and the preposition, and a second-person verbal object, and both witnesses render them as address rather than description -- “There is no one like you, Yahweh. You are great, and your name is great in might.” (web:Jer.10.6). Those verses stand seventeen verses before the row's onset, inside the row's own chapter and inside the same parent frame, so the stated front-seam discriminator does not survive its own chapter. The claim is separately defective as an exclusivity: a first/nothing-before assertion carries an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and the unit, and is never softened by a tier label; neither is present. The boundary is not in question and the item does not ask for one: a seg follows oshb:Jer.10.22 -- at the front seam under the follow-the-verse keying (parashah tier-3, single-witness) -- and the turn into first-person petition addressed to Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.23, יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier), carried on by the second-person imperatives of oshb:Jer.10.24-Jer.10.25, is a speaker-role and addressee change in its own right. The defect lies in the warrant, not in the edge.
P04-004.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the first-occurrence clause and rest the front-seam warrant on the change it can actually carry -- the turn out of third-person report of the northern rumour at oshb:Jer.10.22 into first-person petition addressed to Yahweh from oshb:Jer.10.23, with the splice and tier already in the field. (2) If any first / only / nothing-before claim is retained anywhere in the row, attach an adjacent sweep digit naming the swept object (second-person address to Yahweh) and the unit (verses), and state its scope explicitly. TESTS the cure must pass: the replacement warrant must survive a read of oshb:Jer.10.6-Jer.10.7 -- the read that killed the original -- and no universal or exclusivity claim may stand in any field without an in-sentence digit naming its object and unit.

P04-005.challenge_claim: The opening header is byte-perfect, but two byte-true catchwords cross this unit's closing seam undisclosed, the recurrence claim to the earlier header site carries no tier where one is owed, and confidence is set at high with the frontier flag unset.
P04-005.grounds: Both straddles verify. שִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את stands at oshb:Jer.11.2 inside the span and recurs beyond the cut at oshb:Jer.11.6 as שִׁמְע֗וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את -- skeleton-identical, not byte-identical -- and those are the only two verses in the book carrying the run (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). The summons שִׁמְע֤וּ בְקוֹלִי֙ at oshb:Jer.11.4 recurs beyond the cut at oshb:Jer.11.7 as שִׁמְע֖וּ בְּקוֹלִֽי, again skeleton-identical only (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier). Neither is disclosed in any field of the row, and a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the cut until it is. The counter-reading that this is ordinary sermon vocabulary rather than a device fails on the digit: a clause attested in exactly two verses book-wide is not ordinary vocabulary, and the disclosure duty does not depend on whether the device defeats the cut. The cut itself survives and should be said to survive: the fresh narrative reintroduction at oshb:Jer.11.6, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (byte tier; sweep: 13 verses, skeleton tier), reopens address after the prophet's own reply closes the exchange at oshb:Jer.11.5, and a seg follows oshb:Jer.11.5 at that seam (parashah tier-3, single-witness). The recurrence claim to the earlier header is untiered exactly where the strongest tier is available: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ opens oshb:Jer.11.1, and oshb:Jer.11.1 and oshb:Jer.7.1 are identical across the whole verse (byte tier), the header core standing in exactly 11 verses (sweep: 11 verses, skeleton tier). One qualification: the confidence setting is not an independent defect. confidence and frontier_flag_considered are dependent on the disclosure repair and are re-set after it, not found against on their own; the hard whole-chapter cap arm binds chapter-length spans, and this five-verse span is not one.
P04-005.remedy: (1) device_notes (or boundary_rationale): disclose both straddling runs by verse and tier -- the covenant-words summons at oshb:Jer.11.2 recurring at oshb:Jer.11.6 (skeleton tier; sweep: 2 verses) and the obey-my-voice summons at oshb:Jer.11.4 recurring at oshb:Jer.11.7 (skeleton tier; sweep: 4 verses) -- and state why they do not carry the unit across the seam: the reintroduction at oshb:Jer.11.6 reopens address after the reply at oshb:Jer.11.5. (2) boundary_rationale: tier-label the header recurrence as byte-identical to oshb:Jer.7.1 across the whole verse, with the family digit attached (sweep: 11 verses). (3) confidence and frontier_flag_considered: re-assess as dependent fields once (1) and (2) land. No boundary change is ordered. TESTS the cure must pass: the repaired row names every byte-true run that straddles either of its own seams, with the tier at which each matches; every recurrence sentence carries a tier and a digit; and the closing warrant must still stand with the straddling pair on the page -- the test the original never faced.

P04-006.challenge_claim: The closing verse is characterised as carrying a covenant curse although the curse lexeme reaches MT 11:3 and not MT 11:8 (skeleton sweep: 5 verses book-wide); the covenant-words catchword crossing the opening seam is undisclosed; and the closing-seam assertion that MT 11:9 opens with the same introduction again carries no splice and no tier, the two forms being skeleton-identical but not byte-identical.
P04-006.grounds: All three limbs verify on the bytes. MT 11:8 closes וָאָבִ֨יא עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶֽת כָּל דִּבְרֵ֧י הַבְּרִית הַזֹּ֛את (oshb:Jer.11.8, byte) — the covenant-words object — and carries no curse lexeme anywhere in the verse; אָר֣וּר stands at oshb:Jer.11.3 (byte), outside the span and uncited, the run occurring in 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton) and only there in this chapter. The covenant-words construct chain occurs in 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton), four of them in this chapter at 11:2, 11:3, 11:6 and 11:8, so a byte-true catchword straddles the unit's own front seam while the disclosure sentence names only the two segs — a straddling device argues continuity unless disclosed. The recurrence limb holds too: the onset splice וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.11.6, byte) collates at byte tier at its cited ref, while the same run at oshb:Jer.11.9 reads וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.11.9, byte) in pausal pointing — skeleton-identical, not byte-identical (sweep: 13 verses, skeleton) — and the closing-seam sentence asserts the sameness with neither splice nor tier. The cut itself is untouched: the fresh introduction at 11:9 and the setumah at oshb:Jer.11.8 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3) both stand, so these are citation and disclosure defects, not a boundary defect.
P04-006.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the covenant-curse characterisation of the closing verse with the covenant-words object actually standing in it, spliced from source bytes with its oshb ref and tier; if the curse is to be argued at all, splice it at oshb:Jer.11.3 with its tier and add web:Jer.11.3 to boundary_evidence_refs, since it would then be argued outside the span. boundary_rationale: splice the introduction at oshb:Jer.11.9 with its ref and tier and state the recurrence against oshb:Jer.11.6 as skeleton-identical, not byte-identical. device_notes: disclose the covenant-words construct chain crossing the 11:5|11:6 front seam (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton; four in this chapter) and why it does not defeat the cut — the same straddle faces the seam from both sides, so it is one edit, not two. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: no curse lexeme anywhere in 11:8's bytes; the two introduction forms re-collated separately at byte tier; every recurrence sentence carrying its tier.

P04-007.challenge_claim: The discriminator separating this unit from what precedes — a turn to the present generation's conspiracy rather than the fathers' history just recalled — is contradicted by this unit's own second verse, which names the forefathers twice; and the speech formula at MT 11:11, on which the refusal to cut turns, is left unspliced.
P04-007.grounds: The formula limb is upheld and the contrast limb needs correction. Upheld: the unit's only Hebrew splice sits at its opening, and לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.11.11, byte) — the form on which both the internal-seam refusal and the rejected alternative rest — is quoted nowhere and carries no tier; the prose also calls it a koh-amar clause without naming the therefore-particle prefixing it, so it is not the unbridged verse-initial shape. Corrected: the fathers are not this span's subject. שָׁ֩בוּ֩ עַל עֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתָ֜ם הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.11.10, byte) opens with a finite verb whose subject is the conspiring men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem named at the onset, with the forefathers standing as the owners of the iniquities returned to and as the covenant partners — so the subject contrast the seam rests on survives the bytes and the challenge overstates it. What the bytes do establish is a disclosure debt: the fathers-noun with its suffixes recurs in 4 verses of this chapter (sweep: 44 verses book-wide on the consonantal run, skeleton), at 11:4, 11:5 and 11:7 before the seam and 11:10 inside it, an undisclosed byte-true catchword across the unit's own front seam. Both edges otherwise hold, corroborated by the setumah at oshb:Jer.11.8 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3).
P04-007.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the therefore-prefixed formula from oshb:Jer.11.11 with its ref and tier, naming the particle so the form is not read as an unbridged verse-initial onset; strongest_rejected_alternative, which turns on the same form, inherits that splice. boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: qualify the contrast to the change of grammatical subject at the onset rather than to the disappearance of the fathers. device_notes: disclose the fathers-noun run crossing the front seam (sweep: 44 verses book-wide, skeleton; 11:4, 11:5, 11:7 and 11:10 in this chapter) and why it does not defeat the cut. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: the two forefather tokens inside 11:10 accounted for in the unit's own prose, and every formula the rejected alternative depends on carrying a byte-tier splice at its own oshb ref.

P04-008.challenge_claim: The link holding MT 11:16 and MT 11:17 together is mis-described as a planting in 11:16 although the planting participle occurs at MT 11:17 (skeleton sweep: 1 verse in the book), and the recorded signal labels a prohibition an imperative.
P04-008.grounds: Both limbs verify. The participle הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ stands at oshb:Jer.11.17 (byte) and occurs in exactly one verse in the book (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton), while oshb:Jer.11.16 carries no form of that root at all — its predicate is קָרָ֥א יְהוָ֖ה שְׁמֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.11.16, byte) — so the prose locates an act at a verse whose bytes do not carry it. The binding the argument reaches for is nonetheless real and runs through the second-person feminine chain the unit's own splice already displays: שְׁמֵ֑ךְ at oshb:Jer.11.16 (byte) picked up by הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ and עָלַ֖יִךְ at oshb:Jer.11.17 (byte). The form-class limb holds as well: אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ (oshb:Jer.11.14, byte) is the negative particle with a tav-prefixed prefix-conjugation form (sweep: 3 verses on that run, skeleton), whereas this stem's imperative shape is he-initial and stands in 5 verses elsewhere (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton), at none of them here; both witnesses render a prohibition (web:Jer.11.14), and the unit's own prose says prohibition while its recorded signal says discourse-imperative onset — a form-class label is a byte-checkable claim. Marks and seams are clean: the segs across the span's MT keys at oshb:Jer.11.14 and oshb:Jer.11.17 are both disclosed and correctly typed setumah (WLC, single-witness, tier-3).
P04-008.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the discourse-imperative-onset key with a prohibition/vetitive key agreeing with the form in the bytes and with the unit's own prose. boundary_rationale: re-word the 11:16-11:17 link to the second-person feminine chain the splices already carry, leaving the planting participle at the verse that has it. boundary_rationale, same field, a further defect found here: the opening pairing sets the splice at oshb:Jer.11.14 against a WEB clause (web:Jer.11.14) whose leading connective renders nothing in the spliced run — that verse carries no therefore-particle — and which also runs past the splice to the prepositional object; re-cut gloss extent to splice extent. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: no form of the planting root anywhere in 11:16's bytes; the recorded signal key agreeing with the attested form; each quoted English clause rendering exactly the run spliced beside it.

P04-009.challenge_claim: The statement that nothing before this verse is cast in this voice is refuted by the first-person chain closing MT 11:5 and again by MT 10:19-24, and the exclusivity names no swept object and carries no digit; separately, the closing Yahweh-of-Armies claim rests on MT 11:20, which is left unspliced, so the recorded divine-title signal has no quoted form behind it.
P04-009.grounds: Upheld on the bytes. MT 11:5 closes וָאַ֥עַן וָאֹמַ֖ר אָמֵ֥ן יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.11.5, byte) — the prophet's own first-person report, thirteen verses before the verse said to introduce that voice and inside the same parent — and both witnesses render it as his own speech (web:Jer.11.5). Earlier still, וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי stands at oshb:Jer.10.19 (byte) and first-person petition runs at oshb:Jer.10.23 and oshb:Jer.10.24 (byte). The onset sentence states its exclusivity without qualification, without naming a swept object and without a digit, and an exclusivity of that shape is never dampened by the tier of the splice standing beside it. The second limb holds as well: וַֽיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte) is byte-true but unquoted, leaving the unit's recorded divine-title signal with no quoted form behind it. The onset itself is untouched — 11:18 does open a first-person report after divine speech closes at 11:17, corroborated by the setumah at oshb:Jer.11.17 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3) — so the defect lies in the warrant, not in the boundary.
P04-009.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the unqualified exclusivity, or bind it to a named swept object with a digit and a unit; if a first-occurrence reading is retained, disclose the first-person reply closing 11:5 and the petition voice at 10:19 and 10:23-10:24, and add web:Jer.11.5, web:Jer.10.19 and web:Jer.10.23-Jer.10.24 to boundary_evidence_refs, since they would then be argued outside the span. boundary_rationale or device_notes: splice the divine title from oshb:Jer.11.20 with its ref and tier so the recorded signal has a quoted form. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: 11:5's first-person report and the 10:19 and 10:23-10:24 petition forms all stand in the prophet's own voice, so any surviving first-occurrence sentence must exclude them by a named object; and every recorded signal must be anchored to a byte-tier splice at its own ref.

P04-010.challenge_claim: The English set against the MT 11:22 splice renders a different clause of the verse than the spliced form, and the two therefore-clauses are treated as one object although they are distinct census objects, cited as sweeps of 152 and 50 verses.
P04-010.grounds: The gloss limb is upheld and the count limb needs re-scoping. Upheld: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte) collates at byte tier at its cited ref, but the English paired with it in the same breath renders הַבַּֽחוּרִים֙ יָמֻ֣תוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte), a later clause of the same verse; the clause that actually renders the spliced run is the therefore-Yahweh-of-Armies-says clause the pairing skips (web:Jer.11.22), so gloss extent and splice extent do not match and a byte-verified form is presented as saying something it does not say. Re-scoped: the two digits are not two disjoint objects. The tsevaot-expanded set (sweep: 50 verses, skeleton) is a proper subset of the koh-amar-YHWH set (sweep: 152 verses, skeleton) — 11:22 is counted in both, 11:21 in the larger set only — so the 152 figure is not the count of the without-tsevaot object and cannot be set against the 50 as a separate one. The substantive point survives that correction: the prose calls the second clause a further therefore-thus-says-Yahweh clause carrying the same speaker forward and never names the tsevaot expansion, which is the byte difference between לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte) and the clause at oshb:Jer.11.22, and the unit's recorded signals carry the plain speech formula while that divine-title stack goes unrecorded.
P04-010.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss so the English paired with the oshb:Jer.11.22 splice is the clause that renders it (web:Jer.11.22), or extend the splice to the clause the English renders; in the same field re-cut the oshb:Jer.11.21 pairing as well, whose gloss runs past the splice to the seek-your-life clause — a second extent mismatch found here. boundary_rationale: name the tsevaot expansion as the byte difference between the two therefore-clauses, giving each object its own digit and stating the containment (sweep: 152 verses and 50 verses, skeleton; the second inside the first). observed_substrate_signals: add the divine-title entry for the tsevaot stack standing at 11:22. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: every quoted English clause rendering exactly the run spliced beside it, and any digit named beside a with- or without-tsevaot description stating which set it counts.

P04-011.challenge_claim: Two challenges land here: that the cut before verse 5 separates the complaint from the reply it draws at a join carrying no tier-1 device, with a treachery catchword straddling that seam undisclosed; and that the opening warrant's new-first-person-voice reading is contradicted by dispute, testing and kidneys vocabulary tying 12:1-3 back across the opening seam to 11:20, likewise undisclosed.
P04-011.grounds: Distinct defects at opposite edges of one row; both are real, and one framing needs correction. Opening edge: 11:18-20 is already first-person prophetic speech -- הֽוֹדִיעַ֖נִי וָֽאֵדָ֑עָה at oshb:Jer.11.18 (byte) and גִּלִּ֥יתִי אֶת רִיבִֽי at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte) -- so the first person at 12:1 RESUMES across the intervening koh-amar reply rather than opening a new voice, and the warrant as written is byte-false. The ties verify on their named objects, not merely their digits: אָרִ֖יב at oshb:Jer.12.1 (byte; that form, sweep: 2 verses) answers רִיבִֽי at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte; sweep: 3 verses); the kidneys token stands at בֹּחֵ֥ן כְּלָי֖וֹת וָלֵ֑ב in oshb:Jer.11.20 and at מִכִּלְיוֹתֵיהֶֽם in oshb:Jer.12.2 (both byte; that token, sweep: 4 verses); and וּבָחַנְתָּ֥ לִבִּ֖י at oshb:Jer.12.3 (byte; sweep: 3 verses) answers the testing participle of oshb:Jer.11.20 (sweep: 3 verses). Closing edge: 12:5 opens כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (byte) with no messenger, attribution or word-event formula, and the nearest koh-amar-YHWH sites are 11:22 before and 12:14 after (sweep: 152 verses), none between; כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד closes oshb:Jer.12.1 while בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ stands in oshb:Jer.12.6 (both byte), the family's only two sites in chapters 10-13 (bare consonantal substring, sweep: 12 verses) -- a byte-true catchword crossing this row's own closing seam, undisclosed. Three corrections to the closing-seam framing: an argument resting on the ABSENCE of a paragraph mark at the verse-4/5 join is barred, that layer being tier-3 in the Prophets with absence never counterevidence; the marks do not merely flank the proposed six-verse exchange, since a setumah stands at MT 12:3 inside it (single-witness, tier-3, and the row does disclose it); and כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד is verse-final at 12:1, not the complaint's opening. The cut itself survives on ground the row never argues: 12:1-4 names its addressee, צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte), while 12:5-6 addresses the one whose brothers and father's house are in view -- a byte-visible addressee-referent shift, which is a ruled seam class.
P04-011.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the new-first-person-voice wording with the byte-shown resumption of the first-person voice standing at 11:18-20 across the koh-amar reply of 11:21-23, and ground the cut before verse 5 on the addressee-referent shift read off the pointed bytes (YHWH named as addressee in 12:1-4; the prophet's own brothers and father's house as addressee in 12:5-6) rather than on the absence of a formula. device_notes: disclose BOTH straddling device sets with swept object and verse count -- the dispute, testing and kidneys ties running back to 11:20, and the treachery catchword running forward to 12:6. Delete any sentence resting on a paragraph mark being absent. Boundary PROPOSAL (boss adoption required; not author work): merge 12:1-6 into one petition-and-reply row. Test the cure must pass: the warrant states each half's addressee from the pointed bytes; every device straddling either of the row's own seams is disclosed with object and count; and no evidentiary sentence rests on marker absence.

P04-012.challenge_claim: That the opening cut at verse 5 is the same unmarked join challenged from the complaint's side; and that a treachery catchword crosses that seam undisclosed while both Hebrew splices in the warrant are paired with English running past the spliced extent, the verse's single count-only seg also going undisclosed.
P04-012.grounds: The seam arm is the same defect adjudicated at the complaint's side, not a second finding; the gloss-parity arm is distinct and lands on its own. Parity break one: the splice ends at וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte) while the paired English runs on through the horses clause, which renders תְּתַֽחֲרֶ֖ה אֶת הַסּוּסִ֑ים (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte) outside the splice. Parity break two: the splice אַל תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) is paired with English running on through the beautiful-words clause, which renders כִּֽי יְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ טוֹבֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) outside it. Gloss extent must equal splice extent, and neither pairing meets that. Catchword: בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ in oshb:Jer.12.6 answers the verse-final כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד of oshb:Jer.12.1 (both byte) across this row's opening seam -- the family's only two sites in chapters 10-13 (bare consonantal substring, sweep: 12 verses) -- undisclosed. The count-only seg layer does carry one seg at MT 12:5, but that layer is count-only with no intra-verse position and sits outside the unconditional paragraph-mark symmetry arm, so its omission is a completeness point of low weight and does not lift severity. The high severity attached to the unmarked seam is not sustained: device_notes already concedes that no formula marks the turn, the row holds at reduced confidence with the frontier flag raised -- the sanctioned honest hold -- and the seam survives on the addressee-referent shift visible in the bytes.
P04-012.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut both pairings so each curly-quoted English run renders exactly its adjacent splice -- either extend the splice at oshb:Jer.12.5 through the horses clause and the splice at oshb:Jer.12.6 through the beautiful-words clause, or trim each English run back to the spliced clause; each pairing is one edit. device_notes: disclose the treachery catchword crossing the row's opening seam with its swept object and verse count, and record the single count-only seg at oshb:Jer.12.5 as single-witness with no position claim. Test the cure must pass: every curly-quoted WEB run in the field renders exactly the Hebrew spliced beside it and nothing more, checked against both witnesses' bytes at the same verse; and every byte-true device straddling the row's own seams is disclosed.

P04-013.challenge_claim: That the one-unit warrant's claim that no addressee change and no discourse imperative interrupts 12:7-13 is falsified by the span's own bytes at two verses -- the plural imperatives of 12:9 and the second-person plural suffix at 12:13.
P04-013.grounds: The defect is real; one arm of its framing is not. Byte-true: oshb:Jer.12.9 carries לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ together with הֵתָ֥יוּ (byte; that imperative pair, sweep: 1 verse), so an unqualified denial that any discourse imperative interrupts the span is false at the token level, and the feature goes undisclosed. Byte-true: וּבֹ֨שׁוּ֙ מִתְּבוּאֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם at oshb:Jer.12.13 (byte) carries a second-person masculine plural suffix and turns the speech to the addressed people, a party other than the summoned agents of 12:9 -- likewise undisclosed, and it does contradict the no-addressee-change arm as written. Byte-false: calling 12:13 the span's FIRST direct second-person address does not hold, since the 12:9 imperatives are themselves second-person forms standing four verses earlier; an ordinal of that kind needs its own digit-bearing sweep of the named object and does not survive one. The koh-amar arm holds: nearest sites are 11:22 before and 12:14 after (sweep: 152 verses), none between. The one-unit result also survives: the 12:9 imperatives summon the field's creatures inside the poem's own imagery rather than opening a fresh commission to an audience -- the class this row treats as a seam at 13:15 and 13:18 -- and 12:13 carries no fresh discourse frame. What fails is the unqualified wording and the missing disclosure, not the boundary.
P04-013.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the unqualified three-part denial with a qualified statement naming both in-span features and why neither is a seam of the ruled classes -- the plural imperatives at 12:9 summoning agents inside the poem's imagery, and the second-person plural suffix at 12:13 turning to the addressed people without a fresh discourse frame; keep the koh-amar arm, which the census supports. device_notes: disclose both features with swept object and verse count. Test the cure must pass: no absolute absence claim stands where the span's own bytes carry a token of the named class, and any first/only/sole ordinal carries an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit.

P04-014.challenge_claim: That both frame warrants pair a byte-tier Hebrew splice with English rendering different words of the same verse, so neither the onset formula nor the closure formula is glossed by the text offered as its match; and that the verse's single count-only seg is undisclosed.
P04-014.grounds: Both pairings are broken on the bytes. At 12:14 the other witness renders the formula verse-initially as “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14), while the spliced כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) is paired with the plucking-up clause, which renders הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) -- a different stretch of the same verse. At 12:17 the other witness renders the formula verse-finally as “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17), while the spliced נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.12.17, byte) is paired with the clause preceding it and that English omits the formula's own rendering altogether, inverting the pairing. Gloss extent must equal splice extent; neither pairing meets it. The substantive reading survives: נְאֻם יְהוָֽה is verse-final at oshb:Jer.12.17 (byte), and a fresh private commission opens at oshb:Jer.13.1 with כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (byte; that shape, sweep: 3 verses), so the closure corroboration is correctly placed under the closure-only handling this formula carries at its book-wide density. The count-only seg at MT 12:14 is inventory-true but position-free and outside the unconditional paragraph-mark symmetry arm -- a low-weight completeness point that does not lift severity.
P04-014.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-pair both matches -- pair the koh-amar splice with the WEB rendering “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14) and the neum splice with “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17); if the plucking-up English is retained, splice the clause it renders beside it. device_notes: record the single count-only seg at oshb:Jer.12.14 as single-witness with no position claim. Test the cure must pass: each curly-quoted WEB run renders exactly the Hebrew spliced beside it, verified against both witnesses' bytes at the same verse, with the formula's own rendering never omitted from the pairing that carries it.

P05-001.challenge_claim: That the no-scene-shift clause is contested by an explicit temporal frame and a separate divine-speech onset at 13:6 the enumeration passes over, that the 13:1 formula carries a form label the pointed bytes do not support, and that 13:3's onset is asserted without a pointed splice while 13:8's is spliced.
P05-001.grounds: All three arms hold, at low weight. oshb:Jer.13.6 opens וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים and then carries the separate divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (both byte), commanding a second journey to the river -- an explicit time-and-place transition standing inside the span, so the clause that no addressee or scene shift interrupts the sequence overstates what the bytes carry. The form label fails on the bytes: אָמַ֨ר at oshb:Jer.13.1 (byte) is a suffix-conjugation form, while the narrative wayyiqtol shapes of this span stand at 13:3, 13:6, 13:7 and 13:8 -- so the narrative-preterite label is a form-class claim the pointed text does not carry, and no morphology layer is staged that could rescue it (the challenge's own account of where the wayyiqtol shape stands is narrower than the span's bytes). The commission reading it reaches for is nevertheless corroborated: כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses), distinguishing it from the public-oracle onsets. The splice asymmetry is real: the word-event at 13:8 is spliced at byte tier while the equally load-bearing onset at 13:3 is carried on the other witness's rendering alone. The one-unit result stands unchanged: the addressee never changes across 13:1-11, and the command, performance and interpretation phases of one enacted sign hold together absent an intervening seam of the ruled classes.
P05-001.remedy: boundary_rationale: qualify the scene clause -- name the time-and-place transition at 13:6 and state why it opens no ruled seam (same addressee, same enacted sign, no fresh commission to a new audience); replace the narrative-preterite label with a description the bytes support, namely the koh-amar shape standing in a private commission to the prophet rather than a public oracle onset, with its 3-verse book-wide sweep cited beside it; splice the word-event at oshb:Jer.13.3 at byte tier with its ref and tier named, matching the treatment of 13:8. Test the cure must pass: every form-class label is readable off the pointed bytes cited beside it, and every load-bearing device claim carries its own splice at a named tier.

P05-002.challenge_claim: That the form made to carry the opening seam recurs byte-identically one verse later inside the span, that its imperative label is not what the pointed bytes show, and that the closure warrant places a formula it never splices at a position the bytes contradict.
P05-002.grounds: Two arms hold as stated; one sub-claim needs correction. Recurrence: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם opens oshb:Jer.13.12 and the identical pointed run opens oshb:Jer.13.13 (both byte; that run at byte tier, sweep: 4 verses; the same shape at the consonantal tier, sweep: 18 verses), so the marker carrying the seam is not seam-exclusive and the in-span recurrence is undisclosed. That refines rather than kills the seam: what separates 13:12 from the belt's interpretation is a fresh commissioned saying to a broad audience after that interpretation closes, and the recurrence at 13:13 continues the same commissioned speech rather than opening a second unit. Form label: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם is a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation form, not a morphological imperative -- the imperatives in the neighbourhood are שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ at oshb:Jer.13.15, תְּנוּ֩ at oshb:Jer.13.16 and אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה at oshb:Jer.13.18 (all byte) -- so the label is a byte-checkable claim the text does not carry, though the clause does function as a commissioning frame. Closure position: at oshb:Jer.13.14 the formula נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה stands at the athnach with לֹֽא אֶחְמ֧וֹל and two further negated clauses running to the verse-final מֵהַשְׁחִיתָֽם (byte), so describing it as marking the unit's end misplaces it inside its verse; the closure reading itself survives, a fresh onset following at oshb:Jer.13.15 (sweep: 1 verse). Correction: the paragraph mark is NOT at the internal repetition point -- it is keyed to MT 13:12 while the repetition stands at 13:13; the row's paragraph disclosure for this span is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 13:12 and MT 13:14, single-witness, tier-3), and no variant note falls inside 13:12-13:14. The same misplacement of the closing formula is reproduced in the account that supports this row.
P05-002.remedy: boundary_rationale: describe the opening as a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation commissioning clause rather than an imperative, and disclose that the identical pointed run opens 13:13 inside the span (with its byte-tier verse count), stating why the recurrence continues the commissioned speech instead of opening a second unit; restate the closure as the formula standing inside 13:14 with further clauses following it, corroborated by the fresh imperative onset at 13:15, not as a formula standing at the unit's end, and splice it at byte tier where it is asserted. If the re-description changes the driver, observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence re-open with it. Test the cure must pass: no form-class label stands that the pointed bytes contradict; any marker made to carry a seam is swept for in-span recurrence with the recurrence disclosed; and any position claim about a formula is read off that verse's own pointed bytes.

P05-003.challenge_claim: That a variant note at 13:16 inside the span goes undisclosed even though the disclosure layer is engaged for the paragraph marks, and that a flock lexeme attested in 6 verses book-wide crosses the closing seam undisclosed.
P05-003.grounds: Both hold. oshb:Jer.13.16 stands inside the span and carries one note in the single-witness variant inventory; it is visible in the verse's own bytes as the unpointed ketiv ישית beside its pointed qere וְשִׁ֖ית (byte). The row's disclosure reaches only the paragraph marks at MT 13:14 and MT 13:17, so the disclosure set is incomplete on the book's largest single-witness variant layer at a verse inside the row's own span. Cohesion: עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה closes oshb:Jer.13.17, the row's own last verse, and the same lexeme returns as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (both byte; that consonantal form, sweep: 6 verses) -- a byte-true tie crossing this row's closing seam, undisclosed, arguing continuity against the cut until it is disclosed. The onset is sound and verified: שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.15 and that imperative pair is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse). The third arm is minor but right: declining the lament typing by appeal to which spans are enumerated is not a byte ground; the ground that does hold is וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תִשְׁמָע֔וּהָ at oshb:Jer.13.17 (byte), whose second-person plural verb continues the plural audience addressed from 13:15.
P05-003.remedy: device_notes: add the single variant note at oshb:Jer.13.16 with its type and single-witness disclosure alongside the paragraph marks already carried; add the flock lexeme crossing the row's closing seam from 13:17 to 13:20 with its swept object and verse count, stating why the cut still holds against it. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the refusal of the lament typing on the span's bytes -- the plural address running through 13:17 -- rather than on which spans are enumerated. Test the cure must pass: every variant note falling inside the span appears in the row's disclosure set; every device straddling the row's own seams is disclosed with object and count; and no rejection rests on an enumeration in place of the span's bytes.

P05-004.challenge_claim: Both challenges land on one ground: the rejection of the one-poem rival rests on reading 13:20 as addressed to a second-feminine-singular figure, on one of the twelve doubled-note verses of the variant inventory, with that doubled note undisclosed. One adds that the plural forms opening the verse contradict the reading and that two byte-true ties bracket the two-verse span undisclosed.
P05-004.grounds: The same defect from both lenses, with a distinct second arm added by one of them; the defect is real and the stronger framing overstates it. oshb:Jer.13.20 carries two notes in the single-witness variant inventory -- a doubled-note verse -- and they sit on exactly the forms the rejection reads: the unpointed ketiv שאי and וראי stand in the verse bytes beside the pointed qere שְׂא֤וּ and וּרְא֔וּ (byte), whose plural endings are visible, and their object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (byte) carries a second-person masculine plural suffix under either reading (that imperative-plus-object pair, sweep: 1 verse). The row asserts a second-feminine-singular addressee there and discloses no note, on the largest single-witness variant layer in the book. The characterization is right about the verse's second half -- לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (byte) are feminine singular -- and wrong about its opening, which is where the rejection places the shift. Second arm, byte-true and undisclosed: תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם closes oshb:Jer.13.18 and recurs as תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (that consonantal form, sweep: 4 verses, three of them in this chapter), and עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה at oshb:Jer.13.17 recurs as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (sweep: 6 verses) -- both tie this span to the material past its close and support the rival it sets aside. Framing correction: the seam is not falsified. The opening at oshb:Jer.13.18 is a morphological imperative, אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה (byte), naming a new addressee pair; the addressee does change at 13:20 under either reading of the doubled note; the paragraph disclosure for 13:18-19 is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 13:17 and MT 13:19, single-witness, tier-3) with no variant note inside the span; and the row already holds at reduced confidence with the frontier flag raised and concedes the rival's force. That places this at a ground-rewrite plus a mandatory disclosure, not at a falsified warrant.
P05-004.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the closing seam on what 13:20 actually carries -- plural imperatives with a second-person masculine plural object opening the verse, and the feminine-singular address governing from mid-verse -- instead of an unqualified second-feminine-singular characterization; the corrected ground must hold under BOTH the ketiv and the qere. device_notes: disclose the doubled variant note at oshb:Jer.13.20 with both members named and single-witness disclosure, and disclose the two ties crossing the row's edges -- the glory-crown form recurring from 13:18 at 13:20, and the flock lexeme recurring from 13:17 at 13:20 -- each with swept object and verse count, stating why the cut holds against them. Keep the row's reduced confidence and frontier flag. Test the cure must pass: no form-class ground stands on a verse carrying a variant note unless that note is disclosed and both members are read; and every device straddling the row's edges is disclosed with object and count.

P05-005.challenge_claim: One item: the row's observed_substrate_signals names a koh-amar speech formula that occurs nowhere within Jer.13.20-13.27, the seam and the typing being otherwise byte-sound. The converging item raises the same formula defect and three more: the opening seam's person-shift warrant is not delivered at the opening of 13:20, the woe-lexeme contrast carries a byte-false form label at 22:13 and 23:1, and two byte-true catchwords straddle the row's own opening seam undisclosed.
P05-005.grounds: The formula arm is the SAME defect in both items; the other three are distinct and additional. Formula (upheld): the census object koh amar YHWH returns 152 verses (sweep: 152 verses; with the single adonai-YHWH stack at 7:20 the census is 153), and its chapter-13 sites are 13:1, 13:9, 13:12 and 13:13 (sweep: 4 verses in the chapter), all standing before the span, the next site at 14:10 — none falls inside 13:20-13:27, so the declared signal has no support in the span's own bytes. The span's actual divine formula is נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.25, byte tier). Person shift (upheld): 13:20 opens שאי שְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ וראי וּרְא֔וּ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier for the pointed members; the two ketiv members stand unpointed in the source), a doubled-note verse in the single-witness inventory whose two notes sit on the two opening imperatives — feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere — with the intervening object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) carrying a masculine-plural suffix under either reading. The feminine-singular forms לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) stand in the verse's second half, so the shift is not what 13:20 opens with. The run the row actually splices, הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), is a definite masculine-plural participle with a prepositional phrase and carries no addressee marking at all, while the English paired with it, “Lift up your eyes, and see those who come from the north” (web:Jer.13.20), renders the contested imperatives that lie OUTSIDE the splice: gloss extent exceeds splice extent at exactly the point the warrant turns on. Recording the note as consulted but not spliced is a mark disclosure, not an answer to the reading it complicates. Form label (upheld): 22:13 and 23:1 each open on bare ה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.13 and oshb:Jer.23.1, byte tier) as the verse's first token; the vav-prefixed shape וְה֥וֹי (oshb:Jer.34.5, byte tier) stands at two verses (sweep: 2 verses — 22:18 and 34:5), both funeral cries, so calling the 22:13 and 23:1 onsets vav-prefixed is contradicted by their own bytes. The oy digit is right: that lexeme is token-bound at 8 verses (sweep: 8 verses — 4:13, 6:4, 10:19, 13:27, 18:17, 30:14, 31:16, 48:46), against 14 for a bare consonantal substring (sweep: 14 verses). Cohesion (upheld): תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier) closes 13:18 and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) closes 13:20, that stem standing at 4 verses (sweep: 4 verses — 13:11, 13:18, 13:20, 33:9); עֵ֥דֶר (oshb:Jer.13.17, byte tier) closes 13:17 and הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) stands inside 13:20, that noun at 6 verses (sweep: 6 verses — 6:3, 13:17, 13:20, 31:10, 31:24, 51:23). Both straddle the row's own opening seam, and conceding shared imagery in the rejected alternative is not disclosure of a byte-true device. The seam itself survives — the feminine-singular Jerusalem address does govern 13:20b through the explicit vocative at 13:27 — but the stated ground, the sole cited splice, one of the two declared signals and a named form class are all byte-defective. Parashah disclosure is accurate as written (setumah at 13:19 ahead of the opening, petuchah at 13:27 at the close; single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), and the span carries no paseq seg.
P05-005.remedy: No respan; the cut at 13:20 stands. (1) boundary_rationale: restate the opening ground where the bytes put it — 13:20 opens with the doubled-note imperative pair (feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere) and a masculine-plural object, and the feminine-singular address begins mid-verse at the 'to you' and 'your glory' forms and then governs through the vocative at 13:27; say that the note falls on the very forms the person reading turns on, rather than logging it as consulted-but-not-spliced. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the splice so the spliced extent covers exactly what the paired English renders, then re-collate at byte tier. (3) boundary_rationale: strike 'vav-prefixed' from the woe contrast — 22:13 and 23:1 open on bare hoy as their first token, and the vav-prefixed shape stands at 22:18 and 34:5 (sweep: 2 verses), both funeral cries. (4) observed_substrate_signals: remove speech_formula.koh_amar (no koh-amar verse falls in 13:20-13:27; the chapter's four sites are 13:1, 13:9, 13:12, 13:13); if a divine-formula signal is wanted the span's token is the neum-YHWH at 13:25. (5) device_notes or strongest_rejected_alternative: disclose and answer the two straddling catchwords with their swept objects and digits (the glory stem, sweep: 4 verses; the flock noun, sweep: 6 verses). (6) The signal field is dependent on the driver, so striking one entry re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence.
