P05-006.challenge_claim: The topical-header claim is byte-sound, but a ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed while the row makes a positive absence statement for the parashah layer; secondarily, the appeal to how header-bounded units elsewhere carry their attached content as one piece is uneven across the four attested sites.
P05-006.grounds: Upheld on the bytes, with one finding added. Disclosure: 14:3, inside the span, carries one note in the single-witness inventory and it stands in the verse as unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere, צעוריהם צְעִירֵיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.14.3, byte tier for the pointed member). The row's device_notes state positively that no verse within 14:1-14:6 carries a parashah mark — true on the inventory, as is the petuchah at 13:27 ahead of the row — so one single-witness layer is engaged with a positive absence claim while a present item in the other, the largest such inventory in this book (141 notes over 124 verses), goes unmentioned; that asymmetry is what the span-relevant disclosure rule exists to catch. The header object and digit are sound and are NOT disturbed: the shape carrying the prophet's name returns 14:1, 46:1, 47:1 and 49:34 (sweep: 4 verses), and dropping the name widens the result to five by admitting the to-him variant in the superscription at 1:2 (sweep: 5 verses), so the needle is correctly bounded and not blended with the eleven-verse prose-sermon shape. Secondary arm upheld: 46:1 reads “Yahweh’s word which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.” (web:Jer.46.1) and heads the whole nations collection rather than bundling an attached description, while 47:1 and 49:34 head single-nation oracles each with its own attached setting — the cross-site analogy needs a per-site read. NEW FINDING, raised by neither item: gloss extent and splice extent come apart in the same sentence. The splice ends at דִּבְרֵ֖י (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) while the English paired with it, “This is Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought” (web:Jer.14.1), renders הַבַּצָּרֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) as well — one token past the spliced extent. The span carries no paseq seg, so nothing is owed there.
P05-006.remedy: No respan; the header seam and the 4-verse digit stand. (1) device_notes: add the ketiv/qere note at 14:3 (single-witness), stated as its own layer and kept distinct from the parashah sentence, which is accurate and stays as written. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the header splice so it ends where the paired English ends — extend the splice through the drought noun or trim the English to stop before it — then re-collate at byte tier. (3) boundary_rationale: replace the blanket cross-site analogy with a per-site statement (46:1 heads the nations collection rather than bundling a description; 47:1 and 49:34 head single-nation oracles with their own attached settings), or drop the analogy and rest the bundling on the span's own absence of an addressee or scene shift through 14:6. TEST the cure must pass: span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry clean across BOTH single-witness layers for every verse of 14:1-14:6; the re-cut splice re-collates at byte tier with gloss extent equal to splice extent; every cross-site claim names its own site.

P05-008.challenge_claim: The one-verse boundary is defensible, but the frame-owner ground given for it is contradicted by the run the row itself splices, and the verse's third-person handling of the divine name means describing it as the deity answering the plea over-specifies the mouth.
P05-008.grounds: The first arm is upheld on the bytes; the second is real as an observation but wrongly framed as a defect. Upheld: the row's stated ground is that the pronouncement is spoken about the people rather than to them, but the continuation inside its own splice, לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), is a lamed phrase marking the people as the party addressed, and the row's own paired English reads “Yahweh says to this people” (web:Jer.14.10). The third-person forms the row leans on — אָֽהֲבוּ֙, רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם, עֲוֺנָ֔ם, חַטֹּאתָֽם (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier) — mark the oracle's SUBJECT, not its addressee, so the single sentence carrying the boundary conflates subject person with addressee. Corrected: the second arm's byte facts hold — 14:10 carries no first-person clause (its finite verbs are third person) and refers to the divine name in the third person inside the quotation, וַיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א רָצָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), while the first first-person divine clauses in this stretch stand at 14:12, אֵינֶ֤נִּי שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ and אָנֹכִ֖י מְכַלֶּ֥ה (oshb:Jer.14.12, byte tier) — but they do not make the mouth over-specified. The verse opens on the messenger formula naming the speaker, which is exactly what frame-ownership discipline requires, and third-person self-reference inside a messenger-formula oracle is an ordinary shape, not a misattributed mouth. The defect is therefore one sentence's category conflation, not a frame-owner error. The boundary is not disturbed, and the span's disclosure is in fact complete: setumah at 14:9 ahead of the row and setumah at 14:10 itself (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), with no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg on 14:10.
P05-008.remedy: No respan; the one-verse unit stands. (1) boundary_rationale: rewrite the footing sentence so addressee and subject are not conflated — 14:10 is addressed TO the people (the lamed phrase inside the row's own splice, matched by the paired English) and speaks ABOUT them in the third person; the seam's real footing change is that 14:7-9 addresses the deity, 14:10 addresses the people, and 14:11 turns to private address to the prophet. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: apply the same correction to 'the addressee shifts from Yahweh-as-hearer to the people-as-subject', which mixes the two categories in one clause; state addressee-to-addressee. (3) device_notes, optional: note that the oracle body refers to the divine name in the third person and carries no first-person clause, the first such clause standing at 14:12. TEST the cure must pass: no sentence in any field assigns one clause both roles, and every addressee claim is carried by a form inside the cited splice, with no token in that same splice contradicting it.

P05-009.challenge_claim: The formula the row cuts on recurs verse-initially at 14:14 inside its own span, undisclosed, and the reason given for keeping that turn internal is contradicted by the bytes of 14:13-14:14; on those bytes either 14:14 is a seam or the criterion applied at 15:1 does not hold.
P05-009.grounds: Two arms upheld, the third corrected, and one further defect the item itself misses. Upheld: the opening shape וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.14.11, byte tier) stands verse-initially again at 14:14, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Jer.14.14, byte tier), inside the row's own span, and again at 15:1, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.15.1, byte tier), the three differing only in accents; the shape returns 13 verses (sweep: 13 verses — 1:7, 1:9, 1:12, 1:14, 3:6, 3:11, 11:6, 11:9, 13:6, 14:11, 14:14, 15:1, 24:3). The row names 14:14 only as a doubled-note site and never as a recurrence of the device carrying its own boundary. Upheld: the rejected alternative's blanket sentence, that neither internal turn carries an addressee or scene change of its own, is byte-false for 14:14 — 14:13 is the prophet addressing the deity, וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.13, byte tier), and 14:14 is the deity answering him, so the addressee does alternate across that turn. Corrected: the dichotomy does not follow. The seam at 14:22 into 15:1 is not carried by the formula shape alone — the material closing at 14:22 is a first-common-plural communal plea addressed to the deity, a different speaker role and a different unit type from a private prophet-and-deity dialogue, and it closes on a petuchah (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, corroboration only) — whereas across 14:13 into 14:14 the same two participants continue one sustained private exchange, which under the ruled granularity is a speaker turn and not a tier-1 internal seam. The criterion therefore survives; what fails is the row's blanket sentence and its silence about the recurrence. NEW FINDING: the item's own statement that disclosure is otherwise complete here is byte-false. Two paseq segs fall inside the span, at 14:13 and at 14:16 (single-witness, count-only — no intra-verse position is sourceable from that layer), and neither is disclosed. What the row does carry is accurate: setumah at 14:12, 14:13 and 14:14 within the span, setumah at 14:10 ahead of it, and the doubled note at 14:14.
P05-009.remedy: No respan; 14:14 need not become a seam. (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'neither carries an addressee or scene change of its own' with the byte-true statement — 14:13 is the prophet addressing the deity and 14:14 the deity answering him, so the addressee does alternate — and give the ground that actually holds the exchange together: both turns stay inside one sustained private exchange between the same two participants, whereas the seam four verses on additionally carries a speaker-role change from a communal first-common-plural plea, a different unit type, and a petuchah at 14:22 (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only). (2) boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose that the opening formula shape recurs verse-initially at 14:14 inside the span (sweep: 13 verses book-wide) and say why the recurrence is not cut, since the same shape carries the onset at 15:1. (3) device_notes: add the two paseq segs at 14:13 and 14:16 (single-witness, count-only; assert no intra-verse position) beside the parashah and ketiv/qere disclosures already carried. (4) confidence and frontier_flag_considered: re-open both once the rejected-alternative ground is restated, since the discarded rival is stronger than the present sentence concedes. TEST the cure must pass: no sentence denies a feature the span's own bytes carry; every span-relevant single-witness layer is disclosed for every verse of the span; a device that carries the row's own boundary and recurs inside the span is named with its digit and answered.

P05-010.challenge_claim: The seam driver is a form-class misidentification — the opening word of 14:17 is a waw-consecutive perfect, not an imperative — and the same construction runs mid-verse at 15:2 with no boundary force.
P05-010.grounds: Upheld on the pointed bytes, and it bites harder than the item frames it. Form class: 14:17 opens וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier) — vav with sheva, alef with qamats, mem with patah, resh with sheva, and a final tav carrying dagesh and qamats, the second-masculine-singular suffix-conjugation ending. The form is waw plus perfect, not a morphological imperative. The second-masculine-singular imperative of this verb stands three verses earlier at 13:18, אֱמֹ֥ר (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), with no such ending, and the discourse-frame imperative class that may drive a seam is instanced by true plural imperatives at 4:5 and 10:1. No morphology layer is staged, so this is argued from the pointing plus both witnesses' renderings, which read a modal continuation rather than a command. The weight: the row asserts the class in boundary_rationale AND carries speech_formula.discourse_imperative as its single declared substrate signal, so the mislabel leaves the row with no sound declared driver, and that field is dependent on the driver. Not seam-exclusive: the construction וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier) returns 18 verses (sweep: 18 verses — 5:19, 7:28, 8:4, 11:3, 13:12, 13:13, 14:17, 15:2, 16:11, 17:20, 19:11, 23:33, 25:27, 25:28, 25:30, 26:4, 38:26, 43:10) and the bare form 30 verses (sweep: 30 verses); at 15:2 it sits mid-verse inside a conditional as an ordinary continuation, וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), four verses on in the same stretch. What does NOT follow is a respan: reading 14:17 as mere continuation of the divine speech begun at 14:14 is a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, and the cut is re-groundable without one — 14:14-16 is divine speech to the prophet ABOUT the prophets and the people, while 14:17 commissions a word for delivery TO them, and both witnesses open a fresh quoted message there. The item is also right that 14:16, just ahead of the opening, carries no parashah mark, so no tier-3 corroboration is available at this seam. NEW FINDING: the same construction stands verse-initially at 13:12 and again at 13:13, adjacent verses in the same stretch and both inside the 18-verse set, so the mislabel class reaches past this row.
P05-010.remedy: No respan. (1) observed_substrate_signals: replace speech_formula.discourse_imperative — the form is a waw-prefixed second-masculine-singular suffix conjugation, not an imperative — with a dotted key matching what the bytes carry (a speech-delivery command opening a fresh quoted message, or the change in who the message is addressed to across 14:16 into 14:17). (2) boundary_rationale: strike 'A fresh discourse-frame imperative opens the row'; state the form as the pointed bytes carry it and re-ground the seam on the delivery command plus the addressee change, and disclose that the same construction recurs mid-verse at 15:2 with no boundary force and is attested at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), so it is not seam-exclusive. (3) Dependent fields: this is the row's single declared signal, so its replacement re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence. (4) device_notes: state plainly that 14:16 carries no parashah mark, so this seam has no tier-3 corroboration, rather than leaving it implied. (5) CORPUS-WIDE ORDER, carried as its own sweep and not folded into this row's fix: sweep all 18 sites of the delivery construction (5:19, 7:28, 8:4, 11:3, 13:12, 13:13, 14:17, 15:2, 16:11, 17:20, 19:11, 23:33, 25:27, 25:28, 25:30, 26:4, 38:26, 43:10) plus the 30-verse bare set, and correct every row that labels this waw-perfect an imperative or a discourse-frame imperative, or that rests a seam on its supposed exclusivity — the verse-initial occurrences at 13:12 and 13:13 are the nearest instances. TEST the cure must pass: every form-class label re-read off the pointed bytes at its own site, with the imperative at 13:18 as the contrasting control; no seam-exclusivity claim for a construction whose sweep digit and site list are not stated beside it.

P05-012.challenge_claim: A ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed in the very clause the row cites, and the span description merges two fourfold lists that the bytes keep apart.
P05-012.grounds: Both arms upheld on the bytes, with one framing detail corrected. Disclosure: 15:4, inside the span, carries one note in the single-witness inventory standing in the verse as unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere, לזועה לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.4, byte tier for the pointed member), and it is nowhere disclosed, while the row's device_notes state positively that nothing within 15:1-15:4 carries a parashah mark — true on the inventory, as is the petuchah at 14:22 ahead of the row. Detail corrected: the note does not sit in the clause the row names. The closing sentence cites 15:4 by its Manasseh clause, and the variant stands in the verse's first clause; what carries the obligation is that the verse lies inside the span and is cited at all, not which clause was named. Count objects: the fourfold assignment lies wholly inside 15:2 — אֲשֶׁ֨ר לַמָּ֤וֶת לַמָּ֨וֶת֙ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לַחֶ֨רֶב֙ לַחֶ֔רֶב וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לָֽרָעָב֙ לָֽרָעָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לַשְּׁבִ֖י לַשֶּֽׁבִי (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier) — four pairs in one verse. 15:3 carries a DIFFERENT and separately numbered quartet, אַרְבַּ֤ע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת֙ (oshb:Jer.15.3, byte tier), whose members are sword, dogs, birds and beasts, and the numeral stands there and not in 15:2; so attributing one fourfold assignment of death, sword, famine and captivity to 15:2-15:3 blends two count objects and attaches the numeral's home verse to the wrong list. The row's uncontested calls check out: 15:3 carries the postpositive נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.3, byte tier), and the koh-amar inside 15:2 — itself a census site — is embedded in speech the prophet is told to relay rather than a fresh divine onset, so declining to cut there is right. The span carries no paseq seg. The delivery construction recurring mid-verse at 15:2, which the item leaves unremarked, is the same defect class ruled at 14:17 and is carried there as a corpus-wide sweep rather than duplicated here.
P05-012.remedy: No respan; the 15:1 onset and the uncut koh-amar at 15:2 stand. (1) device_notes: add the ketiv/qere note at 15:4 (single-witness), stated as its own layer and kept distinct from the parashah sentence, which is accurate and stays. (2) boundary_rationale: split the conflated citation — the fourfold death, sword, famine and captivity assignment lies wholly in 15:2, while 15:3 carries a separately numbered quartet of four kinds (sword, dogs, birds, beasts) and is where the numeral stands; name each list with its own verse and its own count object, and carry no digit across both. TEST the cure must pass: span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry clean across parashah AND ketiv/qere for every verse of 15:1-15:4; every enumerated list in prose names its own verse and its own swept object, with no numeral attached to a list it does not stand in.

P05-013.challenge_claim: The row slices at a verse carrying an undisclosed ketiv/qere note, and it calls the cited neighbour verse unmarked while that verse carries one too.
P05-013.grounds: Both arms verify from the bytes. The staged variant inventory records exactly one note inside Jer.15.5-Jer.15.9, at MT 15:9 -- the row's own terminal verse and the verse its closing argument rests on -- and the doubled reading stands in the bytes as the unpointed ketiv beside the pointed qere, באה בָּ֥א (oshb:Jer.15.9, byte tier); MT 15:5-15:8 carry none (sweep: 0 notes across those four verses), so the omission is the whole in-span obligation. The neighbour arm holds too: MT 15:4 carries no parashah mark but does carry one variant note, לזועה לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.4, byte tier), so calling that verse unmarked is true of the parashah layer alone and false of the mark inventory read whole. Parashah handling is otherwise complete and correctly typed (1 marked verse in MT 15:5-15:9, the setumah at MT 15:9; tier-3 weak corroboration in the Prophets, single-witness). No splice runs through either doubled reading and the seam is untouched, so this is a disclosure defect, not a boundary defect. The two arms are unequal -- the neighbour sentence is a precision failure inside a parashah statement, while the in-span note is an outright omission in a verse the row both cuts at and argues from -- and the stated severity survives that split.
P05-013.remedy: device_notes: add the single-witness ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 15:9, naming the doubled reading, and re-word the Jer.15.4 sentence so it names the layer it speaks for (no parashah mark at MT 15:4) plus that verse's one variant note. Leave span, unit_type, confidence and observed_substrate_signals untouched. Cure test (the test that killed the original): every ketiv/qere verse inside Jer.15.5-Jer.15.9 must be named in device_notes under the single-witness label, and no verse may be called unmarked without naming the layer that word covers.

P05-014.challenge_claim: The stated ground for declining a cut at 15:19 is byte-false: the divine reply is not already underway there, because 15:15-18 is the prophet's own voice, so the verse-initial koh-amar does carry a change of speaking mouth; two ketiv/qere notes inside the span are also undisclosed.
P05-014.grounds: The premise fails on the span's own bytes. The reply opening at MT 15:11 runs to MT 15:14; MT 15:15 turns to the prophet addressing the deity, אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier) -- a vocative divine name standing between a second-person-singular verb and two imperatives carrying first-person-singular object suffixes -- and the first-person complaint holds through MT 15:16-15:18, both witnesses rendering those four verses in the prophet's mouth. So the formula at לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) resumes divine speech after four verses in the other mouth: the mouth carrying the formula does change there, and the row's reason for declining the cut -- that it brings no change of frame-owner from a reply already underway -- is contradicted by the bytes it cites. Under the ruled granularity a koh-amar onset WITH a frame-owner change is a licensed internal seam, so what the row sets aside as a non-event is a live seam candidate. The mark arm verifies as well: two variant notes fall inside Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21, at MT 15:11 -- שרותך שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), the verse cited as the reply's onset -- and at MT 15:16, inside the complaint; neither is disclosed. Independently re-verified and NOT defective: the row's 8-verse digit for the alef-initial outcry lexeme matches the byte-derived count object exactly (8 verses, MT keys), while a bare consonantal substring sweep on the same three letters returns 14 verses, contaminated by the enemy and fool bases -- the digit is true only under the token-bound object the row names, and it names it. Parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 15:10, 15:14, 15:16, 15:17, 15:18; petuchah at MT 15:21; the two types never conflated). High stands: the defect sits in the clause that carries the row's whole hold-together argument.
P05-014.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative and the matching boundary_rationale clause: rewrite on a true premise -- the divine reply does not run unbroken from 15:11; it breaks at 15:15 where the prophet's voice resumes, and the formula at 15:19 opens a second divine reply with a changed speaking mouth. Any ground for holding Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21 whole must then be argued from the complaint-and-reply exchange as one scene under the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule, not from a continuous reply. device_notes: add the single-witness ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 15:11 and MT 15:16. Splitting at 15:19 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit owner adoption -- never author work. Cure test: a per-verse mouth check across Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21 must sustain every voice statement the prose makes, and every in-span variant verse must be named.

P06-001.challenge_claim: Two stated grounds are byte-contested -- the koh-amar at 16:5 heads the mourning prohibition itself rather than a rationale at 16:6-7, and the span is not addressed to one hearer named in it -- and the parashah-position statement is wrong for the mark at MT 16:4.
P06-001.grounds: Two arms verify, one is over-read. Formula location: MT 16:5 puts formula and prohibition in a single verse, כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל תָּבוֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית מַרְזֵ֔חַ (oshb:Jer.16.5, byte tier), and MT 16:6-16:7 carry no speech formula at all (sweep: 0 koh-amar verses in MT 16:6-16:7), so pairing the mourning command with a koh-amar rationale at 16:6-7 mislocates the formula; the parallel pairing for the marriage command is right, its formula standing at MT 16:3 with the rationale running to MT 16:4. Mark position: the mark keyed to MT 16:4 stands after that verse, between the marriage command-and-rationale block of 16:2-16:4 and the mourning command at 16:5 -- that is, between two prohibitions -- while only the mark keyed to MT 16:8 falls between a command and its own rationale at 16:9; the row's both is right for one of the two. CORRECTED FINDING on the addressee arm: the name half is true, the prophet's name standing in no verse of chapters 15, 16 or 17 under either attested spelling (token-bound sweeps, MT keys: 109 verses book-wide for the long spelling, 117 verses for any variant, 0 in each of those three chapters), so named is the wrong word; but the conclusion that the one-hearer ground fails outright is over-read. The frame addressee does not change anywhere in the span -- MT 16:2, MT 16:5 and MT 16:8 all carry second-person-singular prohibitions to the one who receives the word at MT 16:1 -- and the plural of MT 16:9, לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם וּבִֽימֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier), stands inside the quoted oracle content, addressing the people the oracle is about rather than the hearer the commands are given to. The no-scene-change ground therefore survives; only its wording fails. No variant note falls in Jer.16.1-Jer.16.9 (sweep: 0 notes), so nothing is owed on that arm, and the disclosure of the petuchah at MT 15:21 ahead of the opening is correct.
P06-001.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the formula sentence so the mourning command's koh-amar is located at 16:5 with the command and 16:6-7 named as its rationale carrying no formula; replace the clause 'Jeremiah is the one hearer named across the span' with a frame-level statement (the second-person-singular addressee of the commands at 16:2, 16:5 and 16:8 does not change), and keep the second-person-plural of 16:9 disclosed as oracle-internal address rather than a frame addressee. device_notes: replace 'Both interior breaks fall inside a prohibition rather than between two of them' with the per-mark reading -- the mark at MT 16:4 stands between two prohibitions, the mark at MT 16:8 between a command and its rationale. No span change; the seam ground survives, so confidence need not move. P07-002.challenge_claim: The unit's statement that 19:15 restates the coming ruin rather than repeating the jar-oracle's own wording is byte-false; the cohesion binding 19:15 back across the unit's own opening seam goes undisclosed; and the setumah cited at 19:14 is a break dividing the span's two verses.
P07-002.grounds: Two arms hold; the first is overstated and carries a tier error of its own. The divine-title stack does stand at both ends of the ch-19 complex, יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.19.3, byte tier) and יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.19.15, byte tier), but the two runs are not byte-identical: the 19:3 run collates against 19:15 at accent_stripped tier only, three of its four words differing in cantillation. Tier-1 (divine-title formula), recurrence at accent_stripped tier. The construction arm does not reach 19:15 either: a contiguous consonantal sweep of the hinneni-plus-participle run returns 7 verses (sweep: 7 verses: 5:15, 11:11, 19:3, 31:8, 35:17, 45:5, 49:5) and excludes 19:15, because the ketiv/qere pair מבי מֵבִ֜יא (oshb:Jer.19.15, byte tier) stands there, its unpointed ketiv breaking the run between the two words. And 19:15's own clause כָּל הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עָלֶ֑יהָ (oshb:Jer.19.15, byte tier) is a back-reference in summary form, so the unit's sentence is an overstatement rather than a falsehood. What is upheld, and is the load-bearing finding, is the cohesion arm: the stack the unit files as its own opening evidence stands twelve verses earlier inside the unit this row is cut away from, so a byte-true device straddles this row's own seam at 19:13|19:14 undisclosed, arguing continuity against the cut until it is disclosed. The parashah arm is upheld as stated: the inventory records SAMEKH at Jer.19.14, a break after that verse, which divides this two-verse span between its two verses, while the field states it as a mark carried by the row's own opening verse with that internal force unstated - and four sibling spans in the same part use the within-the-span wording for the same configuration (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver). New finding: the inventory records a ketiv/qere at Jer.19.15 (1 note) sitting on the participle inside the very construction the non-repetition sentence turns on; neither the Hebrew nor the English quote reaches it, so the declared queue arms are confirmed false positives on quote-binding, but the verse's content is argued in prose and the variant is disclosed nowhere in the row.
P07-002.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the clause asserting that 19:15 restates the ruin rather than repeating the jar-oracle's own wording with a sentence that discloses the recurrence - the same divine-title stack opens the valley proclamation at 19:3 and the temple-court proclamation at 19:15 (recurrence at accent_stripped tier, tier named in-field), and 19:15 refers back to the evil already pronounced. device_notes: (a) state that the SAMEKH recorded at Jer.19.14 falls after that verse and therefore divides this two-verse span, using the same within-the-span wording the sibling spans use; (b) disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.19.15 (single-witness). P07-003.challenge_claim: The rejected alternative tests a weaker internal rival than the unit's own disclosed evidence supports, and the byte-true renaming catchword straddling the closing seam at 20:6|20:7 goes undisclosed.
P07-003.grounds: The first arm is upheld cleanly. The alternative weighed is the day-change split at 20:2|20:3, but the disclosed petuchah falls after 20:3 and 20:4 opens verse-initially on כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה (oshb:Jer.20.4, byte tier), a ki-subordinated messenger-formula restart. A tier-1 speech-formula restart and the tier-3 substrate break (single-witness, never a driver) coincide at 20:3|20:4, a juncture the field leaves untested, while the rival it does test carries neither signal. The ki subordinates the oracle to the renaming that grounds it, so the span itself is not in doubt; the defect is in the field's choice of rival. The second arm holds substantively but is mislabeled twice. The renaming run מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב (oshb:Jer.20.3, byte tier) and the taunt מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒ (oshb:Jer.20.10, byte tier) are not byte-identical: they collate at skeleton tier, the accents differing at both words. The two-word phrase is a 5-verse object at consonantal tier (sweep: 5 verses: 6:25, 20:3, 20:10, 46:5, 49:29), two of whose members sit either side of the seam this row closes at, so the cross-seam cohesion finding stands - at skeleton tier, not byte. And לְמָג֜וֹר (oshb:Jer.20.4, byte tier) is a bare prefixed noun, not a member of the two-word phrase object; counting it as a third member of that object blends two count objects in one digit.
P07-003.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the day-change rival with the 20:3|20:4 rival and state the ground for declining it - the ki subordinates the oracle to the renaming it grounds. device_notes: disclose that the renaming phrase at Jer.20.3 recurs at Jer.20.10, outside this span and across its closing seam, naming the tier (skeleton) and naming the object as the two-word phrase (sweep: 5 verses); keep the bare prefixed noun at Jer.20.4 as its own separate object if it is cited at all. Test the cure must pass: the rewritten alternative must name a rival that carries a disclosed substrate break or a tier-1 device at the juncture it tests, and no recurrence sentence may say byte-identical for a pair that collates at skeleton.

P07-004.challenge_claim: The stated ground for declining the split at 20:13|20:14 is contradicted by the bytes of 20:13; the confession-cycle digit is put in sweep shorthand for a set no sweep produces; and the taunt at 20:10 straddles the row's opening seam undisclosed.
P07-004.grounds: The first arm is real but positionally loose. The imperative pair שִׁ֚ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֔ה הַֽלְל֖וּ אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.20.13, byte tier) stands at 20:13's own opening, so it marks 20:12|20:13, not the declined pivot at 20:13|20:14. What does stand at the declined pivot is an addressee change - 20:12 addresses the deity directly, 20:13 addresses a plural audience with the divine name as the object of its verbs, and 20:14 is an addressee-less curse - together with the SAMEKH the unit itself discloses at Jer.20.13, a break after that verse falling precisely at the pivot the field declines and left unweighed in that field (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver). So the ground as written overstates the pivot's unmarkedness, though not for the reason given. The frontier flag and the held-open statement mitigate the boundary risk but do not repair the ground. The type point is upheld: 20:13 is a hymnic call to praise folded into a span typed as a confession, with no operative-category deviation note, which the closed vocabulary requires wherever a span's bytes deviate from its declared type. The second arm is upheld: the five-span citation puts an editorially enumerated set into the one sanctioned citation shorthand. Sweeps over this corpus return verse or token counts of a named object; confession delimitation is not a byte-swept object and no such object exists in the staged device inventory. The enumeration is standard, its provenance misstated. The third arm is upheld substantively with the same tier correction as the neighbouring span: מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒ (oshb:Jer.20.10, byte tier) and the renaming at 20:3 collate at skeleton, not byte, and the phrase is a 5-verse object (sweep: 5 verses: 6:25, 20:3, 20:10, 46:5, 49:29) straddling this row's opening seam at 20:6|20:7 undisclosed.
P07-004.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the ground so it survives the pivot's own bytes - name the addressee change across 20:12-20:14 and the disclosed break after Jer.20.13, then give the reason the pivot is still declined (no tier-1 onset opens 20:14: no messenger formula with a frame-owner change, no discourse-frame imperative, no scene or date frame) and keep the internal edge held open. boundary_rationale: remove the sweep shorthand from the confession-cycle enumeration - state the enumeration plainly with no sweep citation, or replace it with a digit-bearing sweep over a named byte object with its unit named. device_notes: add the one-sentence operative-category deviation note for the hymnic call at Jer.20.13 inside a confession-typed span, and disclose the renaming phrase recurring at Jer.20.3 across this row's opening seam (sweep: 5 verses; skeleton tier). P07-005.challenge_claim: 21:1 is called a dated header although its temporal element is an occasion clause and the site stands outside the classified date census, and the addressee assigned to the 21:4-21:7 answer is not the one the bytes name.
P07-005.grounds: Both arms verified on bytes. The header at 21:1 is a genuine member of the eleven-verse prose-sermon superscription shape, so the parent flip at this verse is tier-1 warranted and the row does not straddle it. But its temporal element is בִּשְׁלֹ֨חַ אֵלָ֜יו הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.21.1, byte tier), a bet-prefixed infinitive construct naming an occasion: no year word, and not the bet-plus-cardinal shape. The classified date census carries 19 candidate sites (sweep: 19 sites) and 21:1 is not among them; the row's own filed signal list carries no date key, and the rendered header carries no date either. A dated royal embassy therefore overshoots the bytes, the census, and the row's own signals. On the addressee: 21:3 reads כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְרֻ֖ן אֶל צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.21.3, byte tier), naming Zedekiah as the one to be told, and the oracle body then speaks in the plural to those holding the weapons, אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיֶדְכֶם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֜ם נִלְחָמִ֣ים בָּ֗ם (oshb:Jer.21.4, byte tier). The named messengers are couriers, not the addressee, so the rejected alternative's warrant - that 21:8 shifts the address from the king's own messengers to the people at large - mis-names its point of departure. The seam at 21:7|21:8 survives on the byte-true fresh commission at 21:8; only the stated warrant fails. The identical mis-naming stands as the seam warrant of the adjacent span at 21:8-21:10, so this is one wording defect across two units, not two independent ones.
P07-005.remedy: boundary_rationale: drop the dated characterisation of the 21:1 header and describe the temporal element as an occasion clause (the king's sending), unless a year element is shown in the verse's own bytes - there is none; do not add a date_frame key to observed_substrate_signals. strongest_rejected_alternative: correct the point of departure - the address at 21:3-21:7 is to Zedekiah and, in the plural, to the city's defenders, and 21:8 turns it to the people at large. Apply the identical correction to the same warrant sentence in the adjacent span at 21:8-21:10 as one edit, not two. Test the cure must pass: no field may assign a date classification to a site absent from the 19-site census (sweep: 19 sites) or lacking a year element in its own bytes, and the corrected addressee sentence must name the party the relay clause at 21:3 names.

P07-006.challenge_claim: The addressee the seam warrant turns on is mis-named, the English gloss drops the formula its own Hebrew run carries, and an unflagged ketiv/qere sits on the surrender clause the unit argues from.
P07-006.grounds: All three arms verified. The prior addressee is Zedekiah, named in the relay clause כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְרֻ֖ן אֶל צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.21.3, byte tier), with the oracle body addressing the defenders in the plural at 21:4; the named messengers are couriers. The shift at 21:8 is itself byte-true - the verse opens וְאֶל הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.21.8, byte tier), naming a new addressee - so the seam stands and only its stated point of departure is wrong; it is the same wording defect that stands in the preceding span's rejected alternative. On parity: that spliced run ends on the messenger formula while the gloss stops at the commission clause, “You shall say to this people” (web:Jer.21.8); the formula is rendered inside the same verse in the other witness, so the gap is this row's own cut and not the translation's - gloss extent must equal splice extent. On the variant: the inventory records a ketiv/qere at Jer.21.9 (1 note), the pair יחיה וְחָיָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.9, byte tier), unpointed ketiv then pointed qere, standing on the verb that governs the surrender outcome the row summarises as the terms of surrender and cites among its own evidence refs. No disclosure appears in any field, and no declared queue entry exists for this row because no quote binds to that verse, so the variant is neither declared nor examined on a verse whose content is argued in prose.
P07-006.remedy: boundary_rationale: (a) correct the point of departure to Zedekiah and the defenders addressed in the plural, matching the edit made to the preceding span; (b) extend the English gloss so it covers the whole spliced run through the messenger formula, or shorten the splice to the clause the gloss already covers. device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.21.9 (single-witness). Test the cure must pass: gloss and splice must cover the same clause boundaries in the same field, the corrected addressee sentence must name the party the relay clause at 21:3 names, and every K/Q verse whose content is argued in prose must carry a disclosure even where no quote binds to it.

P07-007.challenge_claim: The declared closure signal is positionally false at both cited sites, the ketiv/qere at 21:12 alternates precisely the addressee the unit's driver depends on, and a conjunctive onset plus an in-span messenger formula go unweighed.
P07-007.grounds: All three arms verified on bytes. Neither cited occurrence is verse-final: at 21:13 the formula stands at words 7-8 of 15 and the verse runs on to its closing question, and at 21:14 it stands at words 5-6 of 12, the verse ending on וְהִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּיַעְרָ֔הּ וְאָכְלָ֖ה כָּל סְבִיבֶֽיהָ (oshb:Jer.21.14, byte tier). Across 21:7, 21:10, 21:13, 21:14 and 22:5 every occurrence is clause-internal, five of five. The ruled reading of this formula is closure corroboration only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows: that holds for 21:14, followed by the commissioning imperative at 22:1, and not for 21:13, which is mid-span. So the closes-twice statement is false as a positional claim and half-false as a closure claim. On the variant: the inventory records a ketiv/qere at Jer.21.12 (1 note), מעלליהם מַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.21.12, byte tier), a third-person-plural ketiv against a second-person-plural qere on the deeds, standing verse-final, with כִּפְרִ֥י מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.21.14, byte tier) unvaried on the qere side. The declared disposition is right on its quote-binding arm - the spliced vocative is verse-initial - but the row's filed driver is the addressee shift and the variant alternates exactly that, so a false positive on quote-binding is not a false positive on the driver. On the onsets: the span opens on וּלְבֵית֙ (oshb:Jer.21.11, byte tier), vav-prefixed and lamed-topical, a conjunctive opening left unweighed against the fresh-address claim; and כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.12, byte tier) stands inside the span without appearing among the filed signals, unlike the adjacent spans at 21:8-21:10 and 22:1-22:9, which file it.
P07-007.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the statement that the oracle closes on the formula twice with a positionally true one - both occurrences are clause-internal, and only the 21:14 occurrence corroborates closure, because a fresh tier-1 onset follows at 22:1; weigh the vav-prefixed conjunctive opening at 21:11 against the fresh-address claim in the same field. observed_substrate_signals: add the messenger-formula key for the in-span occurrence at 21:12, then re-check the dependent fields the driver set governs - unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative. device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.21.12 (single-witness) and state that it alternates the addressee the row's driver turns on. Test the cure must pass: no closure claim may assert a verse-final position the verse's own bytes contradict, and a declared false positive may be closed only on the arm it was declared for.

P07-008.challenge_claim: Both lenses land on the same defect: the rejected alternative's ground, that the messenger-formula restart at 22:6 reopens without a change of frame-owner or addressee, is contradicted by the bytes and by the unit's own rationale sentence. One lens adds that high confidence is not supported once the shift is accounted for and proposes the personification pattern as the better warrant; the other adds an unweighed break at the declined juncture and two undisclosed ketiv/qere verses.
P07-008.grounds: Same core defect reached independently by both lenses; the added arms are distinct, and the core is upheld. At 22:1 the house is the destination of a commission, רֵ֖ד בֵּֽית מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.22.1, byte tier), with no preposition, and 22:2 addresses the king himself, שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.22.2, byte tier), in the singular, אַתָּ֤ה וַעֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.22.2, byte tier). At 22:6 the same three-word phrase returns under ayin-lamed, עַל בֵּית֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.22.6, byte tier), and the address is to the house itself, גִּלְעָ֥ד אַתָּ֛ה לִ֖י (oshb:Jer.22.6, byte tier), continued at 22:7 in מִבְחַ֣ר אֲרָזֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Jer.22.7, byte tier). The phrase is a 7-verse object at consonantal tier (sweep: 7 verses: 21:11, 22:1, 22:6, 27:18, 27:21, 32:2, 38:22) and this span carries two of its members under two different frames. The row's own boundary_rationale states the same turn from the reigning king to the house itself, so the rejected alternative contradicts its own unit as well as the bytes. One added arm needs refining: the shift is not cleanly plural-to-singular, since 22:2's own verb and pronoun are singular and the plural forms stand at 22:3, 22:4 and 22:5; the byte-true description is a change of referent carried by the preposition, not by grammatical number alone. The other added arms hold: the SAMEKH recorded at Jer.22.5 falls after that verse, at exactly the 22:5|22:6 juncture the alternative declines, disclosed in one field and left unweighed in the field it bears on (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver); and two ketiv/qere verses sit inside the span, one note each at Jer.22.4, ועבדו וַעֲבָדָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.22.4, byte tier), inside the promise clause the row paraphrases, and one at Jer.22.6, verse-final - neither disclosed, and only the 22:6 one standing in the declared queue, whose narrow quote-binding arm is confirmed since the quoted English stops well before the variant. High confidence with the frontier flag unset is not supported while the stated ground is byte-contradicted at the juncture it declines. The cut itself is not decided here.
P07-008.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the no-change-of-frame-owner-or-addressee ground with the byte-true one - the frame-owner does not change, but the addressee does, from the king addressed at 22:2 to the house addressed at 22:6 under a different preposition - and keep the span whole on the personification pattern, weighing and explicitly declining the disclosed break after Jer.22.5 in that same field. confidence: lower from high to medium. device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.22.4 and at Jer.22.6 (single-witness, one note each). Do not change the span: a split at 22:5|22:6 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit adoption, never author work. Test the cure must pass: the rewritten ground must not deny a shift the row's own boundary_rationale asserts, it must survive the check that killed the original - the preposition and address contrast between 22:1-22:2 and 22:6-22:7, visible in both witnesses - and every K/Q verse inside the span must be disclosed whether or not a quote binds to it.

P07-009.challenge_claim: A verse-initial messenger formula inside the span is left out of the filed signals, the setumah that divides the span is reported without its internal force, and the type-guess supplies an identification the bytes do not carry.
P07-009.grounds: The first arm is upheld: 22:11 opens on כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה (oshb:Jer.22.11, byte tier), a verse-initial ki-subordinated messenger formula absent from the filed signals, although the same shape is filed for the adjacent spans at 20:1-20:6, 21:1-21:7, 21:8-21:10 and 22:1-22:9. The ki subordinates, so cohesion holds and the cut at 22:9|22:10 is not in doubt. The second arm is overstated. The inventory does record SAMEKH at Jer.22.10, a break after that verse dividing the three-verse span, but the field already carries the within-the-span wording that the same construction is faulted for lacking elsewhere in this part; what remains is only that the break is attributed to the opening verse without saying it separates 22:10 from 22:11-22:12 - a wording correction, not a missing disclosure (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver). The third arm is upheld on both counts: the spliced run from 22:11 stops at the royal title while the gloss runs on through הַמֹּלֵךְ֙ תַּ֚חַת יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו (oshb:Jer.22.11, byte tier), so gloss extent exceeds splice extent; and the type field reads the unnamed dead of 22:10 as Josiah, whom 22:10-22:12 never identify as the dead - he appears there only as Shallum's father and as the king Shallum reigned in place of. A byte-unsupported identification in a row field carries the same discipline as a digit.
P07-009.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: add the messenger-formula key for the verse-initial occurrence at 22:11, then re-check the dependent fields the driver set governs - unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative. device_notes: state that the SAMEKH recorded at Jer.22.10 falls after that verse and therefore separates 22:10 from 22:11-22:12 within the span. boundary_rationale: extend the splice from 22:11 through the reign clause so it covers the gloss, or shorten the gloss to the royal title the splice ends on. literature_type_guess: remove the identification of the dead as Josiah and describe the contrast the verses do carry - no weeping for the dead, weeping for the one who goes away, resolved at 22:11 to Shallum. Test the cure must pass: gloss and splice must cover the same clause boundaries, and no row field may name a referent the span's own verses leave unnamed.

P07-011.challenge_claim: The span closes on a doubled ketiv/qere verse (MT 22:23) with no variant disclosure anywhere in the row and an unqualified span-wide null asserted in its place, and the two notes sit on the very feminine-singular forms the addressee-shift warrant rests on.
P07-011.grounds: The variant layer is byte-confirmed and the omission is real. Two ketiv/qere notes stand at oshb:Jer.22.23 - a member of the twelve doubled-note verses - and both pairs sit inline in the source bytes, unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere: ישבתי יֹשַׁבְתְּ֙ and מקננתי מְקֻנַּ֖נְתְּ (oshb:Jer.22.23, byte tier). The parashah half of the disclosure is exact: a setumah closes oshb:Jer.22.19 and no petuchah or setumah falls in Jer.22.20-Jer.22.23 (single-witness, tier-3 weak). But device_notes then states that no mark falls within the span without naming the layer that statement is true of, over the row's own closing verse, in the book's largest variant inventory. The declared false-positive disposition against that finding fails on its own terms: the verse is inside the span, not adjacent to it, and the notes are two, not one. Where the filed framing overshoots is reach. The stated ground is a feminine-singular address, and both readings in each pair carry that same address - the unpointed forms differ from the pointed ones in the archaic final yod, not in the person addressed - so the variants corroborate the warrant instead of contesting it, and the address is independently byte-visible across the span in זֶ֤ה דַרְכֵּךְ֙ מִנְּעוּרַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Jer.22.21, byte tier) and מִכֹּ֖ל רָעָתֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.22.22, byte tier). The English quoted as closing evidence, “Inhabitant of Lebanon, who makes your nest in the cedars” (web:Jer.22.23), renders a sense both readings support, which is why quote coverage triggers the disclosure duty even though nothing in the rendering turns on the choice - and why the contrary position, that no disclosure is owed because only the English of that verse is cited, does not hold: the span-relevant disclosure duty is unconditional, not quote-conditional. The seam is untouched: עֲלִ֤י הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ וּֽצְעָ֔קִי (oshb:Jer.22.20, byte tier) carries no variant note. Corrected finding: a disclosure and clarity defect at medium, not a warrant defect at high.
P07-011.remedy: In device_notes, qualify the null to the layer it is true of (no petuchah or setumah falls within Jer.22.20-Jer.22.23) and add the variant disclosure: two ketiv/qere notes at oshb:Jer.22.23 (WLC, single-witness), a doubled-note verse, unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere in each pair, with one clause stating that both readings carry the same feminine-singular address so the addressee ground is unaffected. Leave span, confidence, unit_type and observed_substrate_signals unchanged. The cure must pass the test that killed the original: the quote-coverage arm over ketiv/qere verses - an English quotation covering a variant-bearing verse must carry a ketiv/qere disclosure - returns clean, and a span-relevant disclosure sweep over Jer.22.20-Jer.22.23 names every layer (parashah none in span, paseq none, special letters none, ketiv/qere two at 22:23).

P08-001.challenge_claim: The single-unit reading is argued in a device vocabulary that cannot register the recurrent macro-onset formula standing twice inside the span - verse-initially at MT 23:5 and in its lachen shape at MT 23:7, each immediately after a setumah the row itself discloses - while the rejected alternative tests a split point with no such support.
P08-001.grounds: Every arm verifies on the bytes. הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה opens oshb:Jer.23.5 verse-initially and לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה opens oshb:Jer.23.7 (both byte tier). The object is book-wide rather than local colour: the three-word announcement run stands in 15 verses (sweep: 15 verses, MT keys), 14 of them verse-initial - 6 bare and 8 lachen-prefixed - the single non-initial member carrying a ki prefix at oshb:Jer.30.3, and one member falling inside the renumbering zone (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25). Both in-span onsets fall immediately after the two setumahs device_notes already names, so the substrate layer and the formula layer coincide at the same two joins, while the cohesion test is worded as the absence of an addressee, scene or discourse-imperative seam - a vocabulary in which neither join can appear. The closing pair is itself a recurring block: oshb:Jer.23.7-Jer.23.8 shares with oshb:Jer.16.14-Jer.16.15 an identical seven-word consonantal opening and, after the one divergent verb form, an identical sixteen-word consonantal run (skeleton tier), which argues that the pair carries its own header rather than terminating one sustained speech, and that goes undisclosed. Tier discipline holds the finding to the warrant: the announcement formula is a tier-1 text signal but is not among the internal-cut classes the granularity rule licenses, so nothing here decides a seam - whether a recurrent announcement onset can close a unit against the postpositive divine formula standing inside it is left open, and any cut at 23:4|23:5 or 23:6|23:7 remains a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work. Two findings beyond the challenge. First, the tested rival is not signal-free: the direct second-person address to the shepherds, אַתֶּ֞ם הֲפִצֹתֶ֤ם אֶת צֹאנִי֙ (oshb:Jer.23.2, byte tier), is not carried past that join - וַאֲנִ֗י אֲקַבֵּץ֙ (oshb:Jer.23.3, byte tier) opens unaddressed divine first-person speech, and 23:4-23:8 speak of shepherds and flock in the third person - so the flat denial that any addressee seam marks the turn is contestable on the row's own criterion, while what the join genuinely lacks is the announcement onset and any parashah mark. Second, one paseq seg stands at oshb:Jer.23.6 inside the span (count-only, WLC single-witness) and is undisclosed. The residual on the 23:6 name is real but low: an onomastic label is applied with no pointed splice, though no digit rests on it.
P08-001.remedy: (1) device_notes: add the one paseq seg at oshb:Jer.23.6 (count-only, single-witness, no intra-verse position claim) beside the setumahs already named; disclose both in-span announcement onsets with pointed splices bound to oshb:Jer.23.5 and oshb:Jer.23.7 at byte tier, naming the swept object and its digit in the sanctioned shorthand (sweep: 15 verses, MT keys) and writing the zone member dually (oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25) if the set is enumerated; disclose the closing pair's near-twin at oshb:Jer.16.14-Jer.16.15 at skeleton tier as cross-seam texture, explicitly not a boundary driver. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut so the tested join is described by the signals it carries and lacks - the second-person address to the shepherds ends there, while no announcement onset and no parashah mark stands - replacing the unqualified no-addressee denial; one sentence plus at most the mandated rival-disclosure sentence. (3) Either splice the pointed name at oshb:Jer.23.6 with its tier or drop the onomastic label. (4) Span, unit_type and confidence unchanged; no boundary change is author work. Tests the cure must pass: a span-relevant disclosure sweep over Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8 names parashah, paseq and ketiv/qere; every device argued in prose carries a byte-tier splice bound to its cited ref and every digit names its swept object and unit; and the re-cut rejected alternative survives a byte re-read of the join it names - the read the original failed.

P08-002.challenge_claim: Both items strike the same sentence: the rejected alternative grounds cohesion on 23:13-23:14 continuing the same first-person indictment opened at 23:9, but 23:9 carries the prophet's own non-indicting distress and the indicting first person is the divine speaker's, not established until 23:11; the second item adds that this speaker change meets the row's own opening-seam criterion at a point inside the span it never engages.
P08-002.grounds: Same defect at core, with the second item adding a distinct arm; both hold on the bytes. At oshb:Jer.23.9 the first person is the prophet's and accuses no one - נִשְׁבַּ֧ר לִבִּ֣י בְקִרְבִּ֗י - with the divine name standing in the third person in that same verse, מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (both byte tier); that is precisely the ground boundary_rationale uses to open the unit. From oshb:Jer.23.11 the first person is the divine speaker's, גַּם בְּבֵיתִ֛י מָצָ֥אתִי רָעָתָ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte tier), with the postpositive formula closing 23:12 as well, and that voice carries רָאִ֣יתִי תִפְלָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.23.13, byte tier) into the sentence at 23:15. The rejected alternative's predicate is therefore false on the bytes and inconsistent with the row's own opening account - a blended speech-role claim of exactly the class the frame-ownership discipline forbids, where the mouth is named at the seam and then left unnamed across the body. The second arm is a genuine disclosure gap: the voice change treated as seam-worthy at the opening recurs inside the span and is never named. It does not, however, open a rival seam - oshb:Jer.23.11 opens כִּֽי גַם (byte tier), a ki-subordinated clause continuing the ground of 23:10, and no tier-1 onset device stands at that join - so cohesion holds and the cut itself is not in doubt. On the disclosure layers nothing further is owed: the marks disclosed over the span are correct under type (setumah at 23:13 and 23:14, petuchah at 23:15, single-witness, tier-3 weak) and no ketiv/qere note or paseq seg falls in Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15.
P08-002.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the ground so it names the mouth at each first person - the opening distress at Jer.23.9 is the prophet's, with the divine speaker in the third person there, while the indicting first person runs from Jer.23.11 through the sentence at Jer.23.15 - and rest the cohesion on the ki-subordination at Jer.23.11 and on the sentence that 23:13-23:14 feeds, not on one continuous voice. Keep to one sentence plus at most the mandated rival-disclosure sentence; span, unit_type, confidence and observed_substrate_signals unchanged. Tests the cure must pass: every first-person claim in the field names whose mouth carries it, and the re-cut sentence survives the byte read of oshb:Jer.23.9 and oshb:Jer.23.11 that killed the original.

P08-003.challenge_claim: The row's own splice shows the opening verse is carried by a verse-initial koh-amar-tsevaot frame, yet the opener is labelled a discourse-frame imperative, the mouth carrying the formula is never named, and the frame is absent from the declared signals - while the rejected alternative excuses the following seam for lacking exactly that marker.
P08-003.grounds: Verified at every point. oshb:Jer.23.16 opens verse-initially on כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת (byte tier); the imperative the rationale names, אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ (byte tier), stands after it, not at the verse head. The splice filed in boundary_rationale contains the whole run including the frame, yet the opener is described only as a discourse-frame imperative and observed_substrate_signals records only the imperative and the addressee shift, so the leading device of the row's own splice is neither named nor filed. Gloss parity fails in the same place, and by the row's own cut rather than the translation's: the English quotation begins after the frame, though the other witness renders it in that same verse, “Yahweh of Armies says,” (web:Jer.23.16), so gloss extent falls short of splice extent. Naming the mouth is substantive here, not pedantic: the tsevaot form of the messenger formula stands in 50 verses (sweep: 50 verses, MT keys), 21 of them verse-initial, and that verse-initial set holds both oshb:Jer.23.16, where the mouth is the divine speaker's reported by the prophet, and oshb:Jer.28.2, where the identical shape is in a false prophet's mouth. The self-inconsistency is real as filed: strongest_rejected_alternative excuses the following seam as opening even without a formal imperative or koh-amar marker, while the row's own opening verse carries one unnamed. One finding beyond the challenge: a paseq seg stands at oshb:Jer.23.19 inside the span (count-only, WLC single-witness) and is undisclosed, alongside the parashah and ketiv/qere disclosures device_notes does carry correctly (petuchah at 23:15 before the span, setumah at 23:18 and 23:22, the span's one variant note at 23:18 consulted and not spliced). The seam at 23:15|23:16 is not in doubt - on the bytes it is better warranted than the row claims.
P08-003.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-describe the opener as the verse-initial messenger frame at oshb:Jer.23.16 with the imperative following it, name the mouth as the divine speaker's reported by the prophet, and extend the English gloss to cover the whole spliced run so gloss extent equals splice extent. (2) observed_substrate_signals: add speech_formula.koh_amar; if the messenger frame is recorded as the leading device rather than a co-signal, treat strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence as dependent fields and re-check them in the same edit. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut so it no longer rests on the absence of a marker the row's own opening verse carries. (4) device_notes: add the one paseq seg at oshb:Jer.23.19 (count-only, single-witness, no position claim). (5) Span unchanged. Tests the cure must pass: gloss extent equals splice extent on every spliced run; every device standing inside a splice appears in the signal list; a span-relevant disclosure sweep over Jer.23.16-Jer.23.22 names parashah, ketiv/qere and paseq; and the rejected alternative no longer cites the absence of a device the row itself splices - the check the original failed.

P08-005.challenge_claim: The unit's defining device - the burden/oracle wordplay supplying the literature type and the whole cohesion argument - is asserted in English only with no pointed splice, the English witness quoted never carries the burden sense at all, and the byte-level pun closing the unit at 23:39 goes unengaged.
P08-005.grounds: Upheld on all three arms, and the splice arm is sharper than filed. The opening splice ends at לֵאמֹ֔ר (oshb:Jer.23.33, byte tier), immediately before the question phrase that carries the noun twice in that same verse: מַה מַשָּׂ֖א יְהוָ֑ה and אֶת מַה מַשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Jer.23.33, byte tier). The quoted English cannot supply the double sense - across web:Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40 that witness renders the noun as the message word 8 times and the burden word 0 times - so a boundary-relevant claim about a two-sense Hebrew noun rests on no quoted evidence, where the engagement class makes a pointed splice with its tier mandatory. The token is hazardous in the direction left undisclosed: the bare noun stands in 7 verses (sweep: 7 verses, MT keys), 4 of them in the sabbath-load material of ch 17 and 3 inside this span, because both forms at oshb:Jer.23.36 are prefixed and invisible to a bare-token sweep. The closing resolution is byte-real and unengaged: oshb:Jer.23.39 reads וְנָשִׁ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם נָשֹׁ֑א (byte tier), whose infinitive absolute carries the same consonantal skeleton as the noun the unit turns on and stands as a bare token in 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys), so the sentence described only as one of forgetting is where the wordplay resolves at byte level. The continuity claim on 23:38 is true but unevidenced and unfiled: oshb:Jer.23.38 does carry לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier), the divine speaker's own mouth with no tsevaot in that verse, yet no form of it is quoted and observed_substrate_signals records only the discourse imperative and a scene shift. Not in dispute and correctly handled: unit_type stays inside the closed vocabulary with the wordplay kept out of it, the one parashah mark in the span is cited correctly under its type, and no ketiv/qere note or paseq seg falls in Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40. The span itself is not challenged.
P08-005.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: splice both occurrences of the noun from oshb:Jer.23.33 at byte tier with the ref and tier named, and state the double sense as a claim about the Hebrew, adding that the quoted English witness renders the noun with a single word throughout the span (sweep: 8 occurrences of the message word and 0 of the burden word over web:Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40) so the double sense is not taken from the English. (2) Splice the frame from oshb:Jer.23.38 at byte tier naming the mouth, and add speech_formula.koh_amar to observed_substrate_signals. (3) Either engage the closing resolution at oshb:Jer.23.39 with its pointed splice, its skeleton relation to the noun and its digit (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys), or drop the claim that the unit closes on the wordplay's own sentence. (4) Wherever the bare-token digit is used, name the swept object and disclose the two prefixed forms at oshb:Jer.23.36 that a bare-token sweep does not see. (5) Span, unit_type and confidence unchanged. Tests the cure must pass: every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim carries a pointed splice bound to its cited ref that re-collates at byte tier with no normalization required; every device argued in prose appears in the signal list; and every digit names its swept object and unit - the tests the original claim never faced.

P08-006.challenge_claim: Onset and closing warrant are byte-true at the claimed positions, but a byte-true clause straddles this unit's own cut and is left undisclosed while confidence stands at high with the frontier flag unset.
P08-006.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. The inedibility clause אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹֽעַ (oshb:Jer.24.3, byte tier) stands in this unit's own closing verse, again at 24:2 inside the span, and again in the first verse on the far side of the cut, אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹ֑עַ (oshb:Jer.24.8, byte tier); the two differ only in the accent on the last word, so the recurrence holds at skeleton tier and not at byte tier (sweep: 4 verses -- 24:2, 24:3, 24:8, 29:17 -- three of the four inside this chapter). Neither the boundary rationale nor the device notes reaches it, and the rejected alternative engages continuity only through the word-event form. Cross-seam cohesion binds: a byte-true device straddling a unit's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and the calibration here is high with the frontier flag unset. The seam itself survives: 24:4 opens verse-initially on וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.24.4, byte tier), a member of the narrative word-event shape (sweep: 21 verses at skeleton tier), a tier-1 device that outweighs a descriptive clause whose fourth site at 29:17 shows it to be figure-vocabulary rather than a structural marker. Low is the right weight. One correction to the challenge's own supporting citation: the digit offered for the word-event shape belongs to a five-word string ending in the infinitive of speaking (sweep: 6 verses at skeleton tier), not to the three-word string quoted beside it (sweep: 21 verses) -- a reproduced digit carried on a narrower object than the one named.
P08-006.remedy: In device_notes, disclose the inedibility clause as a cross-seam recurrence: name the clause, give its verse count and sites (sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier), and state that it is weighed and does not overturn the word-event seam at 24:4. Then set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered to true, or argue in boundary_rationale why high survives the disclosed straddle. Cure test: the disclosed clause must carry a digit-bearing count naming its tier, and the calibration fields must be consistent with an acknowledged continuity counterweight -- the test the original failed was cross-seam silence at high confidence.

P09-001.challenge_claim: Both items make the same charge: the prose separates the one-site concerning-form header from the eleven-site to-form class correctly, but the declared structured signal carries the class stem with no marker distinguishing the variant, so a one-site object is aggregable into an eleven-site object at exactly the level where the three word-event shapes must stay distinct.
P09-001.grounds: Same defect reached independently by both lenses, not two distinct items. The bytes are as the prose states: 25:1 opens verse-initially on הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה עַֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.25.1, byte tier), ayin-lamed, against the class shape הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.7.1, byte tier), aleph-lamed, and the two objects separate cleanly (sweep: concerning-form header 1 verse; to-form header 11 verses, both at skeleton tier). The declared key is the bare stem the two share, and that stem is itself a blended object: it stands in 12 verses -- the 11 class sites plus 25:1 (sweep: 12 verses at skeleton tier). The hazard is not hypothetical. The same bare stem with no preposition marker is the declared signal on the units headed at 30:1, 40:1 and 44:1, all class members, so as the corpus stands the variant is already indistinguishable from the class under any key-level aggregation, while other class units do carry a preposition-marked key. That live collision, not the prose, carries the severity: medium is right and low understates it.
P09-001.remedy: In observed_substrate_signals, replace the bare-stem word-event key with one that marks the variant preposition, following the shape of the preposition-marked key already used on class members; leave boundary_rationale unchanged, its reading being correct. Cure test: aggregate the corpus by word-event signal key and confirm the 25:1 unit no longer falls in the same bucket as the units headed at 30:1, 40:1 and 44:1 -- the test the original failed was key-level indistinguishability from the eleven-verse class.

P09-002.challenge_claim: The unit registers a closure signal that its own close does not carry: the closing verse carries 0 neum tokens, and the 2 tokens inside the span both sit mid-verse, so the declared signal has nothing in this span's bytes to rest on.
P09-002.grounds: The byte facts hold exactly. The close reads וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.25.14, byte tier) and carries none of the formula -- the 162-verse inventory does not list it -- and the two in-span tokens at 25:9 and 25:12 both sit mid-verse and neither closes anything. What the framing overstates is that the signal has nothing to rest on. It rests on the front seam one verse before the span: 25:7 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.7, byte tier) and 25:8 opens verse-initially on לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.25.8, byte tier), a fresh tier-1 onset -- which is precisely the condition under which the ruled treatment lets that formula do closure work, and it is the pairing the boundary rationale itself names. Corrected finding: not a baseless key but an unscoped one, reading as a claim about this unit's own close where the bytes give nothing. Severity holds at low.
P09-002.remedy: Either bind the closure key to the seam it rests on by qualifying it as a front-seam signal, or drop it and let the koh-amar onset key carry the seam alone; in boundary_rationale, state that the closing verse carries no closure formula, so the close rests on the recompense clause completing the sentence begun at 25:8. Cure test: every declared closure signal must be present in the verse it is claimed of -- the test the original failed was a closure key whose only support lies outside the span. For consolidation: this is a corpus_wide_orders candidate rather than a one-unit fix. Ten units declare that closure key and six of them end on a verse carrying none of the 162, and the signal-field contract does not say whether a key may name a device outside the unit's own span; one order should settle the scope question rather than six independent guesses.

P09-003.challenge_claim: The no-split ruling at 25:27 rests on an addressee the bytes contradict, and a second frame-command of the same shape stands undisclosed inside the span at 25:28.
P09-003.grounds: Both halves verified on bytes. 25:27 opens on וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֡ם (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier), a second-person-singular frame-command directed at the prophet, rendered “You shall tell them” (web:Jer.25.27); the forms addressed to the nations are the plurals inside the quoted speech it introduces, שְׁת֤וּ וְשִׁכְרוּ֙ וּקְי֔וּ וְנִפְל֖וּ (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier). Calling that verse a discourse imperative addressed to the nations collapses the outer frame into its own quoted speech, and the rejected alternative's stated ground -- that the addressee stays the same nations already compelled to drink -- is the part the bytes contest. That is where it bites: a rejected alternative is where the replacement warrant has to hold. The second half holds too. The same frame-command stands again inside the span at וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.25.28, byte tier), unmentioned, so the span carries two rival command seams where the prose weighs one (sweep: 18 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, three of them consecutive here at 25:27, 25:28 and 25:30). The one-unit outcome is not overturned -- command, performance and enforcement still hold together on the ruled symbolic-act rule -- and the closing verse carries a genuine postpositive closure device the unit passes over, נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.25.29, byte tier; sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier). Medium is proportionate: prose and rejected-alternative repair, no boundary change.
P09-003.remedy: In boundary_rationale, recut the 25:27 sentence so the frame-command is described as addressed to the prophet and the drinking imperatives as the nations' address inside the quoted speech. In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the addressee ground with the command-and-performance ground that actually carries the one-unit reading, and name the second frame-command at 25:28 as a further rival set aside. In device_notes, record the verse-final closure formula at 25:29 as the close's own corroboration, with its digit and tier. Cure test: every command in the span is read against its verbal form and its addressee before the prose asserts either -- the test the original failed was assigning a second-person-singular frame-command to the plural audience of the speech it introduces.

P09-004.challenge_claim: The seam device is asserted through the English alone and labelled with a form-class the pointed bytes do not carry, while the decisive byte fact for this seam (a single-site construction) goes unused.
P09-004.grounds: The evidence half is right and stands. P09-004.remedy: In boundary_rationale, splice the verse-initial seam construction from 25:30 with its oshb ref and tier named, and either qualify the form word -- command force carried by the fronted pronoun and the following frame-command, not by an imperative form -- or drop the form word; add the single-site digit (sweep: 1 verse at skeleton tier) beside it and state that the 18-verse frame-command shape in the same verse is not the discriminator. In observed_substrate_signals, add a key for the discourse-frame onset the rationale names as the driver, and remove or re-scope the closure key, whose device is absent from the closing verse. Cure test: every device the rationale names as a seam driver appears as a splice with its tier and as a declared signal, and every declared closure signal is present in the verse it is claimed of -- the tests the original failed were an English-only seam warrant and a driver with no signal entry.

P09-006.challenge_claim: One item: the opening edge is warranted but the closing edge at 26:6 has no warrant at all, the participant and scene shift opening immediately after being neither cited nor discussed. The other: the unit is cut exactly where its commissioned words are performed and quoted back, with neither the straddling material nor the resulting risk disclosed while confidence stands at high with the frontier flag unset, and the site is named in prose by the other byform.

The straddle is byte-true in two devices. The threat in the closing verse, וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier), returns as the charge laid against the prophet at כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier): the house phrase is a narrow object (sweep: 6 verses at skeleton tier, half of them in this chapter) and the Shiloh element is per-site, the closing verse's spelling a single site in the book (sweep: 1 verse) against nine for the spelling used across the cut. And the command אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier) is reported carried out at אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier). Neither device is disclosed, and the calibration is high with the frontier flag unset. The byform sub-item does not stand: the construction's campaign name covers all three sites in two spellings, and the site's own attested plene form בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלְכ֛וּת (oshb:Jer.26.1, byte tier) is spliced byte-true in the very sentence that uses the class name, against בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת (oshb:Jer.27.1, byte tier) at the other two (sweep: 1 verse and 2 verses at skeleton tier) -- no digit or form claim is left unattested, so there is nothing to cure there. Medium on the principal charges. This seam is shared with the unit opening at 26:7, and the two cures are one edit.
P09-006.remedy: Paired seam edit, made once for both sides. In boundary_rationale, add the closing-edge warrant: name the participant and scene change at 26:7 as the ruled seam class that stops this unit at 26:6, and add web:Jer.26.7 to boundary_evidence_refs. In device_notes, disclose the two straddling devices -- the threat quoted back at 26:9 with the per-site Shiloh spellings and their digits, and the command reported performed at 26:8 -- and state that they are weighed as continuity and do not overturn the participant seam.
