Cure test: the closing seam carries a named tier-1 warrant plus a reference to the verse that opens after it, and every device crossing the seam is disclosed with its count and tier -- the tests the original failed were a warrantless close and an undisclosed command-and-quotation straddle at high confidence.

P09-007.challenge_claim: The front seam at 26:7 is argued as a clean turn to public narration while two byte-true devices inside the span reach back across it undisclosed, and the boundary is still rated high confidence; the Hebrew engagement offered for the seam is a verb shape that also opens the next seam, so it does not discriminate between the two cuts.
P09-007.grounds: The byte facts are right. The completion clause אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier) reports the charge אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier) carried out; the threat is quoted back at כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier) from וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier), the per-site spellings differing (sweep: 1 verse and 9 verses at skeleton tier); and the seam verb וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֛וּ (oshb:Jer.26.7, byte tier) recurs at וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.26.10, byte tier), one of 7 verses at skeleton tier, so it does not by itself separate the two cuts. Two corrections lower the weight. The continuity relation is not wholly unstated: the rationale names this scene as the one where the preceding private instruction is carried out, so what is missing is the byte-level engagement -- no splice, no digit, no weighing -- rather than the relation itself. And the seam is not carried by the verb: the discriminator the unit states is the participant and scene change, a ruled tier-1 class evidenced by a byte-true splice at the seam verse, with the verb as corroboration. What remains is a disclosure gap plus calibration at high confidence on a boundary that does argue both its edges, the far edge through its rejected alternative. Refined to low.
P09-007.remedy: In device_notes, disclose the two devices reaching back over the front seam -- the completion clause answering the charge, and the threat quoted back with its per-site spellings and digits -- and state that they are weighed against the participant seam and do not overturn it. Set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered to true, or argue in boundary_rationale why high survives the disclosed anaphora. This is the same seam as the unit closing at 26:6: make the two disclosures as one paired edit so both sides agree. Cure test: every byte-true device crossing this seam appears once on each side of the pair with a digit and a tier -- the test the original failed was an English-only allusion to the command-and-performance relation carried at high confidence.

P09-008.challenge_claim: The closure argument rests on an untiered verbatim-class recurrence claim that the bytes contest: accusation and acquittal share a collocation but neither an order nor an accentuation.
P09-008.grounds: Verified. The accusation reads מִשְׁפַּט מָ֨וֶת֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.11, byte tier) and the verdict אֵין לָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ מִשְׁפַּט מָ֔וֶת (oshb:Jer.26.16, byte tier): the same four words, reordered around the negator, and each of the three accented words differently accented across the two verses -- so the recurrence is not byte-identical, and it is not a contiguous four-word run at skeleton tier either. What does recur is two two-word collocations, the death-sentence pair and the this-man pair, each confined to these two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses apiece at skeleton tier). The rationale's claim that the verdict answers the charge in the very words used to accuse is a recurrence claim carrying no tier label, which the standing rule requires at write time, and the exclusivity that would have sharpened it is available and unclaimed. The echo is real and the boundary is untouched; the defect is one of labelling. Low.
P09-008.remedy: In boundary_rationale, replace the very-words wording with a tier-labelled statement: the verdict reuses the accusation's death-sentence and this-man collocations, reordered around the negator, matching at skeleton tier and not at byte tier, each collocation confined to these two verses (sweep: 2 verses each). Cure test: no recurrence claim stands without its tier, and no word-order identity is implied where the bytes reorder -- the test the original failed was an unlabelled verbatim-class claim over a reordered pair.

P09-009.challenge_claim: Both original-language disclosures overstate what the bytes give: the ketiv/qere is reported one word too wide, and the plene Jerusalem contrast is drawn against a comparand that does not isolate the plene variable.
P09-009.grounds: Both arms are byte-true. MT 26:18 runs מיכיה מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier): the unpointed ketiv, then the pointed qere, then ordinary pointed text; the note inventory carries exactly one note at that verse, covering one word. The row names מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י as the qere, which annexes an unnoted word into the apparatus. Second, the plene site is vav-prefixed, וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), while the comparand offered from 25:18 is יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Jer.25.18, byte tier), unprefixed, so the pair varies the conjunction as well as the mater; a same-shape comparand stands in the bytes at וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.27.21, byte tier, also at oshb:Jer.27.20) (sweep: vav-prefixed defective spelling 6 verses; plene spelling 1 verse, this site). Two further defects at the same verse, raised by neither item: the seg inventory carries a paseq at MT 26:18, inside this span, and the row's disclosure sentence speaks only to parashah marks, so the span's seg-layer disclosure is incomplete (count-only, single-witness); and the gloss “Zion will be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps” (web:Jer.26.18) is paired with a splice ending at וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ that does not contain עִיִּ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), so quote and splice are not co-extensive. The seam at 26:17 and the medium_low calibration are untouched; severity is medium on the added findings, not on the challenge as framed, which sits at low.
P09-009.remedy: boundary_rationale: cut the qere report to the single word the note covers (ketiv מיכיה against qere מִיכָה֙), leaving הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י as ordinary text; replace the 25:18 comparand with the vav-prefixed defective spelling at oshb:Jer.27.20 or oshb:Jer.27.21 so the pair varies only the mater, each spelling carrying a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; re-cut the Zion/Jerusalem pairing so the English and the splice are co-extensive (extend the splice through עִיִּ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה or shorten the quote to end at Jerusalem). boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.27.20 / oshb:Jer.27.21 (and web: counterparts) for the new comparand and drop the 25:18 pair if it is no longer argued. device_notes: add the paseq at oshb:Jer.26.18 as count-only, single-witness. Tests the cure must pass: the qere sentence names exactly the one word the note carries; the spelling pair differs in one variable only; every English quote is byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its paired splice; and every verse argued in prose outside the span appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

P09-010.challenge_claim: Each of the row's two pivots turns on a particle it does not weigh: the opening coordinator is byte evidence for the reading the row rejects, and the closing adversative that carries the asserted contrast is left outside the splice while the English reaches wider than the splice does.
P09-010.grounds: The first arm is upheld and the second is real but mis-framed. Upheld: the row's own first word is the coordinator וְגַם (oshb:Jer.26.20, byte tier), which is the byte ground for reading 26:20-26:23 as continuing the elders' speech — the very reading the rationale sets aside with the assertion that the case stands on its own footing; a device sitting at the row's own opening seam argues continuity unless it is answered, and strongest_rejected_alternative answers a different rival (splitting off 26:24). Real but mis-framed: the adversative אַ֗ךְ (oshb:Jer.26.24, byte tier) is indeed outside the splice, which begins at יַ֚ד, and it is the one byte carrying the contrast the same sentence asserts — but the added charge that the English reaches wider is byte-false here: the paired quote “the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah” (web:Jer.26.24) also begins after the adversative, since the verse reads “But the hand of Ahikam” (web:Jer.26.24); gloss and splice are co-extensive and simply start one word late. That charge does land one verse-set earlier in the same row, unraised by either item: “There was also a man who prophesied in Yahweh’s name” (web:Jer.26.20) is paired with a splice ending at מִתְנַבֵּא֙ which does not contain בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.20, byte tier). Disclosure is otherwise correct: the petuchah at MT 26:24 is the only inventory entry across 26:20-26:24, with no segs and no notes there. The boundary is untouched.
P09-010.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the 26:24 splice and its paired English one word left so both begin at the adversative אַ֗ךְ, since the contrast asserted in that sentence rests on it; extend the 26:20 splice through בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה so it covers the English paired with it. boundary_rationale or strongest_rejected_alternative (within its two-sentence limit): add one clause weighing the opening coordinator וְגַם as the byte ground for the continuation reading and saying why the participant turn still governs. Tests the cure must pass: every splice is co-extensive with the English quoted beside it; and the row answers the question its own first word raises — which byte at 26:20 argues against this cut, and what answers it.

P10-001.challenge_claim: The stated ground for holding Jer.27.1-Jer.27.11 together is byte-refuted — the row denies any fresh discourse imperative in verses 5 through 10 and 27:9 carries one — the closure signal in the row's own last verse goes unquoted, three glosses reach past their splices, and the pre-seam false-prophecy clause recurs past the seam undisclosed.
P10-001.grounds: The absence claim fails on the bytes at exactly one of its three limbs. 27:9 opens וְ֠אַתֶּם אַל תִּשְׁמְע֨וּ אֶל נְבִיאֵיכֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.27.9, byte tier): the fronted second-person plural pronoun, then the negative particle with a prefix-conjugation verb — a directive shape, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so it is named by its bytes rather than form-labelled. The shape recurs (sweep: 6 verses book-wide, four in this chapter — 27:9, 27:14, 27:16, 27:17). The row's other two limbs hold: no messenger formula reopens between 27:5 and 27:10 (the chapter's koh-amar sites are 27:2, 27:4, 27:16, 27:19, 27:21) and no addressee changes there, so the one-unit outcome survives — the cure is the stated ground, not the span. The closure device is likewise byte-true and unused: 27:11 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.11, byte tier) and the splice stops at וַֽעֲבָד֑וֹ; with a fresh addressee onset at 27:12, closure corroboration is available at this row's own seam and is in neither the quotation nor the declared signals. The three pairing defects are confirmed: at 27:1 the English runs to “this word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.27.1) while the splice ends at מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה; at 27:3 the English carries “to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah” (web:Jer.27.3) while the splice is only אֶל צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה, not הַבָּאִ֣ים יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.27.3, byte tier); at 27:11 the English carries “that nation I will let remain in their own land,” (web:Jer.27.11) while the splice stops before וְהִנַּחְתִּ֤יו עַל אַדְמָתוֹ֙. The cross-seam recurrence is upheld with its count object corrected: the clause as quoted, כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֣ים לָכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.27.10, byte tier), stands in 2 verses — 27:10 inside the span and 27:14 past its close — not 3; the 3-verse figure belongs to the clause taken without the opening particle, whose third site prefixes the noun and so breaks contiguity. Added, unraised by either item: a second formula shape inside the span is unnamed — 27:2 opens כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.27.2, byte tier), the bare shape addressed to the prophet (sweep: bare shape 152 verses; the full stack the row does declare, 32 verses) — and the row's splice of that verse begins after it. The held-open royal-name crux is handled correctly (sweep: defective spelling 1 verse; full spelling 22 verses), the construction is verse-initial as treated, the inventories carry no entry anywhere in 27:1-27:11, and the disclosed petuchah at MT 26:24 checks out. The pairing class recurs at 26:18, 26:20, 27:18, 28:1 and 28:4 among the rows adjudicated here, so its cure is a sweep across the part, not a spot fix.
P10-001.remedy: boundary_rationale: restate the one-unit ground to what the bytes support — no messenger formula reopening and no addressee change between 27:5 and 27:10 — and either drop the no-fresh-discourse-imperative limb or disclose the directive at 27:9 and say why it does not cut (it addresses the audience already addressed since the relayed message opened); re-cut the 27:1, 27:3 and 27:11 pairings so quote and splice are co-extensive; extend the 27:11 splice through נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה; add the 27:2 formula shape, named as its own count object with a digit-bearing sweep. observed_substrate_signals: add the closure-formula key for oshb:Jer.27.11 and a key for the bare formula shape at oshb:Jer.27.2. device_notes: disclose the false-prophecy clause recurring past this row's own close at 27:14, citing the swept form and its digit. Tests the cure must pass: no absence claim survives unless a sweep of its own object returns nothing in the span; every English quote is byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its splice; every recurrence digit names the exact form swept and its unit; and the span stays as tiled — this is a rationale and evidence-field cure, not a respan.

P10-002.challenge_claim: The addressee turn anchoring this seam is byte-true, but a two-device refrain straddles the seam undisclosed and the ruled closure signal inside the row's own final verse is neither quoted nor listed.
P10-002.grounds: The straddle is byte-true at both devices. 27:14, inside the span, carries וְאַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י הַנְּבִאִ֗ים and closes כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.14, byte tier); 27:16, the first verse past this row's close, carries אַֽל תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֗ם and כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖מָּה נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte tier). Both devices therefore stand on either side of the row's own closing seam undisclosed, and 27:14 is the one verse of the span the rationale never engages. The count objects want naming: the clause with its opening particle stands in 2 verses (27:10, 27:14) and the pronoun byform in 1 (27:16), while the 3-verse figure belongs to the clause taken without that particle; the directive shape sweeps to 6 verses book-wide, four in this chapter. The closure arm is likewise byte-true: 27:15 opens כִּ֣י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.15, byte tier) and the splice begins at וְהֵ֛ם, so with a fresh addressee onset at 27:16 the corroboration standing in the row's own last verse is absent from both quotation and signals. Verified sound: both addressee turns are verse-initial and byte-true; the inventories carry no mark, no seg and no note anywhere in 27:11-27:15, as the row states; and this row's three paired quotes are each co-extensive with their splices, so the pairing defect running through its neighbours is absent here. The boundary stands — the defect is disclosure, not tiling.
P10-002.remedy: device_notes: disclose the two devices recurring across the closing seam — the negative-listening directive and the false-prophecy clause standing at 27:14 inside the span and again at 27:16 immediately past it — each with a digit-bearing sweep naming the exact form swept (clause with the particle 2 verses; pronoun byform 1 verse; directive 6 verses book-wide, four in this chapter), and state why the addressee turn still governs the seam. boundary_rationale: extend the 27:15 splice left to include כִּ֣י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה so the closure formula is quoted, and engage 27:14, the one verse of the span currently passed over. observed_substrate_signals: add the closure-formula key for oshb:Jer.27.15. Tests the cure must pass: no verse inside the span is left unengaged while carrying a device that recurs past the span's own edge; every recurrence citation names the swept form and its unit; and the added quotation stays byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its splice.

P10-003.challenge_claim: The declared speech-formula signal names an object that is not the one at the row's own onset, and three distinct formula shapes inside the span are carried under that single label, including the book's full divine stack at 27:21, which is never named.
P10-003.grounds: Byte-confirmed at all three sites. The onset formula, inside the row's own opening splice, is bare: כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.27.16, byte tier), with no tsevaot, while the declared signal names the tsevaot object. The span then changes shape twice: כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.27.19, byte tier), and כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.27.21, byte tier), the full divine stack, which is its own count object. The three are distinct objects on the bytes (sweep: bare shape 152 verses; tsevaot shape 50 verses; full stack 32 verses, 31 of them with the koh-amar opener), so one key across all three blends count objects that the semantic-class discipline keeps apart, and the site carrying the book's signature stack goes unnamed anywhere in the row while the rejected alternative reaches only the second site. The continuity conclusion itself survives: the mouth and the addressee do run on from 27:16 through 27:22, so the one-unit ruling is not disturbed — the defect is the signal key and the unnamed object. Added, unraised by either item: the 27:18 pairing is not co-extensive — the English runs the whole verse from “But if they are prophets” to “don’t go to Babylon.” (web:Jer.27.18) while the paired splice is only יִפְגְּעוּ נָא֙ בַּֽיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.27.18, byte tier). Disclosure is otherwise complete and correctly typed: petuchah at MT 27:18 and MT 27:22, setumah at MT 27:20, the seg at MT 27:18 cited count-only, and MT 27:15 unmarked.

P10-005.challenge_claim: The row dismisses an internal seam at 28:7 on the ground that no speaker, addressee or formula marks the turn, but 28:7 opens verse-initially with a contrastive particle plus a hear-this-word imperative and an explicit second-person addressee, and neither 28:7 nor 28:8 is quoted anywhere in the row.
P10-005.grounds: The bytes are exactly as challenged: oshb:Jer.28.7 opens אַךְ שְׁמַֽע נָא֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה and continues אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֣ר בְּאָזְנֶ֑יךָ (byte tier) - a verse-initial contrastive particle, a second-person-singular hear-now imperative with a demonstrative object, and an explicit second-person addressee marking, standing at the turn the rejection weighs; the rationale names a contrastive hinge with no form and no verse, and of the five verses in the span the pointed splices cover 28:5, 28:6 and 28:9 only, so the two verses carrying the rejected rival are the two left unquoted. To that extent the absence word 'formula' over-reaches and the defect is real. The challenge's inference does not stand. The shape at 28:7 is the second-person-singular appeal form (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier - 28:7, 28:15, 37:20, 38:20), whose two sites outside this chapter fall inside the courtly address to the king, and its object here is the speaker's own word, not the word of YHWH; the summons form that the ruled internal-seam classes name as a discourse-frame imperative is the plural word-of-YHWH shape (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier), which the span does not carry. The claim that one device is read two ways in one scene fails on bytes: the same second-person appeal shape stands at oshb:Jer.28.15 שְׁמַֽע נָ֣א חֲנַנְיָ֑ה (byte tier), and the seam there is carried by the narrative reply formula reopening after the intervening word event at 28:12, not by the imperative - so the device carries no seam at either site. The speaker and addressee arms of the rejection are byte-true: 28:6 already addresses Hananiah in the second person singular, and 28:6 itself carries the resumptive narrative speech formula וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא (oshb:Jer.28.6, byte), so the repeated speaker formula inside the span stands at 28:6 and not at the weighed turn. Tier-1 text signals throughout; the parashah, paseq and ketiv/qere layers are empty at every MT key from 28:4 through 28:9, matching the disclosed silence.
P10-005.remedy: In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the blanket absence with the named shape: state that 28:7 opens on a contrastive particle and a second-person-singular hear-now imperative whose object is the speaker's own word, then give the holding ground - no speaker or addressee change from 28:6, and the imperative is not the plural word-of-YHWH summons form that the internal-seam classes name. In boundary_rationale, splice the pointed 28:7 hinge at the site where it is argued instead of describing it. Test the cure must pass: a byte read of oshb:Jer.28.7 and oshb:Jer.28.8 must contradict no absence word left in the sentence - the test that killed the original.

P10-006.challenge_claim: First item: the rejected-alternative sentence identifies neighbouring material by narrative position twice instead of by verse. Second item: the rationale calls the formula at 28:11 the full divine formula carried again, where the bytes give the bare two-word shape, and the English gloss departs from the paired Hebrew splice at both ends.
P10-006.grounds: Both items stand and they are distinct defects in different fields. Register: strongest_rejected_alternative carries two position-only cross-references to neighbouring units inside one sentence, where cross-unit references are required to be verse-anchored; a position-only description cannot be checked against bytes on its own terms and stops naming the same material if the sequence changes. Formula object: oshb:Jer.28.11 reads כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (byte tier), the bare two-word shape, while oshb:Jer.28.2 reads כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (byte tier), the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack. These are separate count objects - the koh-amar-headed full stack stands in 31 verses book-wide (sweep: 31 verses, skeleton tier), among them 28:2 and 28:14 but not 28:11 - so calling the 28:11 occurrence the full formula carried again imports the 28:2 form onto a verse that does not carry it, and the row's own signal key names the bare shape, leaving key and prose in disagreement about one site. Gloss parity: the pointed run spliced there runs from the formula through the king's name, while the English paired with it drops the formula's own rendering at the front and runs past the splice to the two-year clause at the back (web:Jer.28.11); each quoted English string is verbatim against the staged text, so the defect is extent, not fidelity. What verifies and must not be disturbed by the cure: the mouth is named as Hananiah's and is byte-true at the verse-initial speech formula of 28:11; the vav-less defective royal-name form at 28:11 is the spelling the bytes carry; and the petuchah and the single paseq seg recorded at MT 28:11 both match the inventories under the types claimed.
P10-006.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace both position-only references with verse anchors (the formula at verse 2; the word event at verse 12), keeping the field to its one-sentence rule. boundary_rationale: name the 28:11 formula as the bare koh-amar shape, and where the earlier occurrence is invoked, name the tsevaot-plus-Elohei-Yisrael stack as the distinct object it is. P10-011.grounds: Two of the three arms stand; the framing that the mark is disclosed without direction does not. The juncture is as described: oshb:Jer.29.9 closes verse-finally on נְאֻם יְהוָֽה and oshb:Jer.29.10 opens כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier for each), so a closure formula does stand immediately before a fresh onset at exactly the seam the row rejects, while the stated ground answers only frame owner and addressee. On that same ruled reading the convergence does not cut: the closure corroborates only where a fresh qualifying onset follows, and a koh-amar carrying no frame-owner change and no fresh addressee is not one - which is why this is a disclosure defect and not a boundary error, and both of those negative findings are byte-true as the row states them. Tests: the corrected rejection must survive a byte read of oshb:Jer.29.9 and oshb:Jer.29.10 - no ground that passes over a verse-final closure standing immediately before a fresh onset - and every formula digit must name the object swept.

P10-013.challenge_claim: First item: the discourse-imperative summons one verse before the front seam is a stronger, undisclosed rival for this unit's opening. Second item: the koh-amar the seam rests on is never quoted in the original language, its mouth and written medium are unnamed, a single-site name-form change inside the span is undisclosed, and a paseq seg in the span is undisclosed.
P10-013.grounds: The two items are distinct and both stand. Rival onset: oshb:Jer.29.20 opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier), the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles - a recurring book-wide shape (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier) standing immediately after a doubled verse-final closure formula at 29:19 and followed at once by the oracle this unit carries - while the disclosed alternative weighs only whether the curse formula of verse 22 should split from verse 21, and never whether that summons belongs forward as this unit's opening. The comparison to the summons cited from elsewhere in the book holds as a class parallel and not as a byte recurrence: the two needles differ at skeleton tier. Evidence mechanics: oshb:Jer.29.21 opens כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (byte tier) verse-initially, and the row's own pointed run begins after it at אֶל אַחְאָ֤ב בֶּן קֽוֹלָיָה֙, so the device carrying the seam is quoted in the other witness alone, against the standing requirement that a boundary-relevant original-language claim be spliced with its tier named. Ownership and medium are unnamed in the one stretch where formulas stand inside a quoted letter and, one chapter earlier, in a false prophet's mouth; the field's signal keys carry the speech formula alone with no letter-frame key, although the units at 29:4-29:14 and at 29:24-29:29 both declare that frame for the same document. The name-form change is byte-real and load-bearing on the row's own rejection: the fuller spelling אַחְאָ֤ב stands at 29:21 and the shorter base וּכְאֶחָ֔ב one verse later at 29:22 (byte tier; skeleton sweeps, finals-normalized: 1 verse each, book-wide), so the sentence binding verse 22 back to verse 21 by name rests on two different attested spellings without saying so. One paseq seg stands at MT 29:21 inside the span, undisclosed, while both parashah marks and the ketiv/qere and exegesis note at MT 29:23 are disclosed. What verifies: the resh-family royal spelling at 29:21 and its contrast with the nun-family forms at 29:1 and 29:3 are byte-true, and both setumah citations match the inventory under their types.
P10-013.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the pointed formula at 29:21 with its tier at the site where the seam is argued; name whose mouth carries it and the written medium it stands inside; and disclose both attested spellings of the name at 29:21 and 29:22 with a per-spelling digit, since the rejection turns on the two names. observed_substrate_signals: add the letter-frame key already carried by the units at 29:4-29:14 and 29:24-29:29. device_notes: add the MT 29:21 paseq seg (single-witness, count-only). strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh the summons at 29:20 as the rival onset. P10-014.grounds: All three arms verify, and a fourth defect of the same family stands beside them. Governing formula: oshb:Jer.29.25 opens כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (byte tier) verse-initially, inside the span, a member of the koh-amar-headed full-stack object (sweep: 31 verses book-wide, skeleton tier; inside chapters 27 through 29 it stands at 27:4, 27:21, 28:2, 28:14, 29:4, 29:8, 29:21 and 29:25), and it governs the quoted rival material at 29:26-29:28; the field carries no speech-formula signal at all and never quotes the formula, so ownership runs divine formula over embedded letter and the one question this stretch turns on is left unanswered. Medium: 29:25 charges the sending of סְפָרִ֗ים, a plural, while 29:29 reports הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה (byte tier for each), one document, and the account uses a single letter throughout - a precision defect rather than a structural one. Front seam: 29:24 opens וְאֶל (byte tier), a conjunctive form binding this address to the one just closed and standing exactly on this unit's own front seam, undisclosed, while the English paired with it carries no conjunction at all - a byte-true continuity signal that argues against the cut unless disclosed. What verifies: the setumah at MT 29:23 and the petuchah at MT 29:29 match the inventory under their types; no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span; the defective gentilic at 29:27 is the spelling the bytes carry; and all three English quotations are verbatim against the staged text.
P10-014.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the pointed formula at 29:25 with its tier, name it as the divine formula governing the quoted letter at 29:26-29:28, and add the matching speech-formula key to observed_substrate_signals. Correct the medium to the plural the bytes carry at 29:25, keeping the singular only where 29:29 warrants it. Disclose the conjunctive opening at 29:24 on the front seam and state why it does not carry continuity against the cut. Re-cut the 29:27 pairing so that gloss extent equals splice extent. Tests: every span-internal tier-1 formula must be quoted at byte tier and keyed; the cross-seam device at the front seam must be disclosed; and gloss extent must equal splice extent at every paired site - the test that killed the original.

P10-015.challenge_claim: The verdict quotation at Jer.29.32 is glossed in English beyond the extent of the Hebrew it cites: the row splices only the opening clause of the verse yet pairs that splice with a three-clause English quotation.
P10-015.grounds: Defect real, framing and severity corrected. P11-001.challenge_claim: The stated warrant that nothing between the header and the closing rubric reopens the address with a new addressee or a discourse imperative is contradicted by Jer.30.2, which the row quotes itself.
P11-001.grounds: Half the challenge holds on the bytes, half does not. MT 30:2 carries כְּתָב לְךָ֗ and דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte for each) — a command form with an explicit second-person singular addressee marker, read as an imperative in the other witness, “Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.” (web:Jer.30.2) — while MT 30:1 carries no second-person form at all. An unqualified denial that any discourse imperative stands between the header and the rubric therefore cannot survive a form standing inside the row's own splice, and that arm of the warrant sentence is defective. The other arm is not contradicted and the challenge does not separate them: the addressee at 30:2 is the figure the header itself names, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), so nothing NEW is addressed — the address is specified, not reopened — and the messenger formula at 30:2 carries no frame-owner change, the mouth being the same throughout. Under the ruled internal-seam classes a commissioning write-command inside a superscription is not the audience-summoning discourse frame that cuts, so the seam stands, as the challenge itself concedes. One further check the challenge did not make: the row's narrower version of the same absence, made in strongest_rejected_alternative about the 30:3/30:4 turn, is byte-true — MT 30:4 carries no speech formula, no imperative and no second-person form (oshb:Jer.30.4, byte). Disclosures verify: SAMEKH at MT 29:32 at the front seam and PE at MT 30:3 inside the span, single-witness, tier-3 weak, and no paseq seg or ketiv/qere note in the span.
P11-001.remedy: In P11-001 boundary_rationale, replace the blanket absence sentence with one that names the class it denies and survives the bytes at 30:2: state that the imperative standing there is a commissioning write-command addressed to the same figure the header names, and that the messenger formula at 30:2 carries no frame-owner change, so neither reaches the internal-seam classes that cut. Test the cure the way the original failed: read the rewritten sentence back against each of Jer.30.1 through Jer.30.4 and confirm it denies no form that stands in the row's own splices. Span, unit_type, confidence, observed_substrate_signals and device_notes unchanged; no boundary change is ordered.

P11-002.challenge_claim: Two items, distinct defects. (i) The unit's own opening quotation, the messenger formula the row relies on as its seam warrant, is glossed in English only from partway through the Hebrew verse spliced beside it at Jer.30.5. (ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: Jer.30.8 carries the span's first second-person singular addressee, so the asserted absence of an addressee change at that turn is byte-false in both witnesses.
P11-002.grounds: Both upheld; distinct defects, one mechanical and one substantive. (i) The 30:5 pair splices the whole verse including כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte) but glosses only from the cry onward, while the staged verse opens “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5) — the formula's own English stands in the same staged verse and is left uncovered, on the single device the row cites as its opening warrant. (ii) Person marking re-derived across the span: 30:5 carries the first-person plural שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ, 30:6 the second-person plural שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ, 30:7 third person throughout, and then 30:8 carries אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק (oshb:Jer.30.5, oshb:Jer.30.6, oshb:Jer.30.8, byte for each), the span's first second-person singular marking, rendered the same way in the other witness, “that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds.” (web:Jer.30.8). A flat denial that any addressee change marks that turn is byte-false. Two calibration points that do not disturb the finding but do bear on how strong the rival is. First, that marking is sustained to the row's own close, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte) and כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י through אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte for each), so this is a turn into a sustained address rather than a one-verse anomaly. Second, the 30:8 clause mixes persons in one breath, עֻלּוֹ֙ third-person beside צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ second-person (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte for each), so the turn is a person shift inside continuous divine speech, not a clean fresh address. A precision note on the framing, not a correction to the finding: the flagged word in that sentence is a restrictive adverb and is a genuine keyword false positive on its own terms; what fails is the absence clause standing beside it. Everything else verifies: no mark at MT 30:4, SAMEKH at MT 30:9, PE at MT 30:11, one paseq seg each at MT 30:8 and MT 30:11 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere; the hoy at 30:7 is the day-alas role and not a woe onset; the Jacob spelling is defective at 30:7 and twice at 30:10 (sweep: 2 token hits at Jer.30.10, 1 prefixed at Jer.30.7, skeleton, finals-normalized) against the plene form at 30:18; and all five pointed runs and all five English runs are byte-true and verbatim respectively.
P11-002.remedy: Two work orders on P11-002. (1) boundary_rationale: extend the 30:5 gloss to cover the formula the splice already contains, “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5), or trim the splice to the cry alone. Test: the paired English and the paired Hebrew must cover the same clauses; re-collate the run at byte tier against oshb:Jer.30.5 and re-check the English verbatim against staged web:Jer.30.5. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: the sentence may no longer assert that no addressee change marks the 30:7/30:8 turn. Re-argue the rejection on grounds the bytes support — state the second-person singular entry at 30:8, weigh it against the mixed person marking inside that same clause and against the absence of any fresh speech formula there, and land the rejection on that. Test the cure the way the original failed: read the rewritten sentence back against oshb:Jer.30.7 through oshb:Jer.30.11 and confirm it denies no form standing in those verses. If the rejection cannot be re-grounded, the alternative becomes a boundary PROPOSAL — a cut at Jer.30.8 — requiring explicit owner adoption, never author work. In the same pass, disclose the second-person plural imperative pair at 30:6 or carry it in observed_substrate_signals, since the row's own rejection criteria treat imperatives as onset candidates and this one stands inside the span undeclared. If the driver changes, observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence re-open with it.

P11-003.challenge_claim: Two items. (i) Both of the row's load-bearing quotations, at its opening and at its close, gloss only part of the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them (Jer.30.12, Jer.30.17). (ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: the exclusivity-shaped claim that nothing divides the complaint from the reversal carries no sweep and is contested by the verse-initial pivot particle at Jer.30.16 inside the span.
P11-003.grounds: Item one upheld as framed; item two refined on its object. (i) The 30:12 pair splices the whole verse including כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) but glosses only from the wound complaint onward, while the staged verse opens “For Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.30.12); the 30:17 pair splices the whole verse including כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.30.17, byte) but glosses only the outcast clause, leaving “For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” (web:Jer.30.17) uncovered. Both are real, and the 30:17 gap is load-bearing twice: the healing clause is the content the row's own close rests on AND the content its rejection of the judgment reading rests on, and both lenses reached that verse independently. (ii) The object is mis-anchored. The digits reproduce exactly on an independent re-sweep of the consonantal skeleton — the token stands in 55 verses book-wide and verse-initially in exactly 2 across MT chs 29-31, MT 29:32 and MT 30:16 (sweep: 2 verses, verse-initial, finals-normalized) — and לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Jer.30.16, byte) does stand verse-initially at the joint. But the sentence challenged denies a fresh FORMULA, and this token is a discourse particle, not a member of any formula class: inside MT 30:12-30:17 the messenger formula stands only at 30:12 and the closure formula only at 30:17, with nothing at 30:13-30:16 (sweep: 1 verse each, span-scoped). On its own object the sentence is byte-true and is not refuted; and a six-verse span-scoped absence readable directly off the bytes is not the exclusivity class that must carry a book-wide digit. What survives is narrower and still a defect: the sentence names no swept object before asserting the absence, and the pivot particle at 30:16 is a byte-true hinge sitting at the exact joint the rejection concerns and goes undisclosed. A byte fact neither reading drew: because that particle turns the announcement at 30:16 rather than at 30:17, it argues the reversal begins one verse earlier than the rejected complaint-only grouping of 30:12-30:16 assumes, so it tells against that alternative rather than for it. Disclosures verify: PE at MT 30:11 at the front seam, SAMEKH at MT 30:17 at the close, one paseq seg at MT 30:15 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere in the span; the feminine-singular onset marking at אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) is byte-real.
P11-003.remedy: Two work orders on P11-003. (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the 30:12 and 30:17 pairs so gloss extent equals splice extent — the 30:17 pair must cover “For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” (web:Jer.30.17), the healing clause its own argument rests on. Test: each paired English run and its paired Hebrew run cover the same clauses; re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.30.12 and oshb:Jer.30.17 and re-check both English runs verbatim against the staged web: verses. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: name the swept object before the absence — state which formula classes were swept across Jer.30.13 through Jer.30.16 and with what digit and unit — and disclose the verse-initial pivot particle at 30:16, including that the announcement turns there. Test the cure the way the original failed: the rewritten sentence must name its swept object and unit, and must deny no device standing anywhere in Jer.30.12 through Jer.30.17 when read back against those six verses. No boundary change is ordered: span, unit_type and confidence stand.

P11-004.challenge_claim: Two items. (i) The row's opening quotation and its quotation of the actively-held closing verse each gloss only part of the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them (Jer.30.18, Jer.31.1). (ii) The covenant formula at Jer.30.22 arrives on a second-person switch the row explicitly denies; the wrath coda at Jer.30.23-Jer.30.24 is an undisclosed near-twin of Jer.23.19-Jer.23.20; and the spelling contrast the row argues rests on two verses outside its own span that its evidence list does not carry.
P11-004.grounds: Both upheld as distinct defects, and the recurrence arm is understated. (i) The 30:18 pair splices the whole verse including כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte) and glosses only from the reversal onward, while the staged verse opens “Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.18); the 31:1 pair splices the whole verse including בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.31.1, byte) and glosses only the covenant clause, leaving “At that time,” says Yahweh, (web:Jer.31.1) uncovered — on the one verse the row holds open, where that temporal phrase is half of its own stated reason for holding it. (ii) Person marking: MT 30:18-30:21 is third person throughout, אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte) and אַדִּיר֜וֹ closing at נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.30.21, byte for each), and 30:22 opens וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם with וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים following (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte), the span's first second-person forms, rendered the same way in the other witness, “You shall be my people, and I will be your God.” (web:Jer.30.22). The flat denial of any addressee change is byte-false. (iii) The coda recurrence verifies and is stronger than claimed: the opening run הִנֵּ֣ה סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה and the closing run עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte for each), together with the run עַד עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), each stand in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses each, skeleton, finals-normalized), and against oshb:Jer.23.19 and oshb:Jer.23.20 all three are identical at BYTE tier, accents included, not merely consonantally; the divergences are סַ֖עַר מִתְגּוֹרֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte) against וְסַ֖עַר מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.23.19, byte), the added חֲרוֹן֙ and the pointing of בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte for each), and one extra closing word at MT 23:20. A byte-tier recurrence of that extent is texture and never a boundary driver, but it is a disclosure object and the row is silent on it. (iv) The prose argues verse 10 and verse 7, resolving to Jer.30.10 and Jer.30.7, from outside the span Jer.30.18-Jer.31.1, and neither stands in boundary_evidence_refs; the spelling substance is right — plene אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte) against the defective form twice at 30:10 and, prefixed, once at 30:7 (sweep: 2 token hits at Jer.30.10 and 1 prefixed hit at Jer.30.7, skeleton, finals-normalized) — so this is a mirroring omission, not a false claim. Two byte facts neither reading drew. The coda names the divine name in the third person twice, הִנֵּ֣ה סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte) and לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב חֲרוֹן֙ אַף יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), immediately after the first-person clause וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte) at 30:22, so 'still the same speaker' is an undisclosed shift as well as an untiered form claim — the audience does stay second-person plural, so only the speaker arm fails. And the held-open close inverts the covenant formula and flips its person: וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ לִ֥י לְעָֽם at oshb:Jer.31.1 (byte) against וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם at oshb:Jer.30.22 (byte), third-person plural where 30:22 is second-person plural, which bears directly on the seam the row holds open and is undisclosed. Disclosures otherwise verify: SAMEKH at MT 30:17, MT 30:22 and MT 31:1, one paseq seg each at MT 30:18 and MT 30:23 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere in the span.

(3) device_notes: disclose the coda recurrence with its object, unit, digit and tier all named — byte-tier identity of the three runs against Jer.23.19-Jer.23.20, exactly 2 verses each book-wide, with the four divergence points listed — and label it texture, never a boundary driver; in the same pass disclose the third-person naming of the divine name at 30:23-30:24 beside the first-person clause at 30:22, and the person flip between 30:22 and 31:1. Test: every recurrence claim carries the tier it was verified at, and every disclosure names its swept object and unit before its digit. (4) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.30.7 and oshb:Jer.30.10, the two out-of-span verses the spelling contrast argues from, or drop the contrast from both boundary_rationale and device_notes. Test: every verse argued outside Jer.30.18-Jer.31.1, including bare 'verse N' mentions resolved against the span chapter, resolves to an entry in the list. P11-005.challenge_claim: Two items. (i) Both of the unit's first two verses are glossed in English only from partway through the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them (Jer.31.2, Jer.31.3). (ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: Jer.31.2 has no addressee at all and Jer.31.3 both reports the deity in the third person and opens a feminine-singular address, so the asserted single continuous voice addressed to one figure is byte-false.
P11-005.grounds: Both upheld, and they interlock rather than duplicate. (i) The 31:2 pair splices the whole verse including כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte) and glosses only from the wilderness clause onward, while the staged verse opens “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.31.2) — again the uncovered element is the unit's own opening seam device. The 31:3 pair splices the whole verse including מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte) and glosses only from the love clause onward, leaving “Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying,” (web:Jer.31.3) uncovered. (ii) MT 31:2 carries no second-person form anywhere: מָצָ֥א and הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte for each) are third person throughout, so there is no addressed figure at 31:2 for 31:3 to keep addressing. MT 31:3 then opens by naming the divine name in the third person beside a first-person singular pronoun, מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte), read the same way in the other witness, and only after that clause do the feminine-singular forms אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ and מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte for each) begin. The asserted single continuous voice addressed to the same figure fails on both halves. The consistency point holds too: the same feminine-singular pointing that carries an onset warrant at אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) is refused that weight here, one device read two ways within six verses. The two items interlock: the clause the quotation leaves uncovered at 31:3 is precisely the clause that falsifies the rejection sentence, so curing the pairing surfaces the evidence against the row's own stated ground. Disclosures verify: SAMEKH at MT 31:1 at the front seam, PE at MT 31:6 at the close, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in the span; the 31:4 and 31:6 pairs are extent-clean, and all four pointed runs are byte-true with all four English runs verbatim.

(2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the continuity assertion with the bytes — no second-person form stands in 31:2, and 31:3 opens a third-person report of the divine name with a first-person singular pronoun before the feminine-singular address begins — then re-argue the rejection on a ground that survives them. P11-006.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Front seam: the opening verse reads כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte) - the messenger formula stands second, behind the particle כִּי (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte), and the same particle opens the verse immediately before the seam, כִּ֣י יֶשׁ י֔וֹם (oshb:Jer.31.6, byte), and the ground-clause inside the span, כִּֽי פָדָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.31.11, byte). The particle-prefixed formula shape is unremarkable in itself (sweep: 29 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys), so the defect is not the shape: it is that a particle binding the span's own opening verse back to what precedes goes unnamed at the seam, while the same particle one verse later is the load-bearing ground for refusing the internal cut. A byte-true device straddling a span's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed. Rejected-alternative ground, refuted: the declined verse opens שִׁמְע֤וּ דְבַר יְהוָה֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.10, byte) - second-person-plural imperatives with an explicit vocative - after two verses of divine first-person report about a third-person group, הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אוֹתָ֜ם (oshb:Jer.31.8, byte) and וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא (oshb:Jer.31.9, byte). At the span's own opening the same noun stands inside a prepositional phrase, בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte), as setting rather than as addressee. The declared heuristic entry carrying that sentence does not survive re-derivation. Second ground, under-reaching: a forward bind to the ground-clause attaches the declined verse to the verse after it, both inside the span, so it bears on nothing at the seam between oshb:Jer.31.9 and oshb:Jer.31.10. Tier-3: a setumah is recorded at oshb:Jer.31.9 (single-witness, weak corroboration in the Prophets, never a driver, absence never counterevidence) - it falls at exactly the declined seam, is disclosed as a mark, and is never connected to the seam it weakly corroborates. Quote-gloss parity: both cited pairs are byte-verbatim against the staged folded text, but the renderings cover 89 and 88 percent of whole-verse splices, dropping precisely the head that renders the particle-plus-formula the onset rests on and the tail that renders the closure formula the signal list claims. Verified in the row's favour: every mark disclosure is exact (petuchah at the front-seam verse, setumah inside the span and at the closing verse, one paseq seg at the opening verse, count-only, single-witness), and the wine-lexeme distinction is byte-true - the attested defective spelling stands in 1 verse book-wide, the plene spelling in 0, against 11 verses for the other wine noun - though the claim ships with neither digit.

The replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original: read back against oshb:Jer.31.10's own bytes it must not deny a vocative addressee there, and it must state the tier-3 setumah recorded at oshb:Jer.31.9 as weak single-witness corroboration standing at the declined seam. boundary_rationale: name the subordinating particle standing before the messenger formula at the span's own opening verse and disclose it as continuity across the front seam, the same particle the row treats as load-bearing one verse later. boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.7 and web:Jer.31.14 to the extent of their splices, so that the head rendering the particle-plus-formula and the tail rendering the closure formula both appear beside the Hebrew they gloss. device_notes: give the wine-lexeme sentence its digits, naming the swept object and unit (attested spelling, verse counts).

P11-007.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. The back-seam statement is byte-false: the name stands in 7 verses book-wide (sweep: 7 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys), two of them earlier in this same chapter - בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Jer.31.6, byte) and וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא (oshb:Jer.31.9, byte) - and the second sits inside the span closing at oshb:Jer.31.14, whose own whole-verse splice carries it and whose own prose names the figure. 'Introduced by name' cannot stand as written. The rejected alternative negates its own premise: it concedes a verse-initial messenger formula in second-person address at oshb:Jer.31.16 against third-person report at oshb:Jer.31.15, then decides on the ground that no addressee or topic shift marks the turn. The bytes carry the shift - כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה stands verse-initially and is followed by מִנְעִ֤י קוֹלֵךְ֙ מִבֶּ֔כִי וְעֵינַ֖יִךְ (oshb:Jer.31.16, byte), second feminine singular, where the preceding verse reports רָחֵ֖ל מְבַכָּ֣ה עַל בָּנֶ֑יהָ (oshb:Jer.31.15, byte) in the third person. A setumah recorded at oshb:Jer.31.15 falls at that same seam (single-witness, tier-3 weak). The hold itself survives on a ground the row does not state: the frame owner does not change across that seam - the divine mouth carries the formula at both verses, with no quoted-prophet or letter-embedded formula anywhere in reach - so a messenger-formula onset alone is not a licensed internal cut under the ruled seam classes, and the second-person answer answers the complaint just reported. The two refuted statements are the row's stated warrant and stated ground, not the only grounds available; the cure is re-grounding, and any change to the seam itself would be a proposal for owner adoption, never author work. Exclusivity discipline: the single-site claim is true on re-run (sweep: 1 verse book-wide, consonantal tier, MT keys) and the boundary sentence carries its digit, but the disclosure sentence repeats the exclusivity with no digit in that sentence; a scope or tier label never carries an exclusivity claim. Quote-gloss parity: three whole-verse splices paired with renderings at 92, 54 and 33 percent; the two short pairs drop the closure formulas the splices carry and the return-clauses the row's own prose narrates in its own words. Verified in the row's favour: the mark and seg disclosures are exact (setumah at the front-seam verse, at the opening verse and at the closing verse; one paseq seg at each of two verses, count-only, single-witness), and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.
P11-007.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'A new figure, Ephraim, is introduced by name at verse 18' - the name stands in 7 verses book-wide, two of them earlier in this chapter and one inside the span closing at oshb:Jer.31.14 - and restate the back seam on the byte-true change, the divine promise giving way to the figure's own quoted speech inside a hearing-report. The replacement must pass the test that killed the original: a book-wide sweep of the attested spellings must not contradict the sentence. strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the ground that no addressee or topic shift marks the turn; it is refuted by the second-feminine-singular address at oshb:Jer.31.16 against third-person report at oshb:Jer.31.15. The replacement must not deny the person switch the bytes carry - ground the hold instead on unchanged frame ownership across the seam and on the answer-to-complaint relation, and disclose the tier-3 setumah standing at that seam. device_notes: put the sweep digit inside the exclusivity sentence itself (verse count, book-wide, named object). boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.15, web:Jer.31.16 and web:Jer.31.17 to the extent of their splices.

P11-008.challenge_claim: A pointed catchword straddles this unit's own back seam undisclosed, the opening description misplaces the speaker of the first half-verse, and the verse-final closure formula the unit splices is left unengaged.
P11-008.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Cross-seam cohesion: שׁוּבִי֙ stands inside the span at oshb:Jer.31.19 and שׁ֚וּבִי immediately across the back seam at oshb:Jer.31.21 (byte at each); the two coincide once accents are stripped (sweep: 3 verses, accent-stripped tier, MT keys - oshb:Jer.31.19, oshb:Jer.31.21, oshb:Jer.31.23; 4 verses at consonantal tier). The root carries no single needle in this book, so only the attested forms are counted here and no root-level digit is asserted. Opening description: the verse opens on the divine first-person hearing-report שָׁמ֣וֹעַ שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי and names the figure in the third person before any quoted speech (oshb:Jer.31.18, byte); both witnesses frame it so. Correction to the challenge's own digit: the quoted speech begins at the FIFTH word, יִסַּרְתַּ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.31.18, byte), not the fourth. The row's next clause supplies the correct frame, so the defect is the ordering of the opening sentence rather than a missing frame. Back edge: the span closes on a verse-final נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.31.20, byte), a formula standing in 162 verses book-wide (sweep: 162 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys). The splice carries it, the paired rendering drops it at 93 percent coverage, and neither the signal list nor the prose records it - the strongest available back-edge corroboration, unengaged, at a seam where a discourse-imperative cluster follows, which is exactly the condition under which such a formula corroborates closure. Verified in the row's favour: the type deviation is disclosed as required; the setumah pair at the front-seam verse and the closing verse is exact (single-witness, tier-3 weak); the inventory records no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note inside the span; the declared entry that only the closing verse answers is confirmed on the bytes.

P11-009.challenge_claim: The seam evidence is under-named - the person and gender switch that actually marks the front seam is not stated as such - and two byte-true recurrences straddle both seams undisclosed, one of them qualifying the back-seam framing.
P11-009.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Front seam: the preceding verse speaks of the figure in the third masculine singular, זָכֹ֥ר אֶזְכְּרֶ֖נּוּ and רַחֵ֥ם אֲֽרַחֲמֶ֖נּוּ (oshb:Jer.31.20, byte), while the span's opening verse turns to second feminine singular address, הַצִּ֧יבִי לָ֣ךְ צִיֻּנִ֗ים and בְּתוּלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.31.21, byte); both witnesses render the switch. The signal list records only a discourse-imperative cluster. Partial correction to the challenge: the row's prose does name the addressee, so the switch is present in substance and missing from the typed signal record and from the seam argument as such, rather than absent from the row altogether. Cross-seam cohesion, front: the pointed form at oshb:Jer.31.21 continues the form standing at oshb:Jer.31.19 (sweep: 3 verses, accent-stripped tier, MT keys), undisclosed. Back: the span's closing address ends עָרַ֥יִךְ אֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Jer.31.21, byte) and the noun returns at once as וּבְעָרָ֔יו (oshb:Jer.31.23, byte) and וְכָל עָרָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.31.24, byte), while בְּשׁוּבִ֖י (oshb:Jer.31.23, byte) carries the same verbal root across the same seam. Neither hook is disclosed, and a byte-true device straddling the span's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed. Noted, not charged: תַּמְרוּרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.31.21, byte) and תַמְרוּרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.31.15, byte) are a same-skeleton pair under different pointing and different sense (sweep: 3 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys). It stands in the neighbourhood, not across this span's own seam, and carries no boundary weight. Calibration: the frontier consideration is recorded as not taken here while it is recorded as taken at the neighbouring spans, at a seam that carries no word-event header of any of the book's three shapes; the honestly held clause at the closing verse is a content question and does not answer that point. Verified in the row's favour: the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.31.21 is real, single, sits mid-verse on the going-verb, and is disclosed rather than resolved (single-witness); the setumah pair is exact; no paseq seg falls in the span; the declared entry about the closing verse is confirmed - the same second-feminine-singular addressee continues under a fresh epithet with no speech formula.
P11-009.remedy: observed_substrate_signals and boundary_rationale: record the person-and-gender switch at the front seam as the seam's evidence - third masculine singular reference to the figure at oshb:Jer.31.20 giving way to second feminine singular address at oshb:Jer.31.21 - not the imperative cluster alone. device_notes: disclose both cross-seam recurrences with their forms and tiers named: the shared form across the front seam (accent-stripped tier, 3 verses) and the cities noun plus the same verbal root across the back seam. frontier_flag_considered: re-examine the setting, given a seam carrying no word-event header inside the poetry-prose alternation where the neighbouring spans record the consideration as taken. P11-010.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. P11-012.challenge_claim: One item: the back boundary is argued only from a recurring days-are-coming incipit absent from the book's tier-1 seam catalog, and the unit's own test for declining a cut at verse 29 applies just as directly to verse 31 without being engaged. The other item: the stated ground for holding verses 29-30 with verses 27-28 is byte-false because the divine first-person voice does not continue past verse 28, and the front-seam device is a widely recurring shape carried without a digit and with a third chapter-internal site undisclosed.
P11-012.grounds: The two items are distinct in target - one goes to the back-seam warrant and to consistency with the declined internal cut, the other to the rejected alternative's stated ground and to the front-seam device's digit - but they converge on one underlying defect: the row's description of the voice pattern across oshb:Jer.31.27 to oshb:Jer.31.31. Upheld: the rejected alternative's ground is byte-false. The first two verses of the span carry divine first-person forms - וְזָרַעְתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.27, byte), שָׁקַ֣דְתִּי and אֶשְׁקֹ֧ד (oshb:Jer.31.28, byte) - while the last two carry none: לֹא יֹאמְר֣וּ ע֔וֹד (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte) and אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנ֖וֹ יָמ֑וּת ... תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו (oshb:Jer.31.30, byte) are third-person throughout, and both witnesses render them so. Upheld: the front-seam device is typed a refrain and ships with no digit; the shape stands in 15 verses book-wide at the consonantal tier and 5 at byte tier (MT keys), three of them in this chapter - oshb:Jer.31.27, oshb:Jer.31.31 and oshb:Jer.31.38 - and the third site is undisclosed. Recurrence at that density does not by itself found a unit. Upheld: quote-gloss parity. All four splices are whole verses and byte-verbatim, but the renderings cover 15, 93, 67 and 100 percent; the 67 percent pair drops the head that renders בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte), the very clause the rejected alternative is about, and the 15 percent pair leaves a sixteen-word splice glossed by four rendered words. Refined: the back-seam framing does not survive re-derivation. The seam is under-STATED, not under-warranted - the third-person proverb material gives way to divine first person at וְכָרַתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.31, byte), a person shift absent at the internal seam the row declines. The parity argument asserts that the same first-person divine voice stands on both sides of the back seam; the bytes refute that in exactly the way the row's own sentence is refuted, so that argument reproduces the defect it is charging. Also refined: the incipit's absence from the enumerated internal-cut classes is real, but the back seam does not rest on the incipit alone once the bytes are read, and a byte-true ground for holding the proverb material with what precedes is available and unused - the declined verse opens בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte), anaphoric to the days named at the span's own opening verse. Verified in the row's favour: the incipit is verse-initial and byte-exact at oshb:Jer.31.27; the setumah pair at the front-seam verse and the closing verse is exact (single-witness, tier-3 weak); the inventory records no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note inside the span; the proverb material is engaged from the bytes with no cross-tradition appeal.
P11-012.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the ground that the same first-person voice continues, which is byte-false at oshb:Jer.31.29 and oshb:Jer.31.30. The replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original - a first-person form check across all four verses of the span - and the byte-true ground available is the anaphoric days-clause opening the declined verse, which binds it back to the span's own opening. boundary_rationale: state the back seam's actual byte warrant, the third-person proverb material giving way to divine first person at oshb:Jer.31.31, instead of resting the edge on the incipit alone. boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals: give the incipit claim its digit and unit (verse counts, tier named) and disclose the third chapter-internal site at oshb:Jer.31.38. boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.27, web:Jer.31.29 and web:Jer.31.31 to the extent of their splices. Whether the seam at oshb:Jer.31.29 should be cut is a boundary proposal for owner adoption, not author work.

P11-013.challenge_claim: One item: the front boundary is warranted only by the same recurring incipit, yet the disclosure describes both edges as carrying unusually strong tier-1 warrant and the batch's only high confidence rating rests on that asymmetry. The other item: the high rating rests on a positional closure claim the bytes refute - the closure formula at verse 34 stands mid-verse with two clauses after it, stands in every verse of the span, and is separated from the following onset by a verse boundary.
P11-013.grounds: The two items are the same defect approached from opposite edges: both target the disclosure sentence claiming unusually strong tier-1 warrant at both edges, and the high rating resting on it. Upheld: the positional closure claim is byte-false. At the span's closing verse the formula נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה stands at words 21-22 of 29 and is followed inside the same verse by כִּ֤י אֶסְלַח֙ לַֽעֲוֺנָ֔ם וּלְחַטָּאתָ֖ם לֹ֥א אֶזְכָּר עֽוֹד (oshb:Jer.31.34, byte); a verse boundary then separates it from כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.31.35, byte, verse-initial). Nothing is immediate about it. Upheld: the formula does not discriminate this edge. It stands in all four verses of the span, and the one verse-final occurrence inside the span sits in the middle of it at oshb:Jer.31.32; it stands in 14 of this chapter's 40 verses and in 162 verses book-wide. Correction to that digit's tier label: 14 is a consonantal-tier verse count aggregating three distinct pointed forms (5, 5 and 4 verses at byte tier), not a byte-tier count. Upheld: the unusually-strong characterisation is unsupported at both edges, and the only high rating in this material rests on it. The front edge's stated driver is the incipit, which stands at 15 verses book-wide at the consonantal tier. Refined: the front edge is not warrantless. The third-person proverb material gives way to divine first person at וְכָרַתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.31, byte) - a person shift the row never states because its neighbouring sentence asserts the opposite. Read correctly, both edges carry real byte warrant and the closure corroboration is genuinely available under the ruled reading, since a fresh tier-1 onset does follow at the next verse; what fails is the characterisation and the rating, not the seams. Refuted: the sub-arm that the rejected alternative reverses what its verse does. The span carries לֹ֣א כַבְּרִ֗ית (oshb:Jer.31.32, byte) answered by כִּ֣י זֹ֣את הַבְּרִ֡ית (oshb:Jer.31.33, byte) - a not-this-but-this construction whose second half completes the contrast the first half opens - so describing the later verse as continuing that contrast is byte-supportable, and the declared entry there is otherwise confirmed. Verified in the row's favour: the incipit is verse-initial and byte-exact at oshb:Jer.31.31; the covenant noun chain holds the four verses together; the setumah pair at the front-seam verse and the closing verse is exact (single-witness, tier-3 weak); no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls inside the span; all four splices are whole verses and byte-verbatim, with renderings at 69, 94, 56 and 29 percent.
P11-013.remedy: device_notes: replace the sentence claiming unusually strong tier-1 warrant at both edges. State the back edge as the bytes carry it - the closure formula standing mid-verse in the span's closing verse, with a fresh verse-initial messenger formula at the next verse, and the same formula standing in all four verses of the span, so it corroborates rather than discriminates - and state the front edge's actual warrant, the third-person proverb material giving way to divine first person at oshb:Jer.31.31. confidence: lower from high to the rating the restated warrants support, since the high rating rests on the withdrawn characterisation. boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.31, web:Jer.31.33 and web:Jer.31.34 to the extent of their splices - the closing pair currently displays only the material standing after the closure formula. P11-014.challenge_claim: One item: this unit's own onset is warranted only by a bare koh-amar recurrence, the same kind of signal its own rejected alternative treats as insufficient to justify a second cut one verse later. The other item: the terminal boundary warrant leans on a verse whose ketiv/qere note the unit nowhere discloses, and two of its three whole-verse splices are paired with renderings covering only part of the spliced run.
P11-014.grounds: The two items are distinct: one goes to the onset warrant, the other to mark disclosure and quote-gloss parity. Refuted, with the refuting bytes: the two onsets are not the same signal. At the span's own front seam the messenger formula stands where the preceding unit carries none in any of its four verses, and it introduces a different oracle shape - a participial creation epithet closing on the divine name-signature יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.31.35, byte). At the declined internal seam the formula recurs inside a matched pair: אִם יָמֻ֜שׁוּ ... גַּם֩ זֶ֨רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל (oshb:Jer.31.36, byte) against אִם יִמַּ֤דּוּ ... גַּם אֲנִ֞י אֶמְאַ֨ס בְּכָל זֶ֧רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל (oshb:Jer.31.37, byte) - the same protasis-apodosis shape on the same subject. Verified in the row's favour: both onsets are verse-initial and byte-exact; every parashah and seg disclosure matches the inventory exactly (setumah at the front-seam verse, inside the span and at the closing verse; one paseq seg at each of two verses, count-only).

P11-015.challenge_claim: The span's own close at Jer.31.40 never states a warrant for stopping there, leaving that shared boundary disclosed only from the far side, while the front seam is fully warranted by contrast.

The span itself is not in dispute: identity numbering throughout, no contact with the book's renumbering zone or its non-Hebrew verse, and all of the unit's pointed splices re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.31.38, oshb:Jer.31.39 and oshb:Jer.31.40.
P11-015.remedy: boundary_rationale: add one closing sentence naming the tier-1 device that ends the span, the prose-sermon superscription heading Jer.32.1, a member of the eleven-verse superscription-shape object, with its header-internal regnal date; and state that the setumah already disclosed in device_notes is tier-3 corroboration only, not the bound. boundary_evidence_refs: add the out-of-span verse argued by that new sentence (Jer.32.1) so every verse argued in prose outside the span is carried in the field. boundary_rationale: attach a digit-bearing sweep to the opening-incipit claim, naming the swept object, the unit and the tier (skeleton 15 verses, byte 5 verses, MT keys), and name the two chapter-internal recurrences at Jer.31.27 and Jer.31.31. P12-002.challenge_claim: A digit-bearing naming claim about the scribe is contradicted by the bytes; the opening splice is described as a voice its own first words do not carry and is glossed by two words of a seven-word run; and the confidence sits above what the seam's signals support.
P12-002.grounds: All three limbs verify on bytes. Naming digit: a token-bound verse sweep of the attested pointed spelling בָּר֣וּךְ (oshb:Jer.32.12, byte) returns exactly two verses inside Jer.32.6-Jer.32.15, oshb:Jer.32.12 and בָּר֔וּךְ (oshb:Jer.32.13, byte). The first-person element the sentence argues from, אֵלַ֥י (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte), stands in the unglossed tail הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte), so the unit's own stated warrant never surfaces in the English half of the pair. Calibration: the onset is a member of none of the three word-event objects, since the twenty-one-verse vayehi list, the eleven-verse superscription list and the four-verse topical-header list all exclude it, and the chapter carries exactly two word-event verses (Jer.32.1 and Jer.32.26). The seam rests on a person shift out of narration plus a davar clause standing outside every inventoried frame object, with tier-3 petuchah at oshb:Jer.32.5 and oshb:Jer.32.15 as its only corroboration (single-witness). Across the eight units of this cluster the confidence set is 7 medium and 1 high, and that single high rating sits on the thinnest inventoried warrant of the set. New finding, raised by neither item: a paseq falls at oshb:Jer.32.8, inside the span and in the very verse the unit splices and discusses, and no field of the unit discloses it (seg layer, count-only, single-witness), so the span-relevant mark and seg set is incomplete.
P12-002.remedy: device_notes: replace the three-times naming sentence with the byte-true count, the scribe's name standing in exactly two verses of this span, Jer.32.12 and Jer.32.13; name the attested pointed spelling and the swept unit, drop the by-implication third site, and note that the chapter's remaining site stands at Jer.32.16 outside the span. boundary_rationale: re-cut the quote-gloss pair at Jer.32.6 so the rendering covers the whole spliced run including the first-person word-event clause, or shorten the splice to the run the rendering actually covers; the first-person element is the stated warrant and must stand on both sides of the pair. device_notes: disclose the span-relevant paseq at Jer.32.8 (seg layer, count-only, single-witness), completing the mark and seg set for the span. confidence: lower to medium unless a further tier-1 class is stated for the onset, and disclose in device_notes that the opening formula stands outside all three inventoried word-event objects. Tests the cure must pass: the corrected digit must survive a token-bound verse sweep of the named pointed spelling restricted to the span; the rendering must cover the full spliced run on read-back; the span's mark, seg and note set must be complete against the inventory; and the confidence must name the tier-1 class carrying it.

P12-004.challenge_claim: One item holds that the internal cut at Jer.32.36 splits a single unchanged-speaker reply opening at Jer.32.26 and that the Hebrew of Jer.32.35 is quoted in the boundary field with no ketiv/qere note beside it; the other holds that the closing sentence attributes the high places to Molech against the construct chain it splices and against its own rendering, and that the same field slices a ketiv/qere verse with no note disclosed in it.
P12-004.grounds: The two note-placement items are ONE defect reached from two directions; the boundary attack and the misattribution are DISTINCT. Misattribution UPHELD: the spliced chain reads בָּמ֨וֹת הַבַּ֜עַל (oshb:Jer.32.35, byte), the high places of the Baal, and the splice stops at the verse's ninth token; לַמֹּלֶךְ֒ (oshb:Jer.32.35, byte) is the fourteenth token of twenty-nine and stands outside the splice. The prose calls them the high places built for Molech, so sentence, splice and rendering disagree on read-back. New finding on the mechanism: the paired rendering runs on through that fourteenth token, so gloss extent EXCEEDS splice extent here, and the English half carries the name the Hebrew half does not, which is where the misattribution enters. Note placement UPHELD as one defect: the ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Jer.32.35 is disclosed only in device_notes while the slice is taken in boundary_rationale. The slice is verse-initial and the pair is verse-final at tokens 26 and 27 of 29, so no counting hazard materialised, but in the book's largest note inventory the disclosure belongs where the slicing happens. The span-relevant paseq at oshb:Jer.32.35 is disclosed in no field although the unit owns that verse (seg layer, count-only, single-witness). The second-person plural pronoun אַתֶּ֣ם (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte) makes its first appearance in the reply there; a pointed scan of MT 32:26-32:35 returns 0 second-person plural pronouns, verb endings or suffixes across those ten verses, and the one skeleton lookalike inside them is the third-person object pronoun אֹתָם֙ (oshb:Jer.32.33, byte), a homograph at skeleton tier only. The declines one seam later are consistent rather than inconsistent: the same pronoun recurs at oshb:Jer.32.43 (byte), so the second-person addressee is already live across Jer.32.42-32.43 and no shift occurs there (sweep: 2 verses carrying that pronoun across Jer.32.26-Jer.32.44, byte tier, MT keys, at oshb:Jer.32.36 and oshb:Jer.32.43). No boundary change is proposed and none is required: the cut at Jer.32.36 stands.
