P12-005.challenge_claim: An exclusivity sentence enumerates three recurrence sites under a single byte label when only two of them are byte-identical, and the closing warrant sentence attributes the bound to the chapter division.
P12-005.grounds: Tier mixing verified exactly. The run אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte) is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.32.43 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, MT keys) and returns those same 2 verses at accent-stripped tier. At the third site the run reads אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.33.10, byte), differing in accentuation and carrying an added meteg; it therefore fails byte and also fails accent-stripped, since that tier strips cantillation but retains meteg, and it matches only at the consonantal skeleton (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys, at oshb:Jer.32.36, oshb:Jer.32.43 and oshb:Jer.33.10). The sentence carries one byte label across all three sites while asserting that the construction stands nowhere else in the book, so a tier label is doing the work of the exclusivity sweep at the one site where that label is false. The construction-level exclusivity is itself sound at 3 verses; only the tier is wrong. Chapter-division attribution verified. Chapter and verse divisions are tier-4 and are never evidence in either direction, so a bound may not be attributed to one. The substantive device is named in the same sentence, the second word-event at Jer.33.1, whose MT verse is verse-initial and a member of the twenty-one-verse vayehi object, so the warrant exists and only its attribution is misplaced, which is why this stays low rather than rising. Recorded in the unit's favour on re-derivation: the closing captivity-reversal run אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.32.44, byte) is byte-identical in exactly two verses (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, MT keys, at oshb:Jer.32.44 and oshb:Jer.33.26), matching the unit's own digit, and the span's mark and seg disclosures are complete against the inventory.
P12-005.remedy: device_notes: split the recurrence sentence by tier, byte-identical at Jer.32.36 and Jer.32.43 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier) and consonantal-skeleton-only at Jer.33.10 (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier), noting that the third site fails accent-stripped because that tier retains meteg, and attach the nowhere-else claim to the skeleton tier where its three-verse digit holds. boundary_rationale: restate the closing sentence so the bound is attributed to the word-event formula at Jer.33.1 alone, and delete the chapter division as the stated bound. Tests the cure must pass: every tier label in the recurrence sentence must reproduce its stated site list on a re-run sweep at that tier, with the exclusivity digit and the tier standing in the same sentence; and the closing sentence must name only a tier-1 device as the bound, surviving with all chapter-division wording deleted.

P12-007.challenge_claim: The three-site recurrence of the quoted-objection construction is asserted beside a byte tier label, but the shared wording holds only at the consonantal-skeleton tier; and one closing gloss reaches past the run it is attached to.
P12-007.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both halves stand. The two earlier sites carry a byte-distinct pointing, אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte), which sweeps to 2 verses by itself at byte tier. So the 3-verse digit and the third-and-last ordinal are both true, but only at the weakest tier -- a contiguous consonantal substring search with its own named hazard -- while the sole tier label in the sentence sits on the adjacent single-verse splice. A recurrence claim owes its own tier at write time, and an ordinal exclusivity riding on an unlabelled digit makes the omission material rather than cosmetic; that is why this settles at medium and not low. The second item is a distinct defect and also holds: the closing splice עַל יְדֵ֥י מוֹנֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.33.13, byte) covers the counter's-hands clause and the divine-speech tag only, while the English paired with it also renders the flock-passing clause, whose Hebrew, עֹ֣ד תַּעֲבֹ֧רְנָה הַצֹּ֛אן (oshb:Jer.33.13, byte), stands outside the run -- gloss extent exceeding splice extent. Neither seam is touched: both onsets are verse-initial divine-mouthed koh-amar formulas, and the span's mark set (setumah at oshb:Jer.33.11 and oshb:Jer.33.13, paseq at oshb:Jer.33.10 and oshb:Jer.33.12, single-witness WLC, count-only) is disclosed in full and matches the inventory.
P12-007.remedy: device_notes: label the recurrence with its own tier -- state the 3-verse digit and the third-and-last ordinal as a consonantal-skeleton sweep, and keep the byte label attached only to the oshb:Jer.33.10 splice it belongs to. Test the cure by re-sweeping the exact pointed run at the tier named: the sentence must not survive if the sweep at that tier fails to return both the digit and the ordinal. boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing pairing at oshb:Jer.33.13 so gloss extent equals splice extent -- either extend the splice back through the flock-passing clause or shorten the English to what the quoted run holds. P12-008.challenge_claim: The internal-seam argument misplaces what the formula at 33:17 governs; the structured signal key files the days-are-coming formula under the date-frame family, which the byte-swept date census excludes; and a paseq inside the span goes undisclosed while the same verse's setumah is cited.
P12-008.grounds: All three hold on the bytes. First: oshb:Jer.33.17 opens כִּי כֹ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.33.17, byte), a ki-subordinated formula, and what follows it is the throne guarantee alone, לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֣ת לְדָוִ֔ד אִ֕ישׁ יֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל כִּסֵּ֥א בֵֽית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.33.17, byte) -- “David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel” (web:Jer.33.17). The turn to the priesthood falls one verse later at וְלַכֹּהֲנִים֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.33.18, byte), which opens on a plain waw and carries no speech formula at all. The row states twice -- in the boundary field and again in the rejected alternative -- that the guarantee turns from throne to altar at verse 17; that is byte-false at the coordinate named, so the rival being declined is described at the wrong verse and under a device that does not stand there. The one-unit reading survives: no addressee or frame-owner change falls anywhere between oshb:Jer.33.14 and oshb:Jer.33.18. Second: the machine-readable key files הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.33.14, byte) under the date-frame family, but the byte-swept date and reign header object holds 19 classified candidate sites and oshb:Jer.33.14 is not among them; the formula is a temporal prophetic onset, sweeping to 5 verses at byte tier and 15 at the consonantal tier, not a dated reign header. Third: the inventory records a paseq seg at oshb:Jer.33.16 inside the span and it is cited nowhere, while that same verse's setumah is cited -- the span's mark set is therefore not fully disclosed, and the asymmetry sits inside a field that has already engaged both layers elsewhere in this part.
P12-008.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: move the throne-to-altar turn to oshb:Jer.33.18 and say that verse opens on a plain waw with no speech formula; describe the oshb:Jer.33.17 device as a ki-subordinated koh-amar introducing the throne guarantee. Test: the rival's verse and its device must both be re-derivable from the bytes at the coordinate named, and the sentence must fail if the formula quoted does not stand at that verse. observed_substrate_signals: replace the date_frame key carrying the days-are-coming formula with a non-date onset key. Test: every date_frame key in the row must resolve to a site the classified date and reign header census actually holds. device_notes: add the paseq at oshb:Jer.33.16 as a count-only, single-witness disclosure. Test: for each layer the field engages, every coordinate the inventory records inside the span is named.

P12-009.challenge_claim: The closing comparison at 33:22 is named as a second analogy from the day-night covenant, but the bytes draw it from the uncountable host of heaven and the immeasurable sand of the sea; and the conditional splice at 33:20 stops short of the words its English renders.
P12-009.grounds: Both hold. oshb:Jer.33.22 opens on its own protasis, אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יִסָּפֵר֙ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֖ד ח֣וֹל הַיָּ֑ם (oshb:Jer.33.22, byte), and only then reaches the apodosis the row splices; the comparandum is creation order -- “As the army of the sky can't be counted, and the sand of the sea can't be measured” (web:Jer.33.22) -- not the covenant of oshb:Jer.33.20 and oshb:Jer.33.21, and the words carrying it lie wholly outside the quoted run, so the mischaracterisation cannot be caught from the splice alone. Same class, second instance: the conditional splice at oshb:Jer.33.20 ends at the first covenant noun while the English paired with it runs on through the day covenant and the night covenant, whose Hebrew, הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י הַלָּ֑יְלָה (oshb:Jer.33.20, byte), is outside the splice. Both are prose-and-pairing defects, not seam defects, which is why this settles at low: the bounding formulas at oshb:Jer.33.19 and oshb:Jer.33.23 are verse-initial members of the 21-verse word-event set (the third and fourth of the four such onsets standing in this two-chapter block, after oshb:Jer.32.26 and oshb:Jer.33.1), no addressee or frame-owner change falls inside the span, and the span's single setumah at oshb:Jer.33.22 is disclosed and matches the inventory with no paseq and no variant note anywhere in the span.
P12-009.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-describe the closing comparison at oshb:Jer.33.22 as drawn from the uncountable host of heaven and the immeasurable sand of the sea, and either extend the splice to carry that protasis or drop the same-covenant characterisation entirely; re-cut the oshb:Jer.33.20 pairing so the English stops where the splice stops, or extend the splice through the night covenant. Test: each characterisation of a comparison must be re-derivable from the bytes of the verse it names, and each curly-quoted rendering from the splice beside it alone -- the original fails both tests as written.

P12-010.challenge_claim: The declared false positive on the in-field variant disclosure is refuted: the form-exact recurrence sweep lands on the qere at one of its two sites, and the field carrying that sweep gives no variant disclosure.
P12-010.grounds: The digit re-derives independently and the exclusivity holds: the quoted clause sweeps to exactly 2 verses at byte, accent_stripped and consonantal tiers alike -- oshb:Jer.32.44 and oshb:Jer.33.26 -- so nothing in the claim's arithmetic is wrong. What is wrong is its disclosure. At oshb:Jer.33.26 the matched run is the pointed qere with the unpointed ketiv standing immediately before it in the same clause, כִּֽי אשוב אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.33.26, byte), while the other site carries no variant note at all, כִּֽי אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.32.44, byte); the inventory records one variant note at oshb:Jer.33.26 and none at oshb:Jer.32.44 (single-witness WLC). The disposition treated as a false positive is the warning that a Hebrew quote in the device field binds to a variant-bearing verse with no variant disclosure in that field, and that warning is exactly true: a form-exact claim asserted across one marked and one unmarked site is the guarded hazard, and the marks were read in the boundary field but not in the field that makes the claim. The declared disposition therefore does not hold. The wider-construction texture standing at oshb:Jer.33.11 is not owed against this row: the claim is explicitly to the exact inflected form and is true at that scope, so severity settles at low -- an incomplete disclosure, not a false claim.
P12-010.remedy: device_notes: add the ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Jer.33.26 beside the recurrence sentence, naming that the matched form is the qere, that the unpointed ketiv stands immediately before it, and that the sweep's other site carries no note (single-witness WLC). Re-mark that flag's disposition from false positive to accepted. Test: every Hebrew quote binding to a verse the variant inventory records must carry the variant disclosure inside its own field, not only elsewhere in the row -- the original passes nowhere else and fails here.

P13-002.challenge_claim: A byte-true release-term chain runs across this row's own closing seam and is disclosed in neither prose field.
P13-002.grounds: The cohesion object is byte-true. The release noun stands inside the span in the very clause naming the covenant this row narrates, לִקְרֹ֥א לָהֶ֖ם דְּרֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.34.8, byte), and again twice past the seam at oshb:Jer.34.15 and oshb:Jer.34.17; the consonantal sweep returns 3 verses book-wide and all 3 sit in this chapter, so the term is attested on both sides of the cut and nowhere else in the book. A byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and neither prose field names it. The cut itself is untouched and the remedy is disclosure, not a respan: oshb:Jer.34.12 is a whole verse opening on the formula itself, וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.12, byte), a verse-initial member of the 21-verse word-event set, which is the book's primary macro-seam device -- hence low. Everything else in the span verifies: the header at oshb:Jer.34.8 is the prose-sermon superscription shape, the closing variant pair is quoted as the bytes have it, and the front petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.7 and the closing setumah and variant note at oshb:Jer.34.11 all match the inventory under the right type (single-witness WLC). Separately observed and not raised against this row: the device field attaches a byte tier label to bare coordinates where no Hebrew run is quoted -- the same shape recurs at oshb:Jer.34.11, oshb:Jer.34.16, oshb:Jer.34.22, oshb:Jer.35.5, oshb:Jer.35.11, oshb:Jer.35.15 and oshb:Jer.35.16 across this part, so it is a sweep-class candidate rather than a one-row fix.
P13-002.remedy: device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the release term inside the span at oshb:Jer.34.8 and its two occurrences past this row's close at oshb:Jer.34.15 and oshb:Jer.34.17 (sweep: 3 verses, all in this chapter), and state that the verse-initial word-event onset at oshb:Jer.34.12 carries the cut against that cohesion. Because one seam is at stake, this and the facing disclosure on the unit opening at oshb:Jer.34.12 are ONE paired edit, not two independent ones. Test: the sentence must name the swept object, its unit and its digit, and must fail if the term proves attested outside this chapter. Corpus-wide order candidate (separate sweep, not this row's work order): strip or re-site the byte tier labels attached to bare coordinates in device_notes throughout this part, so a tier label always names a quoted run.

P13-003.challenge_claim: The structured signal key marks the 34:12 word-event formula as the book's non-initial occurrence, which the verse bytes and the book-wide census both contradict; the parashah citations doing pivot work in the boundary field stand without their witness disclosure; and the release-term chain crosses the row's opening seam undisclosed.
P13-003.grounds: All three items are confirmed on the bytes; the severity settles at medium, not high. Position: oshb:Jer.34.12 is a whole verse of eight words opening on the formula itself, וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.12, byte). The byte-swept census carries this verse among the 21 sites of that shape, records 20 of them verse-initial, and reserves the non-initial label for exactly one site elsewhere in the book, where a ten-days temporal clause precedes the formula. Filing this site under the non-initial term asserts a second exception against a byte-proven single-site fact, inside the machine-readable field, and contradicts the row's own boundary prose, which states the position correctly and quotes the full verse. High overstates it precisely because of that: no boundary moves -- a verse-initial onset is if anything the more ordinary tier-1 warrant -- and no prose digit or exclusivity is corrupted; what is defective is a false structured label, which is medium. Second: the setumah at oshb:Jer.34.16 and the closing petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.22 are both cited inside the field carrying the boundary argument with no single-witness naming, while that disclosure appears only in the device field; this layer requires the disclosure on every citation, and the first of the two sits at exactly the pivot the row declines to cut. Third: the release term reaching this span from oshb:Jer.34.8 (sweep: 3 verses, all in this chapter) crosses this row's opening seam undisclosed -- the facing half of the same seam's cohesion gap. What verifies: both variant pairs are byte-exact at oshb:Jer.34.11 and oshb:Jer.34.17, the span's mark set is otherwise complete and correctly typed, and the refusal to cut at the therefore-clause is sound, the same divine mouth carrying the formula on both sides of oshb:Jer.34.17.
P13-003.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the non-initial word-event key with the verse-initial key of the same shape. Test: the census's non-initial label may stand on exactly one row in the book and only at the site the census names; the position must be re-derived from the verse's own first word before the key is written -- the original fails on the verse's first word. boundary_rationale: add single-witness naming and the mark type to both parashah citations in that field, or drop them there and leave the layer to the device field. Test: every parashah citation in every field names its single witness and its type, petuchah never conflated with setumah. device_notes: disclose the release-term chain crossing the front seam from oshb:Jer.34.8 into oshb:Jer.34.15 and oshb:Jer.34.17 -- ONE paired edit with the facing disclosure on the unit closing at oshb:Jer.34.11, not two.

P13-004.challenge_claim: Two byte-checkable naming lapses: the armies fled from are Chaldean in both witnesses rather than Babylonian, and the ancestor whose charge the unit turns on stands in two attested spellings inside this span, undisclosed.
P13-004.grounds: The first lapse is real; the second is a true byte observation wrongly framed as a lapse of the same class, so the challenge is refined rather than upheld whole. First: oshb:Jer.35.11 reads מִפְּנֵי֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּמִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte) -- for fear of the army of the Chaldeans and for fear of the army of Aram. The Babylon token stands once in that verse and only inside the royal title, נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֮ (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte), and the Babylon token, its directional form and the Chaldeans token are separate count objects that are never blended. Calling the armies Babylonian blends two of them at the single place in the span where the distinction is visible, and both witnesses read otherwise: “for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians” (web:Jer.35.11). Second: the ancestor does stand in two attested spellings in span -- the short form יוֹנָדָ֨ב (oshb:Jer.35.6, byte), which sweeps to 3 verses at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.35.6, oshb:Jer.35.10, oshb:Jer.35.19), and the long form יְהוֹנָדָ֤ב (oshb:Jer.35.8, byte), which sweeps to 4 (oshb:Jer.35.8, oshb:Jer.35.14, oshb:Jer.35.16, oshb:Jer.35.18), both confined to this chapter. But the duty to name a name form is triggered by a digit, a form claim or an exclusivity claim about the name, and this row hangs none: it quotes the ancestor inside a verse splice and counts nothing. Recording the variance would improve the row; its absence is not a defect, and pairing it with the token blend overstates it. Neither item moves a boundary: the header at oshb:Jer.35.1 is a byte-identical member of the prose-sermon superscription shape, the closing seam rests on the verse-initial word-event onset at oshb:Jer.35.12, and the span's marks -- the preceding petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.22, the closing petuchah at oshb:Jer.35.11 and the count-only paseq at oshb:Jer.35.5 -- all match the inventory (single-witness WLC), with no variant note owed anywhere in the span.
P13-004.remedy: boundary_rationale: name the armies by the tokens the verse carries -- the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram -- and leave the Babylon token to the royal title where it actually stands. Test: every nation-token characterisation must be re-derivable from the tokens standing in the verse cited, with the Babylon token, the directional form and the Chaldeans token never blended; the original fails on the one verse where all of them are in view. No work order issues on the name-form half: if the spelling variance is added at all, it must name both attested spellings with their own digits and units, and it must not be recorded as a repair.

P13-005.challenge_claim: The word-event key marks a verse-initial formula as the book's non-initial occurrence; one divine-title key collapses two byte-distinct koh-amar stacks the span carries side by side; the count-only paseq citation carries the wrong digit; and the row gives no disclosure for keeping a koh-amar judgment address under the symbolic-act category.
P13-005.grounds: Three of the four items hold and one is refuted, and one supporting digit is attached to the wrong object. Position: oshb:Jer.35.12 is a whole verse opening on the formula, וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.35.12, byte); the census carries it among the 21 sites of that shape, 20 verse-initial, with the single non-initial site standing elsewhere in the book -- so the non-initial key is byte-false here, exactly as at the sibling site closing at oshb:Jer.34.22, and the cure is the same. Title blending: upheld. The title at the first formula is the full signature stack, יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.35.13, byte), a member of the 32-verse object; the title at the therefore-clause is a different stack, יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.35.17, byte), which sweeps to 1 verse at byte tier and 3 at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.35.17, oshb:Jer.38.17, oshb:Jer.44.7) and is not a member of the 32-verse object at all. Correction to the challenge's own arithmetic: the 5-verse digit does not belong to that five-word run -- it belongs to the shorter God-of-Armies title, יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ (oshb:Jer.35.17, byte), which sweeps to 5 verses at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.5.14, oshb:Jer.15.16, oshb:Jer.35.17, oshb:Jer.38.17, oshb:Jer.44.7); naming the object before the digit is what separates them, and the blending finding stands under either object. The row's own prose quotes and renders both titles distinctly and byte-exactly, so the blend is confined to the single structured key, which is where it must be cured. Paseq digit: upheld -- the inventory records two segs at oshb:Jer.35.15 and the citation names one, and under a count-only convention the digit is the whole content of the citation. Unit type: refuted. The operative-category law permits a per-bytes deviation from the operative category on a one-sentence disclosure; it does not demand a disclosure for using the operative category itself. This span is the interpretation half of a symbolic-act report whose command, performance and interpretation default to one unit except where a tier-1 seam intervenes -- which is precisely what the word-event onset did here -- and the row's own literature type names it as that interpretation. No deviation is asserted, so no deviation sentence is owed. New finding, unraised on this row: the setumah at oshb:Jer.35.16 is cited in the boundary field with no single-witness naming and no type disclosure of its own, and the same citation in the device field carries no witness tag either -- the same class already visible at the sibling site.
P13-005.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the non-initial word-event key with the verse-initial key of the same shape; and split the single divine-title key into two, one for the full signature stack at oshb:Jer.35.13 and one for the God-of-Armies stack at oshb:Jer.35.17. Test: the non-initial label may stand at exactly one site book-wide, and each title key must resolve to one byte-distinct attested stack -- no key covering two, and no digit carried without its object named. device_notes: correct the paseq citation at oshb:Jer.35.15 to the digit the inventory records (2 segs), keeping it count-only with no intra-verse position; and add single-witness naming plus the mark type to the setumah citation at oshb:Jer.35.16 in both fields that cite it. Test: every count-only citation carries the inventory's own digit, and every parashah citation names its single witness and its type. No work order issues on unit_type.

P13-006.challenge_claim: The row gives no disclosure for keeping a self-contained blessing address to the Rechabites under the symbolic-act category rather than a more specific oracle type, since no command, performance, or re-enactment of the wine test falls in its two verses.
P13-006.grounds: The bytes tie these two verses to the act rather than away from it. The span opens on the tag וּלְבֵ֨ית הָרֵכָבִ֜ים אָמַ֣ר יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.35.18, byte), turning the address to the very household whose refusal the wine test staged, and the promise at oshb:Jer.35.19 answers the obedience named in the same verse; both quoted runs are whole verses at byte tier. The closed 13-value unit-type vocabulary carries this chapter's Rechabite material as its own listed symbolic-act example, so the label is the operative category here, not a departure from it, and the one-sentence disclosure the challenge invokes is owed only where a row's bytes push it OFF the operative category, which is the opposite of what these bytes do. The ruled granularity likewise holds a symbolic act's command, performance, and interpretation as ONE unit unless a tier-1 seam intervenes: the two tier-1 seams inside this chapter (the verse-initial word-event onset at oshb:Jer.35.12, one of the 21 verses of that shape, and the verse-initial speaker-and-addressee tag at oshb:Jer.35.18) split the complex into rows without changing the operative category of its parts. Nothing else in the row is disturbed on re-derivation: the koh-amar at both verses stands in Jeremiah's named mouth, the frame-owner requirement met in a book where the full divine formula is also put in a false prophet's mouth (sweep: 2 verses, 28:2 and 28:11); the divine-title key is byte-correct at both, יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.35.18, byte) and יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.35.19, byte), members of the 32-verse full-stack signature; and the mark accounting is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 35:18, PE at MT 35:19, a true absence at the front-seam verse MT 35:17; 0 paseq segs and 0 variant notes in MT 35:18-35:19, single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak in the Prophets). The challenge cites no byte at all: it rests on a category-policy reading alone, which under the symmetric evidence rule is as defective as a row resting on a marker alone.

P13-007.challenge_claim: The rival splitting Jer.36.2-4 from Jer.36.5-7 is refused on a ground the span's own splice supplies against it, a speaker-and-addressee change falling at Jer.36.5; the frame prose miscounts the book's word-event shapes as two; the literature type carries an unsourced reading ordinal; and the two overlapping runs at Jer.36.1 are glossed past their own extent.
P13-007.grounds: All four parts verify on re-derivation, and two of them reach further than charged. (1) The refusal ground is byte-contested exactly where it matters: oshb:Jer.36.2 opens קַח לְךָ֮ מְגִלַּת סֵפֶר֒ (oshb:Jer.36.2, byte), a second-person imperative inside the divine speech introduced by the word clause of oshb:Jer.36.1, while the proposed seam verse opens וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֶת בָּר֖וּךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Jer.36.5, byte), a fresh speech tag with a new speaker and a new addressee. An explicit addressee or scene shift is a tier-1 internal cut class, so the rival is refused on the one term the bytes hand it; the ground's other two terms hold (no date frame and no word-event formula stand between oshb:Jer.36.2 and oshb:Jer.36.7). NEW, same field: the ground also misassigns the mouth, since verses 2 and 3 are the divine commission to Jeremiah, not part of 'the single unbroken commission Jeremiah gives Baruch', which begins only at oshb:Jer.36.4-Jer.36.5. (2) The shape count is wrong against a three-member object: the byte-derived frame census carries THREE never-blended word-event shapes (sweep: 21 verses of the vayehi-debar-YHWH shape; 11 verses of the prose-sermon superscription shape; 4 verses of the OAN/topical header shape). NEW: the two-shape wording stands in TWO fields, the boundary rationale as well as the device note, so the cure is one edit over both. Correcting the challenge's illustration without disturbing its digit: the omitted 4-verse shape is not the nearest in wording, since this verse's own clause הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) shares hadavar and the me'et-YHWH tail with the 11-verse superscription shape the row does name, while the omitted shape reads debar-YHWH without that tail. (3) The ordinal: the only reading in the span is the infinitive complement לִקְרֹ֥א בַסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) under the finite וַיַּ֗עַשׂ (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) in a dateless compliance summary, while the finite narrated reading וַיִּקְרָ֨א בָר֥וּךְ בַּסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.10, byte) falls outside it, so 'first publicly read' settles in-span what the bytes leave held; the heuristic flag standing on that word is a true positive, not a false one. NEW: that ordinal is one chain with the ordinal in the unit spanning Jer.36.9-Jer.36.13, and the two must be cured together. (4) Gloss extent: the first run at oshb:Jer.36.1 ends at הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) yet its rendering carries 'this', whose token הַזֶּה֙ (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) lies outside the run; the second run begins at הַזֶּה֙ (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) yet its rendering carries 'came', whose token הָיָ֞ה (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) lies outside it. Not disturbed: the onset is a verse-initial date frame, so classified among the 19 candidate sites of the byte-derived date object, and the mark set is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 36:3 and MT 36:8, the preceding PE at MT 35:19; 0 paseq segs and 0 variant notes in MT 36:1-36:8, single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak).
P13-007.remedy: 1) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the clause 'with no addressee change, date frame, or fresh word-event formula falling between them' with a ground that names the speaker-and-addressee change at Jer.36.5 and rests the refusal on the frame-plus-speech default (an embedded commission stays with the narrative frame that reports it); in the same edit correct 'the single unbroken commission Jeremiah gives Baruch' so that verses 2-3 read as the divine commission to Jeremiah. TEST the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): read the replacement against the speech tag standing at oshb:Jer.36.5, it must stay true with that tag in view. 2) boundary_rationale AND device_notes: replace 'neither of the book's two named word-event shapes' and 'the book's two named word-event formulas' with the three-shape census, each shape carrying its verse digit; one edit covering both fields. TEST: the sentence must name three shapes with three digits and still hold this onset apart from all of them. 3) literature_type_guess: drop 'first' from 'first publicly read', or add the one-sentence disclosure that the in-span reading is an infinitive complement inside a dateless compliance summary while the narrated reading stands at Jer.36.10; cure this together with the ordinal in the unit spanning Jer.36.9-Jer.36.13, as a paired ordinal cure rather than a spot fix. TEST: no ordinal may remain that the verb forms at Jer.36.8 and Jer.36.10 cannot settle. 4) boundary_rationale: re-cut both renderings at oshb:Jer.36.1 to their splice extents. TEST: no rendering may contain an English word whose Hebrew token stands outside the run it is paired with.

P13-008.challenge_claim: Both boundaries are byte-sound, but two content claims outrun the bytes: a second reading event at Jer.36.10, and a full-year interval between the two dated notices.
P13-008.grounds: Both hold, and each reaches one field further than charged. Interval: the earlier notice carries בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הָרְבִיעִ֔ת (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) with no month token, while this row's own onset carries בַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠חֲמִשִׁית together with בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁעִ֔י (oshb:Jer.36.9, byte), a year and a ninth month. With the earlier notice's month unstated in both witnesses the elapsed time is undetermined, so 'a full year on' is not sourceable from the bytes. NEW: the same unsourced interval stands a second time in literature_type_guess ('the year-later public reading'), so the cure is a two-field edit. Ordinal: the reading of the scroll stands as a finite verb once in this stretch, וַיִּקְרָ֨א בָר֥וּךְ בַּסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.10, byte); the earlier report is the infinitive complement לִקְרֹ֥א בַסֵּ֛פֶר under the finite וַיַּ֗עַשׂ (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) in a dateless compliance summary, so whether Jer.36.10 is a second event or the narration of the summarized one is a held reading, and 'Baruch's own second reading' settles it silently; the same clause also attributes the reading to 'verses 9 and 10' where the reading verb stands at Jer.36.10 alone and Jer.36.9 carries the fast proclamation. NEW: this ordinal is one chain with 'first publicly read' in the unit spanning Jer.36.1-Jer.36.8 and with this row's own device-note phrase 'the first writing-and-reading scene', three sites resting on one undisclosed reading. Severity stays low because nothing here moves a seam: the onset is a verse-initial date frame among the 19 candidate sites of the byte-derived date object; a real addressee turn stands at the rear seam (the relay is to the officials at oshb:Jer.36.13, the sending is to Baruch at oshb:Jer.36.14); the span's mark-absence statement is true (0 PE, 0 SAMEKH, 0 paseq segs, 0 variant notes in MT 36:9-36:13, single-witness WLC) with the preceding SAMEKH at MT 36:8 correctly typed; and the row already sits at reduced confidence with its frontier flagged.
P13-008.remedy: 1) boundary_rationale: replace 'a fresh date frame, a full year on from the row before' with the byte-stated dating, a fourth-year notice carrying no month against a fifth-year, ninth-month notice with the interval undetermined, and apply the same correction to literature_type_guess's 'year-later'; one edit over both fields. TEST the cure must pass: every temporal statement must be resolvable from the two notices' own year and month tokens alone. 2) strongest_rejected_alternative: drop the ordinal in 'Baruch's own second reading', or carry a one-sentence disclosure that the earlier reading stands as an infinitive complement inside a dateless compliance summary; fix the same clause's verse attribution to Jer.36.10; pair the edit with the ordinal in the unit spanning Jer.36.1-Jer.36.8 and with this row's device_notes phrase. TEST: no ordinal may remain that the verb forms at Jer.36.8 and Jer.36.10 cannot settle.

P13-011.challenge_claim: Converging: the machine-readable word-event key tags this row's opening formula as the book's non-initial occurrence though the verse opens on it, and the count-only paseq at the closing verse goes undisclosed inside a field that already walks that layer. Added by one item only: the rival is refused for lack of a fresh formula at the exact verse where the row's own rationale names two, and the closing verse is called Baruch's compliance though the splice fronts Jeremiah.
P13-011.grounds: The two items converge on the SAME two defects (1 and 2 below); one of them adds two further, DISTINCT defects (3 and 4). (1) Position: oshb:Jer.36.27 opens וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.36.27, byte), verse-initial. The byte-derived census carries this shape at 21 verses, 20 of them verse-initial, with the single non-initial site at oshb:Jer.42.7, whose bytes open on the separate temporal clause וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Jer.42.7, byte) before the formula. The key therefore asserts a second non-initial site against a one-site fact, in the machine-readable field, and contradicts the row's own rationale, which calls the same verse the opening of the reply. Tier-1, byte. (2) Disclosure symmetry: the mark inventory records BOTH a SAMEKH and one paseq seg at MT 36:32. The field cites the paseq at MT 36:27, cites the SAMEKH at MT 36:32, walks the closing verses, and adds a true absence statement for MT 36:30, so the paseq layer is engaged for this span and left incomplete at exactly one coordinate (single-witness WLC, count-only, no intra-verse position claimed). (3) The rival splitting Jer.36.29-31 from Jer.36.27-28 is refused for 'no fresh formula marking an inner seam' while the row's own rationale names two at that seam: כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte) and לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.36.30, byte). The ground that actually carries the refusal is frame ownership: at oshb:Jer.36.29 the formula stands inside the divine instruction to Jeremiah, וְעַל יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte), so the mouth does not change across the seam, and a koh-amar onset cuts only WITH a frame-owner change. (4) Agency: the closing splice fronts Jeremiah, וְיִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לָקַ֣ח מְגִלָּ֣ה אַחֶ֗רֶת וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֮ (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), with Baruch first the recipient of the scroll and only then the one who writes on it, so 'Baruch's own compliance' misreads the subject of the two finite verbs the row itself quotes. (5) NEW: in the same rationale a byte tier label stands on a bare coordinate at oshb:Jer.36.31 with no Hebrew run quoted, occupying the splice-and-rendering slot every other citation in that field fills with a spliced run, so the byte assertion has nothing to certify. P14-001.challenge_claim: The larger-unit rival is refused on a ground the row's own full-verse splice contradicts, these two verses being dense with personal names, and the name-form disclosure carries a recurrence claim with no sweep digit while under-naming the attested spellings.
P14-001.grounds: (1) Byte-refuted as charged: the opening verse names five persons in one clause chain, צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte) and נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte), and the prophet is named at oshb:Jer.37.2; both witnesses agree, “Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.” (web:Jer.37.1). The row quotes both verses in full at byte tier, so the denial is contradicted from inside the row, and it is the half doing the work against the following verse. (2) NEW: the ground's surviving term does not discriminate either. Neither of these verses is among the 19 candidate sites of the byte-derived date object and neither carries a year token, but neither does the verse the rival would fold them into: oshb:Jer.37.3 opens וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte) with no date token and no place in that inventory. So the dateless term is true of the span and equally true of what it is contrasted with; the whole ground needs replacing, not half of it. What genuinely separates them is byte-visible: a summary report of the reign and of a general failure to hear, against a narrated sending of two named envoys carrying a request. (3) Upheld: the rationale calls the reign 'dated to a king' installed by Babylon, where the relative clause identifies the installer and the verse carries no date token at all. (4) Upheld, with the framing corrected: the device note says the resh-family spelling 'recurs through the chapters ahead' with no digit and no unit named, in a field that does supply a digit (sweep: 3 verses) for the predecessor's Coniah form, while that spelling stands in 29 verses. The under-naming is real, the book carrying FOUR live spellings (the resh family at 29 verses plus its plene byform at 49:28, which rides a doubled variant note; the nun family at 6 verses plus the vav-less defective form at 28:11 and 28:14), but the corrected finding is a disclosure gap rather than a stated miscount: the sentence asserts no count, it names one alternative indefinitely and leaves two attested spellings unnamed. (5) Not disturbed: the Coniah digit is right token-bound (3 verses: 22:24, 22:28, 37:1) and the three name forms for this one king match the inventory; the onset is a wayyiqtol accession clause and not a word-event formula of any of the three shapes; and the mark statement is true (0 PE, 0 SAMEKH, 0 paseq segs, 0 variant notes in MT 37:1-37:2, single-witness WLC) with the preceding SAMEKH at MT 36:32 correctly typed. Severity stays medium: the row stands at high confidence on a rejected alternative whose stated ground fails on both of its terms.
P14-001.remedy: 1) strongest_rejected_alternative: strike 'with no named individual or dated moment' and rest the refusal on the byte-visible contrast, a summary regnal notice with a general hearing report against the narrated sending of named envoys with a request at Jer.37.3. TEST the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): read the replacement against the five personal names standing in oshb:Jer.37.1 AND against the datelessness of oshb:Jer.37.3, it must survive both. 2) boundary_rationale: strike 'dated' from the installer clause; no date token stands in the verse and this site is not among the classified date-header candidates. TEST: no date word may remain in a sentence whose verse carries no year or month token. 3) device_notes: give the resh-family recurrence its digit and unit (sweep: 29 verses) and name the remaining attested spellings, the plene resh-family byform at 49:28 and the two nun-family forms (6 verses; the vav-less defective at 28:11 and 28:14), or say plainly that one alternative among four attested spellings is named here. TEST: every name-form sentence names its spelling and carries a digit with its unit, matching the digit discipline the same field already applies to the predecessor's name form.

P14-002.challenge_claim: The unit buries the book's primary macro-seam device mid-span at a junction the mark layer independently keys, leaves an in-span ketiv/qere undisclosed, and truncates its own frame splice below the gloss paired with it.
P14-002.grounds: Two of the three components verify exactly; the first is over-framed. Ketiv/qere: one note falls inside Jer.37.3-Jer.37.10, at MT 37:4, standing in the bytes as בֵּ֥ית הכליא הַכְּלֽוּא (oshb:Jer.37.4, byte; unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, single-witness apparatus). The unit discloses the parashah layer and the paseq layer for this span and no ketiv/qere anywhere, while the note one span later at MT 38:2 is disclosed in the material covering Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6, so the convention is present and simply not applied. Upheld. Quote/gloss parity: the frame splice ends on the construct אֱלֹהֵ֣י while the verse continues יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.37.7, byte), and the rendering paired with it supplies the of-Israel element, so the English exceeds the Hebrew offered and the declared elohei-yisrael signal is never quoted whole. Upheld. The macro-seam component is refined rather than upheld as framed. Both of its facts hold: the onset at MT 37:6 is a verse-initial וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.37.6, byte), a member of the narrative word-event shape, standing inside the span; and a petuchah is keyed to MT 37:5, the junction immediately before it (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver, absence never counterevidence). But the ruled granularity for this narrative complex keeps an embedded oracle with the frame it answers, and the bytes support the unit's disposal of the rival: MT 37:7 continues כֹּ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֧חַ אֶתְכֶ֛ם אֵלַ֖י (oshb:Jer.37.7, byte), directing the reply back through the same messengers sent at MT 37:3, so there is no addressee change across the 37:5|37:6 junction. The seam therefore stands. What does not stand is the handling of the mark and the calibration. A mark keyed to a verse keys that verse's closing junction, which is exactly how the same field reads the setumah it keys at MT 37:8 and how the neighbouring units read the marks at MT 37:16, MT 38:6 and MT 38:23; here alone the petuchah is re-described as texture on the content of verse 5, which conceals the corroboration the rival actually carries. And high confidence is not supportable while a verse-initial member of the book's primary macro-seam device sits interior with a tier-3 mark keyed to the junction before it and the rival is answered on content alone. Two further findings on this row, byte-verified and outside the challenge as raised. First, the device-note sentence names three shapes and then says the two never blend: the counted system has three disjoint shapes (sweep: 21 / 11 / 4 verses, no shared verse), so the sentence miscounts the system it invokes, and the exclusivity word carries no adjacent digit, which a tier label can never supply. Second, of the three curly-quoted renderings in this unit two are not byte-identical to the staged verses they cite, and the one keyed to web:Jer.37.6 diverges only in a possessive apostrophe stored as the ASCII character where the staged verse carries the typographic one, in a run containing no nested quotation at all. The standing disposition treating this unit's straight-quote flag as falling on the WEB text's own second-level marks therefore does not reach the divergence that is actually present.
P14-002.remedy: device_notes: add the in-span ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 37:4, single-witness, present-but-not-engaged, alongside the paseq disclosure already there; and re-word the never-blend sentence to name three shapes with its own digit-bearing count (21 / 11 / 4 verses, disjoint). boundary_rationale: extend the frame splice through יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל so the Hebrew run covers every element the paired rendering carries, and re-collate the extended run at byte tier; re-word the MT 37:5 petuchah so it keys the junction it closes rather than the content of its own verse, matching the junction wording already used for the MT 37:8 setumah in the same field; and restore the staged apostrophe in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.37.6, and for the rendering keyed to web:Jer.37.3 re-cut to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation rather than substituting ASCII marks for the staged ones. confidence: high to medium. strongest_rejected_alternative: state that a verse-initial member of the word-event system stands at 37:6 with a tier-3 mark keyed to the junction before it, and that the unit is nevertheless held whole because the reply is directed back through the same messengers. Tests the cure must pass: no apparatus class present in Jer.37.3-Jer.37.10 left undisclosed; the Hebrew run and its paired rendering cover the same elements, byte-collated; every exclusivity word carries an adjacent digit naming the swept object and unit; every curly-quoted rendering is character-identical to its cited staged verse.

P14-004.challenge_claim: The unit's substantive original-language work is byte-correct throughout, but it carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere note inside its own span.
P14-004.grounds: The note is real and in span. MT 37:19 opens ואיו וְאַיֵּה֙ (oshb:Jer.37.19, byte; unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, single-witness apparatus), inside Jer.37.17-Jer.37.21, and no ketiv/qere disclosure appears in any field, while the same class is disclosed one span later at MT 38:2. Nothing else in the disclosure set is owed: the setumah keyed to MT 37:17 and the petuchah keyed to MT 37:16 at the front junction are both cited under their own types with the two never conflated (single-witness, tier-3 weak), and no paseq seg falls in the span. The substantive work does verify. אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.37.20, byte) carries hiriq under the nun, against qamats at the divine-title sites, so the courtly reading is byte-correct, it is argued from the pointing rather than the consonants, and the forward reference to the second of the two courtly sites lands on אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte), which carries the same pointing. Low severity is right: the note is not the token any content claim leans on, and the omission is an inconsistency rather than a missing practice. One finding outside the challenge as raised, byte-verified: all three curly-quoted renderings in this unit diverge from the staged verses they cite, and the one keyed to web:Jer.37.21 diverges only in a possessive apostrophe, in a run carrying no nested quotation anywhere. The standing disposition that both straight-quote flags on this unit fall on the WEB text's own second-level marks inside properly wrapped runs is therefore refuted for that run at least: the divergence there is a verbatim-fidelity one, not a delimiter-nesting one, and the two arms need separate cures.
P14-004.remedy: device_notes: add the in-span ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 37:19, single-witness, present-but-not-engaged. boundary_rationale: restore the staged apostrophe in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.37.21, whose only divergence is that character; for the renderings keyed to web:Jer.37.17 and web:Jer.37.20, which contain second-level quotation, re-cut each run to a stretch of the staged verse that carries no nested quotation rather than substituting ASCII marks, so the verbatim arm and the delimiter arm are satisfied by one edit. Tests the cure must pass: every apparatus class present in Jer.37.17-Jer.37.21 disclosed; every curly-quoted rendering character-identical to its cited staged verse and carrying no second-level quotation mark in either form.

P14-005.challenge_claim: The unit's stated name-disambiguation principle is refuted by the very bytes it splices, and both divine formulas standing in its span are left unquoted with the formula's mouth misassigned.
P14-005.grounds: Both limbs verify at the bytes. Name forms: the device-note principle that the bytes disambiguate each figure by full patronymic fails in both directions inside this material. MT 21:1 carries פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.1, byte) and MT 38:1 carries וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte) - the same name-plus-patronymic pair - so the full patronymic joins those two sites rather than separating them, and the chapter-20 priest the note names instead is not the collision. Conversely the embassy member stands as יְהוּכַ֣ל בֶּן שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte) against וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), where both elements differ in form, so full-patronymic matching would split one man. The unit also splices two different spellings of the Malchiah name into one row under one English name with no spelling disclosure: מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte) against מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte), the second the only such form of that name in the book (sweep: 1 verse) - the exact site the per-attested-spelling rule targets. Frame ownership: two koh-amar frames stand in span, כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte) and כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.3, byte). Neither is quoted, the splice offered beginning after the first; the second goes unmentioned; and the declared koh-amar signal therefore rests on no quoted form. The mouth sentence attached to the splice names Yahweh as the formula's mouth, where MT 38:1 reads אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), making these the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people. One refinement of the framing that does not change the outcome: a clause earlier in the same field does say that what the officials heard is Jeremiah's own proclamation, so the defect is a contradictory mouth attribution in one sentence rather than a wholly unnamed mouth, and the cure is a clause rather than a rebuild. One finding outside the challenge as raised, byte-verified: three paseq segs stand inside Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6, two keyed to MT 38:4 and one to MT 38:6 (single-witness, count-only), and the unit discloses no paseq at all, although the units on either side of it in this material do disclose that layer. The three parashah marks it cites, at MT 38:1, MT 38:2 and MT 38:6, are correct under their own type, and the ketiv/qere at MT 38:2 is correctly disclosed and correctly scoped, the splice ending before the pair.
P14-005.remedy: device_notes: replace the full-patronymic sentence with the per-site reading the bytes give - name MT 21:1 as the site the full patronymic joins rather than separates, and disclose the two Malchiah spellings the unit itself splices, מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה at MT 38:1 against מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ at MT 38:6, with a digit naming the swept object and unit; add the in-span paseq disclosure for MT 38:4 and MT 38:6, single-witness, count-only, no position claimed. boundary_rationale: quote the koh-amar form at MT 38:2 rather than beginning the splice after it, add the second frame at MT 38:3, and re-word the mouth sentence so the formula's mouth is named as Jeremiah relaying it to all the people. Tests the cure must pass: every name form claimed is quoted at its own site in its attested spelling with the count object named before the digit; every declared speech_formula signal has a quoted form standing behind it; every koh-amar citation names whose mouth carries it; every apparatus class present in Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6 disclosed.

P14-006.challenge_claim: The unit narrates the exact token that carries the span's only ketiv/qere note without disclosing the note, against the rule that pmark state is checked before any content claim in a K/Q verse.
P14-006.grounds: Verified. The one note inside Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13 stands at MT 38:11 as בְּלוֹיֵ֣ הסחבות סְחָב֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.38.11, byte; unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, single-witness apparatus), and the sentence saying Ebedmelech gathers rags and cords characterises precisely that word; no ketiv/qere disclosure appears in any field. The variant is specific to the verse the prose leans on - the parallel one verse later is plain pointed text, בְּלוֹאֵ֨י הַסְּחָב֤וֹת (oshb:Jer.38.12, byte) - so this is not a class the unit could have treated as absent. Medium severity is right, above the same omission where no content claim touches the token. The rest verifies: אֲדֹנִ֣י (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte) carries hiriq under the nun, the second of the book's two courtly sites against the qamats-pointed divine title, and the unit argues the pointing rather than the consonants; the setumah keyed to MT 38:6 at the front junction and the one keyed to MT 38:13 at the close both match under their own type (single-witness, tier-3 weak). The epithet observation is byte-true - the Cushite title is carried at MT 38:7, MT 38:10 and MT 38:12 while MT 38:11 reads עֶֽבֶד מֶ֨לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.38.11, byte) alone - but that is a per-site naming variation, not a defect, and no remedy attaches to it. Two findings outside the challenge as raised, byte-verified. A paseq seg also stands at MT 38:11 (single-witness, count-only), the same verse as the undisclosed note, and is likewise undisclosed, so the omission is the whole apparatus of that verse rather than one class of it. And the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.7 diverges from the staged verse at two possessive apostrophes, in a run containing no nested quotation at all, so the standing disposition treating this unit's straight-quote flag as falling on the WEB text's own inner marks does not reach the divergence actually present.
P14-006.remedy: device_notes: add the in-span disclosures for MT 38:11 - the ketiv/qere, single-witness, with the written and read forms named, and the paseq seg, single-witness, count-only, no position claimed. boundary_rationale: where the prose characterises the rag-and-cord token, state that the word it characterises is the one the note stands on; restore the staged apostrophes in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.7; and for the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.9, which contains second-level quotation, re-cut to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation rather than substituting ASCII marks. Tests the cure must pass: every apparatus class present in Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13 disclosed; no content claim rests on a ketiv/qere token without the note disclosed beside it; every curly-quoted rendering character-identical to its cited staged verse.

P14-007.challenge_claim: The divine-title claim at 38:17 has no support in the form the unit quotes, blends distinct count objects, and asserts an in-chapter recurrence the bytes do not contain; a cited K/Q verse is also left undisclosed.
P14-007.grounds: All four limbs verify, and the first is worse at the bytes than as raised. The device-note run is צִדְקִיָּ֡הוּ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte). It is called the full title stack, yet it carries no title element at all: the stack stands next in the verse as אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte). The run is non-parallel to its paired rendering at both ends - it opens on the addressee's name, which the rendering does not carry, and it stops before the three-word title the rendering does carry - so the mandatory engagement on a boundary-relevant title claim rests on a splice containing none of it. The object is blended. The form present is the Elohei-tsevaot Elohei-Yisrael stack (sweep: 3 verses - 35:17, 38:17, 44:7), a different count object from the book's signature stack (sweep: 32 verses), of which 38:17 is not a member: swept from the signature form as it stands at MT 39:16, the 32 verses are returned without 38:17 among them. The recurrence claim is false at the bytes: of the 3 verses carrying the form, exactly 1 falls in chapters 37-38, namely 38:17 itself, so the assertion that the same full stack is used elsewhere in these chapters has no site to point to, and it is made with no digit and no swept object. A tier label on the splice does not stand in for a recurrence check. Ketiv/qere: one note stands at MT 38:16, a verse the unit cites for its mark and characterises as the king's sworn oath, with the pair inside that oath clause, חַי יְהוָ֞ה את אֲשֶׁר֩ (oshb:Jer.38.16, byte; single-witness apparatus); no disclosure appears. High severity is right: this is not a wording matter but a title claim, a count object and a recurrence all unsupported at the bytes, in the field where the unit's one declared speech-formula signal is argued. What holds: the parashah marks keyed to MT 38:13, MT 38:16, MT 38:18 and MT 38:19 all match under their own types with the two types never conflated, and the mouth of the oracle is correctly named as Jeremiah's rather than left to the formula. Two findings outside the challenge as raised. A paseq seg stands at MT 38:20, inside Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 (single-witness, count-only), undisclosed. And the supporting reading offered elsewhere for this unit - that the fuller stack is correctly distinguished from the shorter form used earlier in this narrative - answers a claim the unit does not make: the unit's sentence asserts that the same full stack recurs in these chapters, and that is the sentence the bytes refute.
P14-007.remedy: device_notes: re-cut the splice to begin at the koh-amar word and run through the final element of the title, dropping the addressee's name, so the Hebrew covers exactly what the paired rendering carries, and re-collate the run at byte tier; replace the same-full-stack sentence with the byte-true object and its digit - the Elohei-tsevaot Elohei-Yisrael form, 3 verses book-wide, of which this is the only site in chapters 37-38 - and name it as distinct from the 32-verse signature stack; add the in-span disclosures for the MT 38:16 ketiv/qere, single-witness, present-but-not-engaged, and the MT 38:20 paseq, single-witness, count-only, no position claimed. observed_substrate_signals: correct the declared speech_formula key if it does not name the form actually quoted after the re-cut. boundary_rationale: for the renderings keyed to web:Jer.38.14, web:Jer.38.17 and web:Jer.38.19, which contain second-level quotation stored with ASCII marks, re-cut each to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation. Tests the cure must pass: the title stack claimed is quoted whole in the Hebrew run and byte-collated; every count object is named before its digit and never blended with a neighbouring stack; every recurrence claim carries a digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit; every apparatus class present in Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 disclosed.

P14-008.challenge_claim: The unit's front seam cuts inside one unbroken speech turn, and the showing-formula warrant offered for the cut is contradicted by the bytes and withdrawn by the unit's own device note.
P14-008.grounds: The bytes carry it. The last speech introduction before the seam is וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.20, byte). MT 38:21 then opens וְאִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את (oshb:Jer.38.21, byte) - a waw-conditional, with no speech introduction, no addressee change, no narrative frame and no dated notice. The verse runs to nine words entire, so the account is exhaustive: nothing in the pointed text marks a unit onset there. A conditional series straddles the junction: אִם יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte), then וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא תֵצֵ֗א (oshb:Jer.38.18, byte), then MT 38:21's third protasis on the same exit verb. A byte-true construction straddling a unit's own junction argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and no field discloses it. One refinement of the framing that strengthens rather than weakens the finding: MT 38:17-38:18 belong to an earlier turn of the same speaker, interrupted by the king at MT 38:19, while MT 38:21 sits inside the turn opened at MT 38:20 - so the series runs across two of Jeremiah's turns, and the seam itself falls inside one of them, which is the fact that kills the cut. The showing formula does not carry the seam either. הִרְאַ֖נִי stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - 24:1, 38:21). At 24:1 the formula is the verse's own opening, הִרְאַנִי֮ יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.24.1, byte); at 38:21 it is verse-medial, standing behind the conditional. So the device note's plural reference to the book's formal vision reports overstates a form with one other site, carries no digit, and the same note concedes that the showing is embedded inside an ongoing address rather than standing as a separate report - which withdraws the only warrant offered for the cut. The mark layer offers no corroboration at this junction: marks key MT 38:19 and MT 38:23, not MT 38:20 (single-witness, tier-3 weak; stated as non-corroboration only, since absence is never counterevidence). The lesser point also holds: the poetic-lines characterisation of verse 22 rests on the modern line layout of the English, which is tier-4 and never evidence in either direction, and it carries no tier label. High severity is right: once the warrant is withdrawn, the seam has no surviving tier-1 signal standing in its own onset verse. The unit's closing junction is not in question - the petuchah keyed to MT 38:23 sits at it, no ketiv/qere note or paseq seg falls in Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23, and both pointed splices reach byte tier.
P14-008.remedy: Two parts, and the boundary part is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption - never author work. Author work: device_notes - replace the vision-report sentence with the byte-true form and its digit, the showing verb standing in 2 verses book-wide, verse-initial at 24:1 and verse-medial at 38:21, and drop the plural reference to the book's formal vision reports; boundary_rationale - disclose the conditional series running at MT 38:17, MT 38:18 and MT 38:21 across the unit's own front junction, and either tier-label the poetic-lines characterisation of verse 22 as modern layout or drop it; boundary_rationale - re-cut the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.22, which stores the staged second-level and single marks as ASCII, to a stretch of the staged verse carrying no nested quotation. Boundary PROPOSAL for adoption: fold Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23 into Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 as one unit closing at the mark keyed to MT 38:23. Test any retained seam must pass - the test that killed the original: it must cite a tier-1 signal standing in MT 38:21's own bytes other than the embedded showing clause, and must state why the straddling conditional series and the unbroken speech turn opened at MT 38:20 do not argue continuity against it.

P14-009.challenge_claim: Two distinct items on one row: that the device notes name the unit continuing the account by its sequence position alone, without the verse anchor the unit's other cross-references carry; and that the closing splice runs past the English it is paired with, the added clause being a temporal protasis left open across the unit's own closing seam without disclosure.
P14-009.grounds: Both items hold and they are distinct defects in different fields, not one defect seen twice. First item, in device_notes: the closing sentence carries the custodial notice forward to the day Jerusalem is taken and identifies the continuing account by position alone. The register rule bars positional references to other units and requires every cross-unit reference to be verse-anchored, and the anchor exists - the verse-initial dated frame opens at 39:1, corroborated by a setumah keyed to that verse (single-witness, tier-3 weak). Low severity for this item on its own. Second item, in boundary_rationale, and the heavier of the two: the closing splice ends וְהָיָ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְכְּדָ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.38.28, byte), while the rendering it is said to match stops at the taking of the city and carries no counterpart for that clause - so the Hebrew exceeds the English, and a real divergence between the two witnesses at the unit's own end verse goes undisclosed. That clause is a temporal protasis with no main clause inside the span: the dated notices at MT 39:1 and MT 39:2 intervene and the narrative main clause follows at וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ (oshb:Jer.39.3, byte). A byte-true construction straddling the unit's own closing junction argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and the unit instead reads the verse as a clean custodial close at high confidence. Medium severity, and it governs the combined rating. What holds: this unit's apparatus handling is complete. The petuchahs keyed to MT 38:26 and MT 38:27 and the doubled setumah-plus-petuchah keyed to MT 38:28 are all disclosed under their own types and expressly not conflated, the front junction's petuchah at MT 38:23 likewise, and no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg falls in Jer.38.24-Jer.38.28, so nothing further is owed there. One finding outside both items, byte-verified: the barred positional construction is not confined to this unit - the neighbouring units in this stretch likewise refer to an adjacent unit by position rather than by verse - so the cure for that item is a sweep of the class across the stretch, not a spot fix on one row.
P14-009.remedy: device_notes: replace the positional reference with the verse anchor - name the dated onset at 39:1 and the setumah keyed to it, single-witness, tier-3 weak. boundary_rationale: either re-cut the closing splice to end at יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם so the Hebrew and the paired rendering cover the same ground, or keep the full-verse splice and disclose that the rendering carries no counterpart for the trailing clause; in either case add the cross-seam disclosure that the trailing clause is a temporal protasis whose main clause falls beyond the unit's own closing junction; and restore the staged apostrophe in the rendering keyed to web:Jer.38.24 while re-cutting its second-level quotation to a stretch carrying none. confidence: high to medium, since the disclosed straddling construction now stands against the cut. Carry the positional-reference cure as one sweep across the units of this stretch rather than as a single-row edit. Tests the cure must pass: no field names another unit by position; every Hebrew run and its paired rendering cover the same elements; a byte-true device straddling the unit's own junction is disclosed wherever it stands.

P14-010.challenge_claim: The closing-seam warrant misstates the verb forms the bytes give at Jer.39.4, and one declared substrate signal is not observed anywhere in the unit's own span.
P14-010.grounds: Both components verify at the bytes; the severity is understated. MT 39:4 has a compound subject - Zedekiah together with וְכֹ֣ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte) - and both the flight verb and the exit verb attached to it are plural, וַֽ֠יִּבְרְחוּ and וַיֵּצְא֨וּ (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte); the one singular verb in the verse is וַיֵּצֵ֖א (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte), a verb of going out toward the Arabah, not of fleeing. The rejected alternative's stated ground, that verse 4 turns the account onto the king personally with his own verb of flight, is therefore false at the bytes, and it is a form-class claim made with no pointed splice from that verse anywhere in the unit - the only citation of verse 4 in the row is the English one. The seam itself survives, but on a device the unit never names: the narrative-shift onset וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר (oshb:Jer.39.4, byte). The declared narrative-frame key naming a reign change is not observed in Jer.39.1-Jer.39.3: both dated frames count regnal years to one ongoing reign, לְצִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ (oshb:Jer.39.1, byte) and לְצִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.39.2, byte), and nothing in the span reports a change of reign.observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field; a declared key with no in-span instance is a field defect, not a wording preference. Severity is refined from low to medium. Two independent byte-false items stand in the unit - a form-class claim in the very field that carries the seam's rejected alternative, and a declared substrate key with no observed instance - and form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits. Neither reaches the boundary, which is why this stops short of high. What holds and should be preserved: both date shapes verify against the classified date inventory, the device-note contrast of where the bet-prefix lands is byte-true, the resh-family spelling of the besieger's name is named at its own site, the setumah keyed to MT 39:1 and the doubled setumah-plus-petuchah keyed to MT 38:28 are disclosed under their correct types with the two never conflated, and the span carries no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg, so the disclosure set is complete. This is also the only unit in this stretch whose curly-quoted renderings are all character-identical to the staged verses they cite.
P14-010.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the verb-of-flight ground with the bytes - name the compound subject at MT 39:4 and the narrative-shift onset וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר as the seam's warrant. boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.39.4, and carry a byte-collated splice from that verse into the field that argues it, since a form claim about a verse cannot stand without one. observed_substrate_signals: drop the reign-change key; if a second key is wanted, use one the span observes, such as the second dated frame the unit already argues at MT 39:2. Tests the cure must pass: every form-class claim is quoted from the verse it is made about and collated at byte tier; every key in observed_substrate_signals has an instance inside the row's own span; the seam warrant names a device standing in the onset verse's own bytes.

P14-012.challenge_claim: This unit's content sits inside the same flagged narrative-overlap block as the immediately preceding unit but, unlike that unit, discloses no relationship to the closing appendix's parallel account of the same events; no apparatus mark inside the span compensates for the gap.
P14-012.grounds: The factual premise holds and the apparatus premise holds; the disclosure duty does not. The burning of the city, the deportation and the provision for the poor are reported a second time at the corresponding point of the closing appendix (web:Jer.52.13, web:Jer.52.14, web:Jer.52.15, web:Jer.52.16), and across MT 39:8-39:10 the parashah, paseq, ketiv/qere and special-letter inventories are all empty, so nothing enumerated is owed inside the span and nothing is over-claimed. But the appendix relation is typed-relation metadata whose ruled standing is never boundary evidence and never counterevidence; the neighbouring unit's note is worded precisely to withhold evidentiary weight, so it creates no disclosure object whose symmetry can be swept the way the mark, ketiv/qere and island layers are swept. A note that carries no evidentiary force cannot generate an omission defect elsewhere, and the item cites no bytes and no ref for the duty it asserts. What is defective in the very field the item points at is adjacent and checkable: device_notes argues that the guard-captain's title is carried forward by 'the following span', a positional cross-reference, where the title in fact stands as רַב טַבָּחִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.39.11, byte) and again at oshb:Jer.39.13, neither of which appears in boundary_evidence_refs, though that field does carry oshb:Jer.39.7 for the front seam. A verse argued in prose outside the row's own span belongs in the refs, and a cross-row reference is verse-anchored, not positional. Second, undetected by either item: the quotation of web:Jer.39.8 in boundary_rationale renders the staged text's two right single quotation marks as straight typewriter apostrophes, in 'king's' and in 'people's' - the straight-for-curly class; the unit's other two renderings, of web:Jer.39.9 and web:Jer.39.10, are character-exact against the staged text. The challenge as framed drops to low; the row's final weight is set by that quote-fidelity defect, which is the same class this material carries at medium elsewhere.
P14-012.remedy: Three orders. (1) In device_notes, replace the positional forward reference with a verse-anchored one naming oshb:Jer.39.11 and oshb:Jer.39.13, and add both refs to boundary_evidence_refs; test: no positional or relative cross-row wording survives in any field, and every verse argued outside Jer.39.8-Jer.39.10 resolves inside boundary_evidence_refs. (2) In boundary_rationale, restore the two right single quotation marks inside the web:Jer.39.8 rendering; test: the quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied - the test the original fails. (3) No appendix-relationship note is owed; if one is added anyway it stays prose-only, with no structured ref, no entry in boundary_evidence_refs and no boundary role.

P14-013.challenge_claim: A ketiv/qere note at MT 39:12, inside this unit's own span, goes wholly undisclosed while the special letter at 39:13 and the setumah at 39:14 are disclosed correctly; and the roster is said to name four officers, a digit the bytes it cites contradict.
P14-013.grounds: Both items stand, and they are distinct defects rather than one. The ketiv/qere inventory records a note at MT 39:12, inside Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14. The unit engages two other apparatus classes in the same short span - the book's one special-letter seg at MT 39:13 (inventory: 1 site book-wide) and the setumah at MT 39:14 - so the layer is live here and symmetry is completed by sweeping the span, not by spot-citing the verses the prose happens to reach; MT 39:12 is reached by no sentence and by no individual ref, appearing only inside the outer range citation, while boundary_evidence_refs itemises oshb:Jer.39.10, oshb:Jer.39.11, oshb:Jer.39.13 and oshb:Jer.39.14 around it. The officer digit is independently defective. MT 39:13 names three officers, each carrying his own title - נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָ֣ן רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים וּנְבֽוּשַׁזְבָּן֙ רַב סָרִ֔יס וְנֵרְגַ֥ל שַׂר אֶ֖צֶר רַב מָ֑ג (oshb:Jer.39.13, byte) - and then a collective body, וְכֹ֖ל רַבֵּ֥י מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:Jer.39.13, byte). The staged rendering quoted beside the digit yields no four-member list either, and the digit names no count object before counting, so it fails the bytes in both witnesses and the name-the-object-first rule at once. Sound and to be preserved: the special-letter handling is exact - the seg is x-small, disclosed single-witness, and the verse carries exactly one word ending in a final nun bearing the seg's accent (count: 1 in-verse), the second officer's name, so the attribution is byte-determinable rather than assumed; the resh-family royal spelling and the guard-captain title are right per site. Lesser finding neither item raises: device_notes claims a fuller patronymic than any other figure sharing the name and points to that other bearer as 'named earlier', with no verse anchor and no sweep digit; the comparandum stands at oshb:Jer.38.1, which is argued in prose but absent from boundary_evidence_refs.
P14-013.remedy: Three orders. (1) In boundary_rationale, disclose the ketiv/qere note at MT 39:12, single-witness, marked present-but-not-engaged if no splice reaches it, and add oshb:Jer.39.12 to boundary_evidence_refs; test: every ketiv/qere verse inside Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14 is disclosed, checked by sweeping the span's inventory rather than by spot cite. (2) In boundary_rationale, replace 'names four officers' with the named count object and its byte-supported digit - three officers each carrying his own title, followed by the collective body of the king of Babylon's chief officers; test: the digit is reproducible from oshb:Jer.39.13's own bytes and from the staged rendering quoted beside it. (3) In device_notes, verse-anchor the comparandum at oshb:Jer.38.1, add that ref to boundary_evidence_refs, and either carry a digit-bearing sweep for the 'any other' comparison or drop the exclusivity wording; test: no exclusivity claim stands without an adjacent digit, and no unanchored positional cross-reference remains in any field.

P14-014.challenge_claim: One item: the unit's own rendering of verse 18 carries straight typewriter marks where the staged text carries curly ones, and the resumptive, pre-fall timing of verse 15 goes undrawn. The other: the opening-seam warrant misdescribes the word-event system - the shape it contrasts 39:15 against is not verb-initial and the system counts three shapes, not two - while the declared title stack is never quoted and the closure token at 39:17 and 39:18 is never named.
P14-014.grounds: The word-event item is upheld and can be put more sharply. Of the three counted shapes (21, 11 and 4 verses) exactly one, the narrative-onset shape, is verb-initial (1 of 3). The superscription shape opens with the article-noun and stands its verb third - הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה (oshb:Jer.40.1, byte) - and the topical-header shape opens with the relative particle; the counted inventory further separates the three as different unit classes, narrative onset against prose-sermon superscription against topical header, so calling them 'the book's two counted narrative shapes' both undercounts the system and mis-classes the shape it names. The non-membership finding survives intact: 39:15 fronts a prepositional addressee phrase ahead of the verb - וְאֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.39.15, byte) - and belongs to none of the three.
