The form-label is also wrong: that fronted element is not the object, and the clause subject is the word-of-YHWH phrase itself. The declared-signal item is upheld and extends further than stated: the full signature title stack stands at כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.39.16, byte) and is never quoted, tier-labelled or mouth-named, and the unit's rendering of that verse is cut with an inserted ellipsis - a character the staged text does not carry - at exactly the point where the staged rendering goes on to render that stack, so the sole speech-formula entry among this unit's 2 declared signals loses its evidence in both languages at once. The closure token does stand at MT 39:17 and MT 39:18 (2 verses in span), unnamed; at 162 verses book-wide it is closure corroboration only, so that is under-engagement, not a missing driver. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: the rendering of web:Jer.39.18 degrades four marks, not two - the contraction in 'won't', the mark closing the embedded clause after 'trust in me,', and both marks in the trailing pair after 'says Yahweh' - and a fifth degraded mark stands in the rendering of web:Jer.39.15, in 'Yahweh's', which no item names. The resumption point is refuted as a defect: the pre-fall setting argues for this cut rather than against it, and the disclosed cohesion duty runs to byte-true devices straddling the seam that argue continuity against the row, so its absence is an unused corroboration, not an omission. Confirmed sound: the ketiv/qere note at MT 39:16 is disclosed present-but-not-engaged and correctly scoped, since the rendering stops before it, and the setumah marks at MT 39:14 and MT 39:18 verify under their own type.
P14-014.remedy: Four orders. (1) In boundary_rationale, correct the contrast: name the three counted shapes and state that exactly one of them is verb-initial, or drop the verb-initial comparison and keep only the byte-true non-membership finding; test: every shape-class statement is reproducible from the counted inventory's own verse sets and from the opening word of each shape's bytes. (2) In boundary_rationale, re-label the fronted element as a prepositional addressee phrase, not the object, and name the word-of-YHWH phrase as the clause subject; test: the form-label is checkable against oshb:Jer.39.15's pointed bytes. (3) In boundary_rationale, quote the 39:16 formula in pointed Hebrew with its tier and its mouth named and re-cut the English rendering so the declared signal's own words are not what the ellipsis removes, or else drop speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh_tsevaot_elohei_yisrael from observed_substrate_signals; test: every declared substrate signal has a quoted, tier-labelled form in the prose, and no quoted run carries a character the staged text lacks. (4) In boundary_rationale, restore all five staged marks in the web:Jer.39.15 and web:Jer.39.18 renderings; test: each quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied. No change is owed for the pre-fall timing observation.

P15-001.challenge_claim: One item: the device note asserts that Gedaliah is not named in this stretch, though the name stands inside the unit's own byte-tier splice of 40:5, and the paseq inside the span is undisclosed while the ketiv/qere in the same span is disclosed. The other: the header-shape argument is well grounded, but two renderings carry straight marks where the source carries curly ones, and the paseq at 40:1 goes unmentioned.
P15-001.grounds: The naming defect is real, is the heaviest in this material, and is self-refuting in-row. MT 40:5 reads אֶל גְּדַלְיָ֣ה בֶן אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן שָׁפָ֡ן (oshb:Jer.40.5, byte): the personal name stands immediately before the patronymic that device_notes offers as kinship-only pointing, and it stands inside the full-verse splice the unit itself carries at byte tier in boundary_rationale. The staged rendering of the same verse names him as well, and the unit's English quotation of 40:5 is cut back to its closing sentence, so the rendering that would have exposed the error is the part not shown. The claim is therefore false in both witnesses and contradicted by the unit's own quoted evidence, and it carries an unanchored positional forward reference to the unit that follows on top of that. High severity is right. The apparatus item is also upheld: the paseq inventory records a seg at MT 40:1, inside Jer.40.1-Jer.40.5, and the unit discloses the ketiv/qere at MT 40:3 and the preceding setumah at MT 39:18, so the layer is engaged and the sweep is owed across the span. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: three marks are degraded, not two - the opening mark of the embedded speech in the web:Jer.40.2 rendering, and in the web:Jer.40.4 rendering both the contraction in 'don't' and the closing mark after 'go there'. Sound and to be preserved: the header's membership in the eleven-verse superscription shape is byte-correct at oshb:Jer.40.1, carrying the aleph-lamed form rather than the one-site variant; disclosing that the shape frames a release narrative rather than sermon content, instead of letting the formula name the unit, is the right handling and should survive the repair; and the renderings of web:Jer.40.1, web:Jer.40.5 and web:Jer.40.6 are character-exact, the 40:5 one at a live continuation-fold verse.
P15-001.remedy: Three orders. (1) In device_notes, strike the claim that Gedaliah is not yet named in this stretch; if the kinship observation is kept at all, re-cut it to the bytes - both the personal name and the two-generation patronymic stand at oshb:Jer.40.5 - and verse-anchor any forward reference instead of naming the unit that follows; test: every name-presence claim is checkable against the unit's own splice and against the staged rendering of the cited verse, which is the check the original fails. (2) In boundary_rationale, disclose the paseq at MT 40:1, single-witness, seg-layer, count-only, with no intra-verse position asserted; test: the span's paseq inventory is swept, not spot-cited. (3) In boundary_rationale, restore the three staged marks in the web:Jer.40.2 and web:Jer.40.4 renderings; test: each quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied.

P15-003.challenge_claim: One item: a paseq at MT 40:7 inside the span is not mentioned while the ketiv/qere and paseq at MT 40:8 are disclosed together, and the rendering of verse 9 opens the embedded speech with a straight mark. The other: the same 40:7 omission, with the device note's wording that apparatus converges at 40:8 read as a uniqueness claim the inventory does not support.
P15-003.grounds: The omission is upheld; the uniqueness reading is not. The paseq inventory records a seg at MT 40:7 and another at MT 40:8, both inside Jer.40.7-Jer.40.10; the unit discloses only the second, and it quotes MT 40:7 in full in the same field, so the verse is squarely inside its attention and the layer is explicitly engaged - symmetry here is completed by sweeping the span. But the device note's sentence, that two apparatus classes converge at 40:8, is byte-true as written: MT 40:8 alone in this span carries both a ketiv/qere pair and a paseq (inventory across Jer.40.7-Jer.40.10: 2 paseq segs, 1 ketiv/qere note), and the sentence asserts a co-occurrence, not the exclusive presence of the paseq layer. The defect is the missing 40:7 disclosure, not the convergence wording, and the sentence should be preserved rather than rewritten once the omission is cured. Severity is medium rather than low: this layer's disclosure symmetry is unconditional and the omitted verse is quoted in full in the field that engages the layer. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: three marks are degraded, not one - in the web:Jer.40.9 rendering both the opening mark of the sworn assurance and the contraction in 'Don't', and in the web:Jer.40.10 rendering the closing mark after 'you have taken', which no item names. Sound and to be preserved: the ketiv/qere at MT 40:8 is stated in the right direction, written form before read form, both standing in the verse's own bytes, and labelled single-witness; the setumah at MT 40:6 verifies under its own type with no petuchah conflated into it; and the referent split between the Chaldeans and the king of Babylon in adjacent clauses of oshb:Jer.40.9 is byte-true. Lesser finding neither item raises: the ketiv/qere disclosure is spliced into the middle of the sentence that introduces the named arrivals, leaving that sentence ungrammatical in the stored prose.
P15-003.remedy: Three orders. (1) In boundary_rationale, disclose the paseq at MT 40:7 beside the one at MT 40:8, single-witness, seg-layer, count-only, no intra-verse position; keep the existing convergence sentence, which is byte-true, and let it claim the two-class co-occurrence at 40:8 only; test: the paseq inventory for Jer.40.7-Jer.40.10 is swept and every disclosed seg is count-only. (2) In boundary_rationale, restore the three staged marks in the web:Jer.40.9 and web:Jer.40.10 renderings; test: each quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied. (3) In boundary_rationale, repair the sentence carrying the ketiv/qere disclosure so the disclosure stands as its own clause rather than interrupting the naming sentence; test: the sentence parses on its own and the disclosure keeps its single-witness label.

P15-004.challenge_claim: The front-seam argument is contradicted by the bytes the unit itself quotes, and the one disclosed cross-seam cohesion device misdescribes the verse it appeals to: the verse named as the source of the recurrence carries a three-item list, not the two-item pairing claimed, and the shared words are not byte-identical.
P15-004.grounds: The recurrence half is upheld on the bytes; the front-seam half is narrowed. The unit's closing verse carries the two-item יַ֥יִן וָקַ֖יִץ (oshb:Jer.40.12, byte tier), while the verse named as the source of the recurrence carries a three-item list, יַ֨יִן וְקַ֜יִץ וְשֶׁ֗מֶן (oshb:Jer.40.10, byte tier), matching “gather wine and summer fruits and oil” (web:Jer.40.10). Neither shared word is byte-identical across the two verses: the produce noun agrees only once accents are stripped, and the conjoined word differs in its own vowel, sheva at oshb:Jer.40.10 against qamats at oshb:Jer.40.12, so it agrees only at skeleton tier. The oshb:Jer.40.10 form is spliced in no field of the unit and the recurrence carries no tier label, so a sameness claim stands with no quoted form behind it and on the wrong count object, a pairing named for a three-item list. The front-seam half is narrowed rather than upheld as framed: calling the incoming population unconnected to the captains is byte-true about who the group is, since the Jews in Moab, Ammon and Edom are not the field captains, so the bytes do not contradict it. What is defective there is a disclosure gap of the same class the unit elsewhere honours: its own onset verse opens on the additive particle וְגַ֣ם (oshb:Jer.40.11, byte tier), rendered “Likewise” (web:Jer.40.11), a byte-true continuity signal standing directly across the unit's own front seam and left undisclosed while a different cross-seam device is disclosed.
P15-004.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the phrase making oshb:Jer.40.10 the source of the same pairing with a form-named, tier-labelled statement that splices the oshb:Jer.40.10 list beside the oshb:Jer.40.12 pair, names both count objects (three-item list against two-item pairing), and gives the tier at which each shared word actually agrees; device_notes: re-cut the catchword sentence to that corrected extent. boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose the verse-initial additive at oshb:Jer.40.11 as cross-seam cohesion, or restate the word 'unconnected' so it does not read against it. Tests the cure must pass: each quoted form re-collates at the tier claimed against its own cited ref, and the recurrence sentence survives the check that killed the original, namely that oshb:Jer.40.10 carries three items and that neither shared word is byte-identical across the two verses.

P15-005.challenge_claim: Two challenges: the curly-quoted rendering paired with the byte splice at web:Jer.40.14 is truncated against the staged folded text and drops the disbelief clause; and the ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Jer.40.16 names a qere letter that no codepoint in the verse supports.
P15-005.grounds: Distinct defects, both byte-confirmed, both upheld. First, the splice for oshb:Jer.40.14 is the entire verse and runs through וְלֹא הֶאֱמִ֣ין לָהֶ֔ם גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן אֲחִיקָֽם (byte tier), but the rendering paired with it stops at the warning question: the staged folded text carries “But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam didn’t believe them.” (web:Jer.40.14) after it and the frame “and said to him,” (web:Jer.40.14) before it. Gloss extent no longer equals splice extent, and the clause that falls out is the refusal to believe on which the unit's own characterisation of the scene turns. The verse is one of the staged continuation-paragraph fold sites, where fidelity is judged against the folded text rather than a re-derived layout. Second, the bytes at oshb:Jer.40.16 read תעש תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה (byte tier): the ketiv תעש is three letters, tav-ayin-shin, and the qere תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה is four, tav-ayin-sin-he. The disclosure names a five-letter qere closing he-yod; no codepoint in the verse carries a yod. The rationale's own spliced pair is correct, so the error is confined to the letter-naming prose, but it lands on a disclosure offered together with the closing segment mark at the unit's end verse, inside the book's largest such note inventory. Everything else on this unit verifies: four full-verse splices at byte tier, the closing mark correctly typed as setumah and disclosed single-witness, the paseq at oshb:Jer.40.14 cited count-only, and the exclusivity claim for the Ammonite king carrying its own in-sentence digit and byte-true (sweep: 1 verse). The declared heuristic false positives on this unit are confirmed.
P15-005.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the rendering paired with the oshb:Jer.40.14 splice to the whole staged folded verse, opening frame and disbelief clause included. device_notes: correct the qere to its four letters, tav-ayin-sin-he, and delete the yod. Tests the cure must pass: the paired rendering covers the same verse extent as the Hebrew splice at that ref, the check that killed the original being a splice running to the disbelief clause against a rendering stopping at the question; and every letter named in the ketiv/qere sentence is supported by a codepoint in the cited verse.

P15-007.challenge_claim: Renderings paired with full-verse splices are truncated at web:Jer.41.8 and web:Jer.41.6 and absent entirely at web:Jer.41.9; and the same single-witness segment layer is invoked as corroboration at oshb:Jer.41.10 while the mark of identical type at oshb:Jer.41.6 is given only texture status, with the date-object distinction drawn at oshb:Jer.41.1 not drawn at oshb:Jer.41.4.
P15-007.grounds: The quotation items converge on one defect class and are upheld as framed. The splices at oshb:Jer.41.6, oshb:Jer.41.8 and oshb:Jer.41.9 are each the entire verse at byte tier. The rendering paired with oshb:Jer.41.8 stops at the plea and omits “So he stopped, and didn’t kill them among their brothers.” (web:Jer.41.8), whose Hebrew is spliced in full as וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל וְלֹ֥א הֱמִיתָ֖ם בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.41.8, byte tier); the rendering paired with oshb:Jer.41.6 gives only the spoken line and omits “Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went, and as he met them, he said to them,” (web:Jer.41.6); and oshb:Jer.41.9 carries no paired rendering at all. The same unit renders oshb:Jer.41.4, oshb:Jer.41.5, oshb:Jer.41.7 and oshb:Jer.41.10 at full verse extent, so the practice is inconsistent inside one unit. Of the three affected verses only 1 is a staged continuation-paragraph fold site, so this is a gloss-extent failure in its own right and not only fold mishandling. The segment-layer item is upheld in narrowed form. Both marks are present and correctly typed as setumah at oshb:Jer.41.6 and oshb:Jer.41.10 and both are disclosed, so the disclosure sweep is complete; what is asymmetric is the argumentative use, the mark at the adopted end boundary invoked as corroboration for the reading adopted while the mark of identical type inside the span is set aside as texture without its equal implication for an internal seam being stated. Under a weak single-witness tier that corroborative force cannot be switched on at one site and off at the other. The date item is upheld and sharpened. The onset bytes read לְהָמִ֣ית אֶת גְּדַלְיָ֑הוּ (oshb:Jer.41.4, byte tier), a relative-day back-reference naming the preceding unit's own event; the site is not a member of the book's classified date-header candidate object, and the object distinction the parallel month notice receives is not drawn here. Beyond that, the back-reference itself reaches across the unit's own front seam and is nowhere disclosed as cohesion. The rest verifies: all eight splices reach byte tier, the per-site Shiloh form is claimed with no cross-site count offered, and the paseq entries at oshb:Jer.41.9 and oshb:Jer.41.10 are cited count-only. The declared heuristic false positives on this unit are confirmed.
P15-007.remedy: boundary_rationale: restore full-verse renderings beside the full-verse splices at oshb:Jer.41.6 and oshb:Jer.41.8 and supply the missing rendering for oshb:Jer.41.9. boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: either state the equal implication of the setumah at oshb:Jer.41.6 for an internal seam there, or drop the corroboration use of the setumah at oshb:Jer.41.10; keep both disclosures either way. boundary_rationale: name the object at oshb:Jer.41.4 as the relative-day back-reference it is, state that it is not a member of the classified date-header object, and disclose it as a byte-true device reaching back across the unit's own front seam; observed_substrate_signals: re-check the date_frame key against that corrected object. Tests the cure must pass: every full-verse splice in the unit has a paired rendering of the same verse extent in the staged folded text, the checks that killed the original being the sparing clause at web:Jer.41.8, the narrated frame at web:Jer.41.6 and the absent gloss at web:Jer.41.9; the segment layer carries the same weight at both of its span-relevant sites; and no date label stands without naming the object it does and does not belong to.

P15-008.challenge_claim: The closing device claim is byte-false in making the interception site the place the abduction had been heading away from, since that place is named nowhere in the abduction report; and the same sentence overstates that the closing mark closes the abductor's part in the account.
P15-008.grounds: The place claim is byte-false and is upheld. The abduction report locates the seizure at אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּצְפָּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.41.10, byte tier) and gives its destination as וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.10, byte tier), toward the children of Ammon. The interception place-name enters the account only at the interception itself, אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.12, byte tier), and again in the retrospect at מִגִּבְעֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.16, byte tier); the consonantal sweep returns that name in 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses), the third outside this narrative altogether. The site the abduction was heading away from is Mizpah, not the interception site, so the sentence assigns a place to a verse that does not carry it. The second, softer half of the challenge is refuted on the bytes and needs no repair. The consonantal sweep returns the abductor's name in 19 verses, none of them beyond this chapter (sweep: 19 verses); at oshb:Jer.41.16 he stands as the object of the recovery and at oshb:Jer.41.18 inside a causal back-reference to the killing already narrated. He performs no further narrated action after the escape at the unit's end verse, so reading the closing mark as closing his part in the account holds on narrative agency. The rest verifies: five full-verse splices at byte tier, renderings covering their whole verses, front-seam and closing marks both correctly typed as setumah and disclosed single-witness, and no mark, note or seg entry inside the span left undisclosed. The declared heuristic false positives are confirmed.
P15-008.remedy: device_notes: replace the clause making the interception site the point the abduction was heading away from with what the bytes carry, namely that the abduction leaves Mizpah for the children of Ammon at oshb:Jer.41.10 and that the interception site first enters the account at oshb:Jer.41.12, retaining a sweep digit for the name if the name is kept. Leave the closing-mark half of the sentence as drafted. Test the cure must pass: every place the sentence assigns to a verse is present in that verse's bytes, the check that killed the original being that the interception site is absent from oshb:Jer.41.10.

P15-009.challenge_claim: The exclusivity claim for the place at oshb:Jer.41.17 is dampened with a witness label where a digit-bearing sweep is owed, the identical claim-type at oshb:Jer.40.14 carrying its digit; and the closing seam warrant asserts a first joint-subject occurrence at oshb:Jer.42.1 that the bytes contradict.
P15-009.grounds: Both items upheld. The exclusivity item is the same defect from both sides; the first-occurrence item is additional and only one side reached it. On the first: the device sentence claims the place is named only here in the book and offers a single-witness label where an in-sentence sweep count naming object and unit is owed, and an exclusivity claim is never tier-dampened, a witness label proving the quote and not the exclusivity. The underlying fact does hold, the bytes reading בְּגֵר֣וּת כמוהם כִּמְהָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.41.17, byte tier) with the consonantal sweeps returning the place noun in 1 verse and the qere name in 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse each), so this is a disclosure failure and not a false fact; the identical claim-type at oshb:Jer.40.14 does carry its digit, which is why the declared false-positive disposition standing on this hit in the flag queue does not hold. On the second: the closing warrant says the field captains become the account's subject together for the first time at oshb:Jer.42.1. The bytes contradict it three times, once inside this unit's own opening verse - וְיֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּן קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה בָּ֥אוּ (oshb:Jer.40.13, byte tier), וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ יוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.41.11, byte tier) and וַיִּקַּח֩ יוֹחָנָ֨ן בֶּן קָרֵ֜חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֧י הַחֲיָלִ֣ים (oshb:Jer.41.16, byte tier), each a joint subject of a finite verb - and the phrase stands in 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses). What is genuinely new at the seam is word order alone, וַֽיִּגְּשׁוּ֙ כָּל שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.42.1, byte tier), fronting the captains ahead of Johanan; that is a defensible seam observation and is not what the unit claims. That sentence is also a first-occurrence claim carrying no sweep digit, so the declared false-positive disposition standing on it does not hold either. The rest verifies: three full-verse splices at byte tier, the ketiv/qere pair quoted exactly as the bytes carry it, and the front-seam, interior and closing marks all disclosed and correctly typed.
P15-009.remedy: device_notes: attach an in-sentence sweep count naming the swept object and unit to the exclusivity claim, on the pattern the same claim-type already uses at oshb:Jer.40.14; the witness label cannot carry it. boundary_rationale: replace the first-occurrence claim at oshb:Jer.42.1 with the word-order observation the bytes support, or keep a first-occurrence claim only with a sweep digit that survives the phrase's book-wide count. Flag queue: re-open the declared false-positive dispositions on this unit's device_notes exclusivity hit and on its boundary_rationale first-occurrence hit. Tests the cure must pass: the exclusivity sentence carries its own digit naming object and unit; and the seam sentence survives the sweep that killed the original, the phrase already standing as joint subject at oshb:Jer.40.13, oshb:Jer.41.11 and at this unit's own opening verse.

P15-010.challenge_claim: The note claims both name spellings are given as the bytes carry them, yet only one of the two forms is spliced anywhere in the unit, and the two figures are separated on a translation rendering rather than on the Hebrew.
P15-010.grounds: Upheld on the bytes. The two forms are not the same spelling: וִֽיזַנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן הַמַּ֣עֲכָתִ֔י (oshb:Jer.40.8, byte tier) carries the long form closing he-vav, against the short form closing he in וִֽיזַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן הוֹשַֽׁעְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.42.1, byte tier). Only the second is spliced anywhere in the unit; the first appears in none of its fields, though its ref is properly carried in the evidence list. The difference is invisible in the second witness, which renders the two alike, “Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite” (web:Jer.40.8) beside “Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah” (web:Jer.42.1), so as drafted the disambiguation rests on the patronymics in translation while the byte-level long-versus-short distinction, the live name-form hazard class here, goes unstated in the very sentence that claims to have stated it. The sweep is itself a trap at this pair: a consonantal sweep for the short spelling returns 2 verses because it matches inside the long form (sweep: 2 verses), while the long spelling returns 1 (sweep: 1 verse), so only a token-bound per-spelling read supports the claim. The rest verifies: three full-verse splices at byte tier with renderings covering their whole verses, the front-seam setumah correctly typed and disclosed single-witness, and the negative mark statement accurate, the inventories carrying no mark, note or seg entry at oshb:Jer.42.1, oshb:Jer.42.2 or oshb:Jer.42.3. The declared heuristic false positives are confirmed on their own class; this defect sits inside one of those sentences and belongs to a different class.
P15-010.remedy: device_notes: splice the oshb:Jer.40.8 form beside the oshb:Jer.42.1 form with the tier named and state the long-versus-short difference explicitly, or drop the claim that both spellings are given. Test the cure must pass: every claim that forms are given as the bytes carry them has each named form spliced at its own ref and re-collated at the tier claimed, the check that killed the original being that the oshb:Jer.40.8 form appears in no field of the unit.

P15-011.challenge_claim: The unit's internal-cohesion argument rests on a syntactic form claim that neither witness supports, the reply being called one unbroken sentence.
P15-011.grounds: The form claim is defective and that half is upheld; the framing that the cohesion argument rests on it is not, and is corrected here. The splice opens with the narrative frame וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ (oshb:Jer.42.4, byte tier), which stands outside the reply it introduces, and the verse divides internally at כְּדִבְרֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.42.4, byte tier), which carries the etnachta; the second witness sets three sentence stops inside the reported speech, two of them internal (web:Jer.42.4). No morphology or syntax layer is staged, so a sentence-level form label is a byte-checkable claim held to the discipline of a digit, and here both witnesses cut against it. The operative ground is separable and byte-true, so the boundary does not depend on the label: the speaker changes on both sides, the petition closing at oshb:Jer.42.3 and a fresh reported-speech frame opening at oshb:Jer.42.5, and no internal speaker turn falls inside the verse. The negative disclosure is accurate, no mark, note or seg entry standing at oshb:Jer.42.3, oshb:Jer.42.4 or oshb:Jer.42.5, the next falling at oshb:Jer.42.6, and the single-verse span is written in the full form. The declared false-positive disposition on the flagged word holds on its own class, since the word is not an exclusivity claim owing a sweep; this defect is a different class and is not covered by that disposition.
P15-011.remedy: boundary_rationale: drop the phrase calling the reply one unbroken sentence, or restate it as the operative claim the bytes carry, a single reply with no internal speaker turn bounded by a speaker change on both sides. Test the cure must pass: no sentence-level form label survives that the verse's own internal division or either witness's own sentence punctuation contradicts, the checks that killed the original being the etnachta inside the verse and the three sentence stops in the second witness's rendering.

P15-013.challenge_claim: The frame reasoning at the book's one non-initial word-event site is byte-correct, but the rendering paired with the closing verse's full-verse splice covers well under half of it, dropping the conditional frame and the obey-the-voice clause; the challenge grades this low.
P15-013.grounds: The defect is real and upheld; the severity as filed is understated and is corrected here. The splice at oshb:Jer.42.13 is the entire verse at byte tier, but the rendering paired with it gives only the quoted refusal: the staged folded text opens “But if you say,” (web:Jer.42.13) and closes “so that you don’t obey Yahweh your God’s voice,” (web:Jer.42.13), and both fall out. The dropped closing clause is לְבִלְתִּ֣י שְׁמֹ֔עַ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.42.13, byte tier), the obey-the-voice construction, and the dropped opening is וְאִם אֹמְרִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.42.13, byte tier), the conditional frame the unit's own device note argues from when it ties this hypothetical to the conditional structure opened earlier in the span. A gloss that drops the frame the device note reasons from is not a cosmetic extent miss, and the same defect class is graded medium where it stands at web:Jer.40.14 and at web:Jer.41.8, so a low grade here is inconsistent with its own class. A second, smaller instance in the same field was named by neither challenge: the rendering paired with oshb:Jer.42.14 drops that verse's own leading frame, “saying,” (web:Jer.42.14). Neither closing verse is a staged continuation-paragraph fold site, so the truncation pattern here reaches past the fold verses. The load-bearing frame reasoning is independently verified and stands: the onset verse carries the word-event formula only after its own ten-day wait clause rather than verse-initially, and the digits match the object exactly, 21 verses carrying that formula, 20 of them verse-initial, this the single exception (sweep: 21 verses). The messenger formula at oshb:Jer.42.9 is named on its actual form without the armies element and is the scene's first, a scan of oshb:Jer.42.1 through oshb:Jer.42.8 returning none. The front-seam setumah at oshb:Jer.42.6 is correctly typed and disclosed single-witness, and no mark, note or seg entry falls inside the span. The declared heuristic false positives are confirmed.
P15-013.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the rendering paired with the oshb:Jer.42.13 splice to the whole staged folded verse, conditional frame and obey-the-voice clause included, and restore the leading frame in the rendering paired with oshb:Jer.42.14. Test the cure must pass: gloss extent equals splice extent at every ref in the unit, measured against the staged folded text, the check that killed the original being a full-verse splice at oshb:Jer.42.13 set beside a rendering covering only the quoted refusal.

P15-016.challenge_claim: That the sentence disclosing the opening verse's mark is grammatically broken and should be repaired for clarity, the underlying mark facts being sound; and that the same sentence contradicts itself about what the mark does, that a byte-true negated-obedience clause brackets oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7 across the row's own closing seam undisclosed, and that a device note claims both name spellings are given as the bytes carry them while only one is spliced.
P15-016.grounds: The two items land on one row and are partly one defect. SENTENCE (same defect site, both items): the boundary rationale reads that oshb:Jer.43.1 'is marked with a closing setumah (...) falls inside this same opening verse', two finite predicates on one subject, and the sentence after it opens lowercase on 'disclosed here as texture:'. The prose break is real, but the clarity-only reading understates it: the parashah layer is keyed by verse (303 marked verses, type recorded per verse, single-witness, tier-3) and carries no intra-verse positions, so 'falls inside this same opening verse' is not sourceable from it; what the inventory records at that key is a setumah closing oshb:Jer.43.1, correctly typed and never conflated with petuchah. The mis-stated shape stands a second time in strongest_rejected_alternative ('the setumah that falls inside it'), so it sits on load-bearing prose, not decoration. Upheld at medium, not low. CROSS-SEAM CONSTRUCTION (refined): the negated obey-the-voice construction does stand either side of the row's own closing seam, וְלֹֽא שָׁמַע֩ ... בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.43.4, byte) and כִּ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.43.7, byte), and no field of the row names it, so a disclosure is owed under the cross-seam-cohesion rule; the construction stands in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, 11 token occurrences), 6 of them inside oshb:Jer.42.6-oshb:Jer.44.23. Three corrections to the framing: it is verse-medial at both sites, closing the etnachta colon while oshb:Jer.43.4 runs on to the dwelling-in-Judah phrase and oshb:Jer.43.7 to the arrival at Tahpanhes, so neither verse ends with it; the two are not one clause repeated, the verb being singular of Johanan at the first site and plural of the whole company at the second; and it does not bracket oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7, since oshb:Jer.43.1 carries no instance -- the two instances close two consecutive units, which corroborates a cut between them as readily as it argues continuity across it. Disclosure gap real; the continuity reading is not carried by these bytes. NAME FORM (upheld): device_notes states both spellings are given exactly as the bytes carry them, but only עֲזַרְיָ֤ה בֶן הוֹשַֽׁעְיָה֙ (oshb:Jer.43.2, byte) is spliced; no Hebrew form from oshb:Jer.42.1, וִֽיזַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן הוֹשַֽׁעְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.42.1, byte), appears in any of the row's 22 fields. The two patronymics are consonantally identical and their pointing differs only in the accent, so the claim is true but unquoted on one side. The span itself is not contested.
P15-016.remedy: boundary_rationale: rewrite the opening-verse disclosure as two complete sentences -- one stating that the inventory records a setumah closing oshb:Jer.43.1 (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration not driver), one stating the setumah closing oshb:Jer.42.22 -- and delete the 'falls inside this same opening verse' position claim; restore sentence-initial capitalisation at the second. strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the rival on the mark as the inventory records it (a segment close at oshb:Jer.43.1), keeping the existing answer that the opening verse is the temporal clause governing the accusation after it; the sentence stays one sentence. boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose the negated obey-the-voice construction recurring at oshb:Jer.43.4 and oshb:Jer.43.7 with a digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit (sweep: 10 verses), stating it is verse-medial at both and that the seam is not overturned by it. device_notes: either splice the oshb:Jer.42.1 patronymic beside the oshb:Jer.43.2 form, each with its own oshb: ref and tier named, or narrow the claim to the one form actually quoted. TESTS the cure must pass: no mark claim may assert an intra-verse position for a verse-keyed layer, and every mark claim must validate under its claimed type at its MT key; the cross-seam device must carry a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; every form claimed as given as the bytes carry it must stand in the row as a byte-tier splice with its own ref; the replacement rejected alternative must still name a real rival. No boundary change is proposed or implied by any of this.

P15-017.challenge_claim: That the row twice describes the following word-event as a dated notice, which its bytes do not carry, and that it sits at high confidence on an onset carrying no formula, vocative, or participant change, with the negated-obedience clause bracketing oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7 across that onset likewise undisclosed.
P15-017.grounds: Both charges stand as made. DATE LABEL: oshb:Jer.43.8 reads וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בְּתַחְפַּנְחֵ֖ס לֵאמֹֽר (byte) -- a verse-initial narrative word-event formula with a place adjunct and the quotative, carrying no year, month, regnal or ordinal element; the second witness carries none either, “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,” (web:Jer.43.8). The verse is absent from the 19 classified date-header candidate sites and present among the 21 verses carrying that formula (sweep: 21 verses; the single non-initial site is oshb:Jer.42.7), so the tier-1 driver named for the close is byte-true and only the dated qualifier fails. It fails twice: once in the closing warrant and once in strongest_rejected_alternative, where it is the stated ground for not carrying past the seam. CALIBRATION: the onset reads וַיִּקַּ֞ח יוֹחָנָ֤ן בֶּן קָרֵ֨חַ֙ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.43.5, byte) -- the same actors already named at oshb:Jer.43.4, a narrative action verb, and no formula, vocative, addressee change or participant change; only the close is formula-bound. The row nonetheless sits at high with frontier_flag_considered false, while the adjoining span at Jer.43.1-Jer.43.4, whose edges are of the same softness, sits a step lower. I do not contest the span: the turn from the verbal refusal to the taking-and-going is a defensible scene seam. What fails is the posture, and confidence is an ordinary row field, so correcting it is not a respan. BRACKET SUB-ITEM: real but re-framed. The negated obey-the-voice construction at oshb:Jer.43.4 and oshb:Jer.43.7 is undisclosed here as well and is owed a disclosure, but it is verse-medial at both sites rather than verse-final, the verb differs in number between them, and it saturates this arc -- 6 of its 10 book-wide verses (sweep: 10 verses, 11 token occurrences) fall inside oshb:Jer.42.6-oshb:Jer.44.23 -- so it is complex-wide texture owed disclosure, not a seam-specific counter-device.

P16-004.challenge_claim: Two defects, raised from both sides: the closing warrant and the device note describe the recurring address tag at Jer.44.24 as adding the women beside the men, though the span's own opening verse already names them; and the unit is typed judgment_oracle and carried at high confidence over a stretch its own prose says opens with no messenger formula, with no operative-category deviation disclosed.

At oshb:Jer.44.20 (byte) the tag runs עַל הַגְּבָרִ֤ים וְעַל הַנָּשִׁים֙ - the men and the women both stand there, inside an al-appositive naming who had answered. At oshb:Jer.44.24 (byte) the addressee run reads אֶל כָּל הָעָ֔ם וְאֶ֖ל כָּל הַנָּשִׁ֑ים: the women are addressed rather than described, the preposition moves from al to el, and the men-term of oshb:Jer.44.20 does not recur at that verse at all. So the boundary prose's 'now with the women named beside the men' fails in both halves - the naming is not new, and no men-term stands at the second site. The device note is a different matter: scoped as it is to the vayomer-Yirmeyahu-el-kol-ha'am tag, the addition of all the women at oshb:Jer.44.24 (byte) is true of that tag, and what is wrong there is the gloss, which carries a conjunction the named token does not have and drops the preposition that is the actual change. The second defect verifies independently: across oshb:Jer.44.20-Jer.44.23 (byte) no messenger formula stands anywhere - the koh-amar shape first enters this movement at oshb:Jer.44.25 - and every reference to the deity is third-person, at oshb:Jer.44.21 and oshb:Jer.44.22 alike. A per-bytes type deviation is allowed with a one-sentence disclosure; the device note carries none, while the five-verse oracle at Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5 discloses its own deviation in exactly that field. The checkable defect is the missing disclosure, not the type value itself, and confidence high rests on top of it.
P16-004.remedy: boundary_rationale, closing sentence: strike 'now with the women named beside the men' and state the byte change at oshb:Jer.44.24 instead - the addressee preposition moves from al to el and no men-term stands there - quoting that verse's addressee run at byte tier, since the claim is about its bytes and this row quotes none of them. device_notes: keep the tag-scoped recurrence claim, re-cut its gloss to the splice extent so the glossed words are the named token's own, and add the one-sentence operative-category disclosure for unit_type judgment_oracle over a span with no messenger formula and no divine first-person speech; re-set confidence from high once the type rests on a disclosed deviation. P16-006.grounds: Upheld on the verse's own bytes; the two sides raise the same single defect, differing only in severity. Medium rather than low, on a ground neither side states: this close cites no forward onset anywhere. The warrant offers the mis-positioned formula, the tier-3 mark closing oshb:Jer.45.5 (single-witness), and the chapter end, and neither the prose nor the evidence refs reach the fresh header at oshb:Jer.46.1 - so the defective claim is the only text-internal closure device the row puts on the record, and the tier-3 mark cannot carry the seam alone. P16-006.remedy: boundary_rationale, closing sentence: strike 'closing on the neum-YHWH formula' and state the position the bytes carry - the formula stands mid-verse at oshb:Jer.45.5 and the verse's last clause is the life-grant.
