P17-001.challenge_claim: Three defects: the collection-scope rubric is folded into a single-nation oracle without the rubric-as-its-own-unit rival ever being tested; the address at Jer.46.11 is called the vision's first direct address although second-person imperatives already stand at 46:3 and 46:9; and the hedge withholding a count at 46:10 is attached to the bare adonai token rather than to the prefixed form actually quoted.
P17-001.grounds: All three verify on bytes. Scope first: oshb:Jer.46.1 (byte) closes on עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם, plural and naming no nation, while oshb:Jer.46.2 (byte) opens לְמִצְרַ֗יִם, lamed-scoped to one. The row states that scope difference in its own prose and then carries the span to Jer.46.12, and the rival it does test is a cut after both header verses on the prose-to-poetry shift - a different seam from the one its own scope sentence raises. That rival is live under the ruled granularity, since a lamed-initial nation header is itself a tier-1 onset, and the book's opening title stands as its own superscription-typed unit at Jer.1.1-Jer.1.3; leaving it unengaged is the defect, and any actual respan is a proposal, not a finding. Second: oshb:Jer.46.3 (byte) opens עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה and oshb:Jer.46.9 (byte) opens עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙, plural imperatives rendered as commands in both witnesses, and the row's own prose calls them imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants and a summons to the allied troops. Those are direct addresses; what is new at oshb:Jer.46.11 (byte) is the named vocative בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, so the defensible claim is first named vocative, and a first-claim of any kind carries a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit. Third: the form quoted at oshb:Jer.46.10 (byte) is לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת, the lamed-prefixed title stack - its own token object, byte-attested at two verses in the OAN block and invisible to a bare-token sweep. The hedge withholds a count on the ground that the bare skeleton token's point-aware split is unverified here, which is a different object; the caution is real but misfiled, and the count it declines is in fact available for the object actually quoted.
P17-001.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: engage the rival this row's own scope sentence raises - a cut at the oshb:Jer.46.1 / oshb:Jer.46.2 seam leaving the collection-scope rubric its own unit - and decide it on stated grounds; the rival now in the field is a different seam. Author work is to state and decide the rival in that field; moving the seam is a boundary proposal for owner adoption, never author work. boundary_rationale at oshb:Jer.46.11: replace 'The vision's first direct address' with the first named vocative, or keep a first-claim only with an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit. boundary_rationale at oshb:Jer.46.10: re-attach the hedge to the lamed-prefixed title stack actually quoted, or cite that object's own byte-attested site count instead of withholding one. Test: each cure must be re-derivable from the cited verse's own bytes for the object it names - the tests that killed the originals are reading oshb:Jer.46.3 and oshb:Jer.46.9 for imperatives before calling oshb:Jer.46.11 a first, and reading the oshb:Jer.46.10 form for its prefix before naming the sweep object.

P17-002.challenge_claim: The sole ground given for rejecting the strongest rival - that the heading carries no content of its own once split from the proclamation it frames - is false about Jer.46.13; the class generalization backing it carries no sweep digit and is contradicted at three sites of the eleven-verse header list; and the English run for 46:18 is left without its curly delimiter.
P17-002.grounds: The decisive half is upheld and the middle half needs correcting on both framing and digit. Upheld: oshb:Jer.46.13 (byte) carries its own topic clause, לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם - Nebuchadnezzar's coming to strike the land of Egypt - which is content, and is what makes the verse a topical header at all; the row quotes that very clause in its own boundary prose and then rejects the rival on the ground that the verse has no content of its own. Whatever decides that rival, this ground cannot. Correction: the class claim is that the book's other prose headers open onto their first movement rather than standing as isolated citations, and a header verse that is itself content-free and hands the movement to the next verse is not a counter-instance to that reading, so 'contradicted' overstates. What is true, and is the residual defect, is that the claim is an undigited class generalization and that the class does not behave uniformly in the respect invoked: of the eleven verses carrying the hadavar-asher-hayah header shape, four are content-free - oshb:Jer.7.1, oshb:Jer.11.1, oshb:Jer.18.1 and oshb:Jer.30.1, byte-identical eight-token headers reading הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר - and seven carry topic material. Four, not three; oshb:Jer.18.1 belongs in the count object, and a digit that names the wrong extension is itself a defect. The declared heuristic-false-positive disposition on this field's universal-claim flags does not survive: those flags land on this ground and on this generalization, and both are defects. The third item verifies in substance: the staged folded text of web:Jer.46.18 opens its second run with a curly double quote and the row's rendering substitutes a straight one, leaving that run undelimited; the run is otherwise character-for-character the staged text, so the defect is exactly the substitution, not a paraphrase.
P17-002.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the ground that the heading carries no content of its own - oshb:Jer.46.13's own topic clause refutes it - and decide the rival on a ground the bytes support, or re-decide it. Same field: either drop the class generalization about the book's other prose headers or give it a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; on bytes the eleven-verse header class splits four content-free against seven content-bearing, so no uniform pattern may be asserted bare. boundary_rationale, the web:Jer.46.18 run: restore the curly opening the staged folded text carries on the second run, so the run is delimited and character-exact against that text. Test: the replacement ground must survive being read against oshb:Jer.46.13's own bytes - that reading killed the original - and every WEB run in the field must pass a character-for-character comparison with the staged folded text, run by run rather than at the one cited site.

P17-003.challenge_claim: The inclusio framing is overstated at the bytes: the shared element is a construct standing three times in the chapter, the same second-person address with that construct already stands at 46:11 across two row seams and undisclosed, the closing occurrence is third-person rather than the address the opening verse carries, and the framing claim carries no sweep digit.
P17-003.grounds: The substance is upheld with its framing corrected: the bracket is real at the construct level and cannot bear the weight the row puts on it. A token-bound skeleton sweep of the construct returns exactly three verses, all in this chapter - oshb:Jer.46.11, oshb:Jer.46.19, oshb:Jer.46.24 (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) - so 'overstated' is right where 'absent' would not be. What the bytes will not carry is the framing as written. The opening edge at oshb:Jer.46.19 (byte) is a second-person address, עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ with the vocative יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם; the closing edge at oshb:Jer.46.24 (byte) reads הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה, third-person throughout. What returns at the close is therefore the construct, not the address, and the device note's gloss of both edges as one dwelling daughter fits only the opening verse - the participle stands at oshb:Jer.46.19 and nowhere at the close, so gloss extent overruns splice extent there. The third occurrence is the material one: oshb:Jer.46.11 (byte) carries the same construct under the same second-person address, עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י with בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, eight verses earlier and outside this span, disclosed nowhere in the row and absent from its evidence refs. A byte-true device straddling a row's own seams argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and this one runs across two of them. The front seam itself survives - the address at oshb:Jer.46.19 is genuinely fresh against the oath closing before it, and the tier-3 mark there is correctly held to corroboration - but the span-bounding force claimed for the bracket does not.
P17-003.remedy: device_notes and the closing sentence of boundary_rationale: re-cut the framing claim to what the bytes bracket - the bat-Mitsrayim construct, carrying its digit and object (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) - and state that the opening edge is a second-person address while the closing edge is third-person, so the bracket is on the figure and not on the address; drop the participle from the gloss of the closing edge, which does not carry it. Same fields: disclose the third occurrence at oshb:Jer.46.11, standing outside the span under the same address, and add that ref to boundary_evidence_refs. Test: the corrected framing must survive reading both edge verses for person and form, and the cohesion disclosure must come from a sweep of the construct across the chapter rather than a note at the argued edge - that sweep is what killed the original.

P17-005.challenge_claim: The couplet's cross-verse recurrence claim is left untiered where the byte tier is exact, and the English run for 46:28 is presented with no curly delimiter, with a source curly mark rendered straight inside it.
P17-005.grounds: Both items verify. The recurrence is exact at the byte tier: the four-token run אַל תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ stands identically at oshb:Jer.46.27 and oshb:Jer.46.28 (byte), the sole divergence being the conjunction on the opening word - וְ֠אַתָּה at oshb:Jer.46.27 against אַ֠תָּה at oshb:Jer.46.28 (byte). The row calls that nearly verbatim with no tier named, where every recurrence claim is tier-labelled at write time and where naming the tier would strengthen this row's own cohesion argument rather than weaken it. The quote mechanics also hold: the staged folded text of web:Jer.46.28 carries a curly closing mark after the servant address, and the row's rendering substitutes a straight double quote there - a character-level divergence inside a run presented as verbatim, and the same substitution class that stands in this row's neighbourhood at web:Jer.46.18. On the missing opening delimiter the byte record refines without dissolving the point: the staged verse text itself opens mid-quote, so no opening mark was dropped; what the row still owes is a delimited run, since the mandatory curly-plus-inline-ref pairing cannot be satisfied by an opening mark the source does not supply. Low is right - neither item touches the seam, and the rest of the unit holds: the addressee shift at oshb:Jer.46.27 is a tier-1 class, the marks at oshb:Jer.46.26, oshb:Jer.46.27 and oshb:Jer.46.28 each stand at their claimed type (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), the single paseq at oshb:Jer.46.28 is cited count-only, no ketiv/qere falls in the span, and the type deviation is disclosed.
P17-005.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'nearly verbatim' with the tier-named claim - the four-token address run is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.46.27 and oshb:Jer.46.28, diverging only in the conjunction on the opening word. Same field, the web:Jer.46.28 run: restore the curly closing mark the staged folded text carries after the servant address, and give the run its own opening delimiter, since the staged verse opens mid-quote and supplies none to inherit. Test: every WEB run in the field must pass a character-for-character comparison against the staged folded text, run by run rather than at the cited site - that comparison is what killed the original - and the recurrence sentence must name the tier it collates at.

P17-006.challenge_claim: The header's dating element is labelled a relative clause in two fields, but its bytes are a temporal clause, and the verse's only relative particle heads the header shape itself.
P17-006.grounds: Upheld on the verse's bytes. At oshb:Jer.47.1 (byte) the dating element is בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכֶּ֥ה פַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת עַזָּֽה - beterem plus a prefix-conjugation verb, a temporal subordinate clause - and the other witness renders it the same way, before Pharaoh struck Gaza. The verse's single relative particle is אֲשֶׁ֨ר, which opens the asher-hayah header shape itself, so the label both misassigns the form class and, read literally, would hand the header's own particle to the date. A form-class label is a byte-checkable claim under the same discipline as a digit, and this one is asserted twice, in the boundary prose and again in the device note, with the unit carried at high confidence and no morphology layer in the substrate to have suggested otherwise. Low is right: nothing in the seam turns on the label. The rest verifies - the header at oshb:Jer.47.1 is one of the four verses carrying that shape, the divine-speech formula at oshb:Jer.47.2 sets this frame rather than changing an established one, the marks at oshb:Jer.47.1 and oshb:Jer.47.5 stand at their claimed type with the preceding mark at oshb:Jer.46.28 cited correctly (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), the single paseq at oshb:Jer.47.2 is cited count-only, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.
P17-006.remedy: boundary_rationale and device_notes: replace 'relative clause' in both fields with the byte-true class - a temporal clause on beterem plus a prefix-conjugation verb - and, if the contrast with the numbered-year date frames is kept, state it as a difference of clause type rather than of relativization. Test: the corrected label must be re-derivable from oshb:Jer.47.1's own bytes, and reading that verse for its relative particle must land on the header shape and not on the date - that reading is what killed the original.

P17-009.challenge_claim: Two items. Raised by both challenges: the front-seam warrant at Jer.48.9 is a plural imperative with no named vocative addressee - the same shape the unit closing at Jer.48.8 refused as a seam at Jer.48.6 on exactly that no-named-vocative ground - and the row reconciles the two nowhere, no other tier-1 or tier-3 signal falling at the seam. Raised by one challenge: the singleness asserted for the slackness noun at Jer.48.10 is stated in words only, with neither of the two digits that would make the point.
P17-009.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects on one row, not one defect twice. Item 1 (raised by both), the front-seam parity objection: byte-true as far as it goes. oshb:Jer.48.9 opens תְּנוּ (byte), a plural imperative, with Moab standing in the lamed phrase לְמוֹאָ֔ב (oshb:Jer.48.9, byte) and a third-person suffix on her cities, so no vocative addressee is named; oshb:Jer.48.6 opens נֻ֖סוּ מַלְּט֣וּ (byte), likewise plural imperatives with a second-person plural suffix and no vocative. Correction to the objection's evidence: Moab is not named at all in oshb:Jer.48.6, so the two verses are not parallel in the way one challenge states them; the genuinely shared feature is the absent vocative, not third-person reference to Moab. The only differentiator the row offers is a change of figure (wings against flight on foot), which is texture rather than a device class, so the warrant as written would license a cut at oshb:Jer.48.6 just as well. That is the real defect, and it is a warrant-and-disclosure defect, not evidence that the span is wrong. NEW FINDING, undisclosed by the row and by both challenges: oshb:Jer.48.8 closes verse-final on אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.8, byte), a three-token relative-clause divine speech attribution standing in exactly one verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, contiguous token sequence, skeleton tier) - a speech-formula-class closure signal on the near side of the seam, which under the ruled ordering corroborates a close wherever a fresh onset follows, as the imperative at oshb:Jer.48.9 does. No comparable attribution stands before oshb:Jer.48.6, which is exactly the distinction the row fails to draw. Seam environment re-derived: within Jer 48 the messenger formula stands only at oshb:Jer.48.1 and oshb:Jer.48.40 (sweep: 2 verses, koh-amar bigram, skeleton tier), the chapter's only inventoried woe site and its only nation header both sit at oshb:Jer.48.1 (1 site each, this chapter), and the sole parashah mark anywhere in oshb:Jer.48.1-Jer.48.30 is the setumah at oshb:Jer.48.11 (1 mark) (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets) - so the negative half of the objection verifies. Item 2 (raised by one challenge), the undigited exclusivity: upheld outright. The row asserts the slackness noun רְמִיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.48.10, byte) is 'the single attested token at this one site' and appeals to 'every occurrence of the prophet's own name', with no digit anywhere in the field. The digits exist and are exact: whole-token equality returns 1 verse at byte and at skeleton tier (oshb:Jer.48.10); the bare consonantal substring returns 118 verses and 132 token occurrences, because the prophet's name carries that skeleton. An exclusivity claim is never tier-dampened, so the byte label on the splice does not cover it. NEW FINDING on the declared-flag queue for this row: the three universals flags split - the one landing on the singleness sentence marks a real defect, while the two 'never' flags (never as a book-wide count; never generalized into a count) are self-scoped statements about the row's own practice and are genuine false positives that need no edit. Severity held at medium: a front-seam warrant that cannot survive the neighbour-parity test plus an exclusivity claim with no sweep digit; no boundary change is proposed and none is needed.
P17-009.remedy: Work order, fields boundary_rationale (primary) and device_notes (dependent). (1) In boundary_rationale, replace the fresh-figure differentiator with the byte-attested seam evidence: splice the verse-final speech attribution from oshb:Jer.48.8, cite it at byte tier with its digit (sweep: 1 verse), keep the imperative onset at oshb:Jer.48.9 as the far-side signal, and state explicitly that no such closing attribution precedes oshb:Jer.48.6. TEST THAT KILLED THE ORIGINAL: the rewritten warrant, applied verbatim at oshb:Jer.48.6, must NOT generate a seam there; any wording that would equally license a cut at oshb:Jer.48.6 fails. (2) In boundary_rationale, either give the singleness sentence an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit (token-bound: 1 verse; bare consonantal substring: 118 verses, 132 token occurrences) or delete the singleness wording; TEST: the exclusivity sentence must carry a digit naming the swept object and its unit in the same sentence, and a byte-tier label does not substitute. (3) Leave the two self-scoped statements in boundary_rationale and device_notes as written - they are false positives. No span change is ordered or proposed: the boundary stands on the evidence above; any respan would be a proposal requiring adoption.

P17-011.challenge_claim: Both challenges, one and the same defect: the row calls Jer.48.20 the second of the book's twelve doubled ketiv/qere verses, when in that book-ordered inventory it stands eighth (Jer.48.7 being seventh); the cure is to drop the ordinal.
P17-011.grounds: Both challenges raise one and the same defect, and it is upheld. Re-derived from the byte-derived mark inventory rather than from either challenge's list: the verses carrying more than one variant note, in book order, are Jer.3.19, Jer.4.19, Jer.6.25, Jer.13.20, Jer.14.14, Jer.22.23, Jer.48.7, Jer.48.20, Jer.49.39, Jer.50.6, Jer.50.11 and Jer.51.34 (12 verses, inside a book-wide layer of 141 notes over 124 verses, single-witness). oshb:Jer.48.20 is the EIGHTH member and carries exactly two notes; oshb:Jer.48.7 is the seventh. The row's sentence scopes the set to the book, so no chapter-scoped reading rescues the ordinal: within ch 48 the site would be second, but that is not what the field says, and the scope is stated there explicitly. Object check, not digit check: the challenges' count object (multi-note verses, book order) is the right object and their digit holds, so this is a true ordinal error against the campaign's largest disclosure inventory rather than a reproduced digit attached to the wrong object. Everything else the row discloses for its span verifies independently and completely: one variant note at oshb:Jer.48.18 and two at oshb:Jer.48.20, each given written-against-read in the correct direction; one paseq seg at oshb:Jer.48.20 cited count-only with no intra-verse position (single-witness, seg layer); and no parashah mark and no further paseq seg anywhere in oshb:Jer.48.17-Jer.48.20 (0 marks, 1 seg in the span), with none claimed. Severity medium: a digit-class error in the heaviest disclosure layer, curable in one sentence with no consequence for the span.
P17-011.remedy: Work order, field boundary_rationale. Delete 'the second of' from the doubled-note sentence and state membership in the twelve without an ordinal, exactly as the same disclosure is made at oshb:Jer.48.7; if an ordinal is wanted, write the book-order position (eighth of twelve) or name the chapter scope explicitly with its own digit. Leave both written-against-read pairs and the paseq disclosure as they stand - both verify. TEST THAT KILLED THE ORIGINAL: any ordinal in a mark-disclosure claim must resolve against the book-order list of multi-note verses (3:19, 4:19, 6:25, 13:20, 14:14, 22:23, 48:7, 48:20, 49:39, 50:6, 50:11, 51:34); a scope-less ordinal fails by default.

P17-012.challenge_claim: Three items on one row: the closing form contrast leans on translation-layer poetry-line metadata, states that metadata inaccurately, and names the staged data key verbatim in prose; and the rationale's statement that no fresh tier-1 onset follows at Jer.48.26 conflicts with the imperative-onset warrant used at Jer.48.9, understating the row's own closing warrant.
P17-012.grounds: All three items are real; the third one's framing needs correcting, and that correction explains why the same row can be read as sound or as defective depending on which field is read. Item 1, the line-count texture: upheld on its policy ground. Modern poetry-line breaks are translation-layer metadata that is never boundary evidence and never counterevidence, so it cannot do the distinguishing work device_notes assigns it (texture distinguishing this span from the scene before it and the scene after it). The figures also fail to support the wording: in the staged folded text the in-span counts run 1, 0, 0, 1, 1 across web:Jer.48.21-Jer.48.25 against 3, 4, 2, 3 across web:Jer.48.17-Jer.48.20 and 3 at web:Jer.48.26 - a relative contrast in which three of the five in-span verses carry a line, not a run at or near zero. Independently re-derived; the challenge's digits are exact. Item 2, the leaked key: real, with its class corrected - what surfaces in device_notes is a staged data FIELD name, machine register inside row prose, rather than a staged file name or stem; the cure is identical either way. Item 3, the onset misclassification: real, and its locus is sharper than the challenge states. NEW FINDING: the conflict is not primarily with the neighbouring seam at Jer.48.9 - it is INSIDE this row. boundary_rationale calls oshb:Jer.48.26 'a fresh imperative with a different figure' and, in the same sentence, says the row stops there 'since no fresh tier-1 onset follows immediately at that verse'; strongest_rejected_alternative says the opposite, that the form 'shifts cleanly' into 'a fresh imperative scene with its own figure at the very next verse' and uses it as one of two independent grounds. Both statements quote the row correctly, so the row supports opposite readings of its own closing warrant field by field. The bytes settle it: oshb:Jer.48.26 opens הַשְׁכִּירֻ֕הוּ (byte), a plural imperative with object suffix and Moab in the third person - the same device class the unit beginning at that verse carries as its onset driver and the same class used as the onset driver at oshb:Jer.48.9 - while oshb:Jer.48.25 closes verse-final on נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.25, byte; the last two of the verse's seven tokens). Under the ruled ordering the closing formula therefore DOES count as corroboration, so the row's own prose understates a warrant the bytes grant it. Severity held at low: the boundary is not in question. The list form at the onset is byte-true (the names are chained by repeated conjunctions with no verbal frame between them across oshb:Jer.48.22-Jer.48.24), the closing formula is verse-final, a fresh onset follows, and the span's mark disclosure verifies complete (one variant note at oshb:Jer.48.21; no paseq seg and no parashah mark anywhere in oshb:Jer.48.21-Jer.48.25 (0 marks, 0 segs), none claimed). All three items are prose repairs with no span consequence.
P17-012.remedy: Work order, two fields. (a) device_notes: delete the clause carrying the machine line-count field name and its at-or-near-zero characterization; if a form contrast is kept, ground it only in the byte-attested chain of repeated conjunctions across oshb:Jer.48.22-Jer.48.24. TEST: no translation-layer line or paragraph datum may appear in any field as a distinguishing or corroborating signal in either direction, and no staged data field name may appear in row prose. (b) boundary_rationale: replace 'no fresh tier-1 onset follows immediately at that verse' with the byte-true statement that a plural-imperative onset does stand at oshb:Jer.48.26 (splice the onset token, byte tier), so the verse-final formula at oshb:Jer.48.25 is closure corroboration under the ruled ordering, and align the sentence with strongest_rejected_alternative, which already carries the two-ground reading. TEST THAT KILLED THE ORIGINAL: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative must be read together and must not assert opposite things about the same verse; any closure claim must name the following verse's onset device class with its byte citation. Consolidation note, no per-row action: the plural imperative without a named vocative is treated as a seam driver at Jer.48.9 and Jer.48.26 and denied at Jer.48.6 and inside this row's own rationale at Jer.48.26 - one consistent treatment of that class across the Moab stretch is a sweep-shaped order, not a single-row edit.

P17-013.challenge_claim: The middle step of the row's own onset-escalation argument is byte-false: Moab is not named in the verse where the row says the second person turns onto Moab by name.
P17-013.grounds: Re-derived from the source bytes. The consonantal skeleton of MT 48:27 carries no Moab token at all; the one nation named there is Israel, standing as the object of the derision rather than as the addressee -- הָיָ֤ה לְךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.48.27, byte tier). Inside the span the Moab token stands only at the two flanking verses (sweep: 2 of the span's 3 verses): the third-person object of the drunkenness imperative, מוֹאָב֙ (oshb:Jer.48.26, byte tier), and the vocative יֹשְׁבֵ֖י מוֹאָ֑ב (oshb:Jer.48.28, byte tier). The second-person forms at the middle verse are pronominal and suffixal only -- לְךָ֙ and דְבָרֶ֥יךָ (oshb:Jer.48.27, byte tier). The rationale's sentence therefore fails on the words 'by name', and the three-rung escalation it builds (unnamed third party, then Moab named in the second person, then explicit vocative) collapses to two rungs, taking with it the stated warrant for holding these three verses as one taunt. Everything else on the row re-verifies: all four of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses; the variant note at MT 48:27 is real (1 note, single-witness) and correctly disclosed written-against-read, and the row neither counts nor slices across it; the paseq at that same verse is real (1 seg, single-witness) and correctly disclosed count-only with no intra-verse position asserted; no parashah mark falls anywhere inside the span, so no mark disclosure is owed and the absence is not treated as counterevidence.
P17-013.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the clause 'a rhetorical question turns the second person onto Moab by name' with a formulation the bytes support -- second-person address without the nation named, the nation named at that verse being Israel as the object of the derision -- and re-state the escalation as two rungs (third-person object at Jer.48.26, explicit vocative at Jer.48.28). Dependent field: device_notes' sentence on where second-person address to Moab begins must be re-read against the corrected rungs, since it currently leans on the deleted middle rung. Test the cure must pass: a token-bound sweep of the Moab token across Jer.48.26-Jer.48.28 must return the two flanking verses only, and no sentence in any field may attribute the name to the middle verse. Span, unit_type and confidence are untouched; this is a prose-and-warrant repair, not a boundary change.

P17-014.challenge_claim: Item one: the quoted WEB wording at three internal attribution points renders the source's curly quotation marks as straight ASCII quotes, and at Jer.48.38 additionally appends a curly closing mark the source does not carry. Item two: the rejected alternative denies any byte-attested new addressee inside the eleven-verse span while the row's own rationale identifies one, and the bytes side with the rationale.
P17-014.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one. Item two stands exactly as put and is upheld unchanged: the held-together warrant asserts that none of the internal split candidates reopens the lament frame with a fresh divine-speech formula, a woe, or a new addressee of its own, and it names the direct address to the vine of Sibmah as one of those very candidates; the bytes at that site carry exactly a new addressee -- אֶבְכֶּה לָּךְ֙ הַגֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה נְטִֽישֹׁתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.48.32, byte tier), a second-person feminine singular pronoun, a vocative, and a second-person feminine singular suffix, with two further such suffixes closing the verse -- while the verse before it is first-person singular speech about Moab in the third person. The rationale concedes the direct address in so many words, so the two fields cannot both stand. Item one needs correction on two points. First, the substitution class is real and byte-confirmed, but it stands at FOUR quoted spans in this field, not three: the source's curly marks are rendered as straight ASCII twice inside the quotation of web:Jer.48.30, twice inside web:Jer.48.35, once inside web:Jer.48.38 and once inside this field's forward-looking quotation of web:Jer.48.40 -- six substituted marks over four spans. Second, the curly pair enclosing each quoted span is NOT an extra mark: it is the mandated wrapper for WEB text carrying an inline web: ref in the same field, and it is applied uniformly across every one of this field's eleven quoted spans, so singling out the trailing mark at Jer.48.38 as an anomaly misreads the convention; the only defect is the internal downgrade. Independently re-derived and confirmed: the closure formula stands at exactly three verses inside the span (MT 48:30, 48:35, 48:38), the row engages all three and correctly holds the verse-final one as corroboration because no fresh tier-1 onset follows it; the single parashah mark in the span is the SAMEKH closing MT 48:39; and there are no variant notes and no paseq segs anywhere in MT 48:29-48:39, none claimed. All thirteen of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses.
P17-014.remedy: boundary_rationale: restore the source's own curly quotation marks inside the quoted runs of web:Jer.48.30 (two marks), web:Jer.48.35 (two), web:Jer.48.38 (one) and web:Jer.48.40 (one), leaving the enclosing wrapper pair as it stands. strongest_rejected_alternative: drop the new-addressee disjunct, or replace it with an argued statement of why a vocative to a vine is not an addressee change of the class that cuts -- the bare denial cannot stand beside the rationale's own concession. Test the cures must pass: (a) a CODEPOINT-EXACT comparison of each quoted run against the staged WEB text of its cited verse, character for character -- note that the standing verbatim-quote check passes this field clean today, because its verbatim arm normalises punctuation before comparing and its straight-delimiter arm skips spans shorter than three words, so 'the quote check is green' is NOT an adequate test for this class; (b) the repaired rejected_alternative must survive a byte read of oshb:Jer.48.32 that names the second-person feminine singular forms. No boundary change is proposed.

P17-015.challenge_claim: Item one: two of the span's WEB quotations render the source's curly quotation marks as straight ASCII quotes. Item two: the novelty leg of the onset warrant is an undigited exclusivity claim the bytes contradict -- the eagle figure is neither unused nor unlike anything before it, and this unit's own second verse recurs at byte tier later in the same nations block; a second undigited exclusivity sits in the closing parenthesis about the interjection.
P17-015.grounds: Distinct defects, both upheld; only the smallest leg of item two needs a correction, stated below. Item one verifies exactly: the source carries a curly opening mark immediately after the introductory clause of web:Jer.48.40 and a curly closing mark immediately before the closing attribution of web:Jer.48.43, and this field substitutes a straight ASCII mark at both -- two spans, one mark each, and the digit two is right for this row. Item two, novelty leg: the eagle noun stands at four verses book-wide by consonantal sweep (4:13, 48:40, 49:16, 49:22 -- sweep: 4 verses), so an earlier eagle figure precedes this onset; the narrower kaf-prefixed comparative shape stands at three (48:40, 49:16, 49:22 -- sweep: 3 verses), of which this onset is the first. Neither the rationale's 'unlike anything before it' nor the rejected alternative's 'unused eagle figure' names its object or carries a digit, which the exclusivity discipline requires and which no tier label may dampen. Item two, recurrence leg, independently re-derived at token level: MT 48:41 tokens 4-6, וְֽ֠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י (oshb:Jer.48.41, byte tier), are token-for-token identical, accents included, to MT 49:22 tokens 8-10, and MT 48:41 tokens 8-12, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כְּלֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.41, byte tier), to MT 49:22 tokens 12-16 -- eight of the nine words of that stretch, broken only by the nation name (Moab against Edom), and MT 49:22 additionally opens on the same eagle-and-outspread-wings image under a different verb pattern. That is an undisclosed byte-tier recurrence inside the same nations collection bearing directly on how distinctive this onset is, and it is exactly the recurrence class that must be tier-labelled at write time. CORRECTION to the third and smallest leg: the closing parenthesis about the interjection is ambiguous rather than flatly false. Read as a claim that this interjection is not used elsewhere in the book it is false -- the interjection at MT 48:46, אוֹי (oshb:Jer.48.46, byte tier), stands at eight verses token-bound (4:13, 4:31, 6:4, 10:19, 13:27, 15:10, 45:3, 48:46 -- sweep: 8 verses). Read as a claim that it is not the woe-oracle lexeme used elsewhere it is true -- that lexeme, ה֗וֹי (oshb:Jer.47.6, byte tier), stands at seven verses token-bound (sweep: 7 verses). The sound finding is that the parenthesis is an undigited, scope-ambiguous exclusivity claim, not that it is false as written. The onset itself is NOT contested and re-verifies: the verse-initial divine-speech formula at MT 48:40 is byte-true and divine-mouthed, the SAMEKH closing MT 48:39 sits at this row's front seam and is correctly typed and tier-held, the variant note and the apparatus note at MT 48:44 are both real and correctly disclosed as single-witness, no other disclosure-bearing mark falls inside the span, the self-magnification clause is a two-verse object (sweep: 2 verses) matching at skeleton tier only exactly as the row states, and all nine of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses.
P17-015.remedy: boundary_rationale: restore the source's curly marks inside the quoted runs of web:Jer.48.40 and web:Jer.48.43; replace 'an eagle figure unlike anything before it' with a scoped, digit-bearing formulation naming the swept object (the eagle noun at four verses book-wide; the kaf-prefixed comparative shape at three, this site the first of them); and re-cut the closing parenthesis so its object is explicit -- the interjection here is the lexeme distinct from the woe-oracle lexeme, with a digit for each. strongest_rejected_alternative: delete 'unused' or replace the leg with the digit-bearing form; the leg currently carries part of the weight against the shared-divine-speaker rival. device_notes: add the undisclosed recurrence with its tier and extent -- the eight-of-nine-word overlap between oshb:Jer.48.41 and oshb:Jer.49.22 at byte tier, broken only by the nation name -- and state how the onset's distinctiveness survives it. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of any driver re-weighting and must be re-read if the novelty leg is dropped rather than repaired. Tests the cures must pass: a codepoint-exact comparison of each quoted run against the staged WEB text of its cited verse (the standing quote check normalises punctuation and will not catch the substitution); every exclusivity word in every field carrying an adjacent digit-bearing sweep that names its object and unit; and a token-level re-collation of the two Jer.48.41 runs against oshb:Jer.49.22 reproducing the byte-tier match. No boundary change is proposed.

P17-016.challenge_claim: The closing texture note mis-locates the book's colophon outside the collection this unit declares for itself, when that colophon is the collection's own terminal verse.
P17-016.grounds: Upheld on the row's own fields plus the bytes. The device note frames this unit's terminus line as a smaller-scope model of the book's closing colophon and places that colophon well beyond this collection's span; but the row's own parent_collection field declares the collection running through Jer.51.64, and the colophon stands at that very verse -- so it is the collection's last verse, not anything beyond it. The two lines are formally kin at the bytes, opening on an identical pointed pair, tipcha included: עַד הֵ֖נָּה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט מוֹאָֽב (oshb:Jer.48.47, byte tier) beside עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.51.64, byte tier); that consonantal opening stands at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses). Stating the containment correctly strengthens the terminus argument rather than weakening it, so this is a fix-in-place wording defect and not a boundary dispute. ADDITIONAL, same sentence: it calls the collection's span 'dated', which no header in that collection supplies -- fold that word into the same rewrite. The boundary is NOT contested and re-verifies: the interjection opening the span is byte-true and is genuinely the other lexeme from the one cited against it, and both runs reach byte tier at their cited verses; the terminus clause is byte-attested and does close the whole Moab oracle rather than only this unit; the SAMEKH at MT 48:47 is real and correctly typed, witnessed and tier-held; the layout fold at web:Jer.48.47 is real in the staged English layer (1 continuation paragraph) and correctly held as tier-4 metadata that is evidence in neither direction; neither verse carries a variant note or a paseq seg, and none is claimed.
P17-016.remedy: device_notes: rewrite the closing sentence so the containment is right -- the terminus line is a sub-unit line on the model of the book's own closing colophon, which stands at the final verse of the collection this unit belongs to rather than beyond it -- and drop the word 'dated' from the description of that collection's span. Test the cure must pass: the rewritten sentence must be consistent with this row's own parent_collection value, and any verse it names must resolve inside that declared range. No boundary change, no confidence change.

P18-001.challenge_claim: Five defects, one load-bearing for the rear seam: the divine-title stack does not close the span's last verse; the closure contrast drawn against the second verse is incomplete because that verse carries both formulas; the stack is mis-counted as a two-site object; the type label calls an undated header dated; and the parashah sentence calls the mark one chapter back the nearest to this span while a mark one verse past the span goes undisclosed.
P18-001.grounds: Three legs upheld, two corrected. UPHELD and load-bearing: the rationale ends the span on a terror pronouncement said to close on the divine-title stack. In the bytes MT 49:5 runs sixteen tokens, the stack נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת (oshb:Jer.49.5, byte tier) occupies tokens 4-7, and eight tokens follow it -- מִכָּל סְבִיבָ֑יִךְ וְנִדַּחְתֶּם֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּ֖ץ לַנֹּדֵֽד (oshb:Jer.49.5, byte tier) -- matching the WEB continuation of the same verse. The stack is medial in both witnesses, so no closure formula stands at the rear seam this row cuts, and under the ruled treatment of that formula as closure corroboration only, the seam loses the closure signal the sentence implies. UPHELD: the device note contrasts the perfect-verb tag closing the second verse against the participial formula said to close the last. MT 49:2 does close on the perfect-verb tag, אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.49.2, byte tier), but the same verse also carries the participial formula mid-verse at tokens 4-5, נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.49.2, byte tier), so the formulas are not distributed one per verse and the contrast fails at both ends. UPHELD: the type label reads this as a dated nation-header oracle; the header verse is a lamed-prefixed nation name bound to a divine-speech formula and carries no year, reign or month token of any shape, and it is absent from the book's nineteen classified date-candidate sites (sweep: 19 classified verses; MT 49:1 not among them). P18-004.challenge_claim: Item one: the span's only disclosed seam driver is a bare reintroduction of the divine-speech formula by the same speaker already carrying the oracle through the preceding span, without a disclosed addressee, scene or frame-owner change to justify treating the restart as a fresh onset. The two neighbouring header rows each disclose an accompanying addressee shift; this one does not. This does NOT refute the boundary: a verse-initial messenger-formula restart standing immediately behind a parashah break is a tier-1 signal and may drive a seam. What it defeats is the sufficiency of the warrant AS DISCLOSED and the confidence resting on it. Paseq: the rationale places the mark later in the verse in the same sentence that says the inventory gives no position within it. The seg layer is count-only and intra-verse position is unsourceable, so the first half of the sentence asserts what the second half says cannot be known; the object itself is real (1 seg at MT 49:12, single-witness) and only the position words go. Gloss extent: the closing sentence names Bozrah as an astonishment and a perpetual waste. REFINEMENT 2, framing: the declared heuristic disposition on that sentence HOLDS on the axis it was tested against -- the wording is not an unswept exclusivity claim -- and that axis never tests substantive consistency, so both readings stand and only the second is a defect; the cure is to fix the sentence, not to relabel the flag. P18-011.grounds: The headline claim verifies on both legs; one sub-claim is refuted and one residual is stronger than stated. Form class: the object marker settles it -- אֶת שבית שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.39, byte tier) puts the second variant pair immediately after the marker, as the NOUN the preceding verb governs, and the same construction without variants at the Ammon coda, אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier), shows it unambiguously; with no morphology layer staged, a form-class label of that reach is a byte-checkable claim and the bytes refuse it. The variant census defines a closed class of TWELVE doubled-note verses and names MT 50:11 among them at 4 notes, beside MT 50:6 at 2 and this unit's own verse at 2; the sentence uses that class exactly and parenthesizes the four-note count besides, so it is precise rather than misleading. REFINED residual, the most useful correction here: the Ammon idiom is indeed invoked with no quoted form and no tier, and the recurrence is byte tier -- but on the READ side only. The run אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier) is byte-identical to the corresponding run at this unit's verse under both read forms, while the written forms differ at both tokens; the identity is qere-borne, which is exactly what a doubled-note site obliges the prose to disclose. One point flagged and NOT decided, because it is owner-level: whether the latter-days temporal frame counts as a fresh tier-1 onset is what licenses the closure formula ending Jer.49.38 to close under the ruled closure-corroboration-only treatment; it stands neither among the enumerated onset classes nor excluded from them, and that reading governs this unit's confidence.
P18-011.remedy: device_notes: replace 'the restoration idiom's own two verbs' with the correct form classes -- the verb, and the object noun it governs standing after the object marker -- and add the recurrence tier with its condition: byte-identical to the run at Jer.49.6 under the READ forms only, the written forms differing at both tokens. boundary_rationale: re-anchor the parashah sentence so the entry keyed to MT 49:39 corroborates the back seam at Jer.49.39|Jer.50.1, and state that no mark-layer entry falls at the front seam at Jer.49.38|Jer.49.39; add the single-witness and tier-3 labels. confidence: lower from high, since the front seam's only signal is the content pivot plus the temporal frame. LEAVE UNCHANGED: the doubled-note comparison at Jer.50.6 and Jer.50.11 -- it matches the census class and its counts exactly. CURE TEST: the corrected form-class sentence must survive a read-back against the object marker standing in the verse, and the re-anchored mark sentence must name WHICH seam the entry sits on -- the two tests the original failed. ROUTE TO THE OWNER, not the author wave: whether a latter-days temporal frame is a fresh tier-1 onset for closure-formula purposes.

P18-012.challenge_claim: Convergent on one defect: the curly-quoted English at Jer.50.2 runs through the first god-name while the Hebrew splice beside it stops at the city name -- and the splice additionally opens on an imperative the gloss does not render, so the extents diverge in both directions. P18-012.grounds: The convergent core is one and the same defect, and the two-directional statement is the accurate one. The parashah entries keyed to MT 49:39 and MT 50:5 leave MT 50:1 through MT 50:4 unmarked, so the segment opening after MT 49:39 does run across this unit's back seam at Jer.50.3|Jer.50.4 while the same layer is cited at the front seam. The header at Jer.49.34 does OPEN its own unit, whose material closes at Jer.49.39, so 'just closed at Jer.49.34' misplaces it; and the sentence opening 'This Jer.49.39, the Elam restoration coda' is malformed as written. NOT DISTURBED, because they re-verify: the davar-asher-dibber header shape at Jer.50.1, recorded in the header census as its own non-lamed shape and correctly held apart from the three word-event shapes and from the nations-header shape at Jer.49.34; the summons splice matching its gloss exactly; and the front-seam entry keyed to MT 49:39. P18-012.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss so its extent equals the splice's -- either narrow the curly-quoted English to the words the splice covers, INCLUDING the imperative it opens on, or extend the splice through the god-name material the gloss already reaches; one edit, not two half-edits. Repair the malformed sentence opening 'This Jer.49.39', and replace 'just closed at Jer.49.34' with the header's actual role -- it opens its unit, whose material closes at Jer.49.39. Add one sentence recording that no mark-layer entry falls inside Jer.50.1-Jer.50.3 and that the segment opening after MT 49:39 runs past this unit's back seam, disclosed as tier-3 weak and single-witness and NOT as counterevidence in either direction; add the single-witness and tier-3 labels to the front-seam citation. P18-013.challenge_claim: Two separate challenges. First: the closing curly excerpt for Jer.50.5 is not byte-verbatim against the staged translation and carries no inline web: citation of its own. The seam itself survives the correction: the turn from Babylon's fall to the children of Israel and Judah is a scene-and-participant change, a tier-1 class in its own right, and the row's own prose already states it. Disclosure verifies: SAMEKH at MT 50:5 (tier-3, single witness), no paseq and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in MT 50:4-50:5. The declared heuristic entry on the pairing sentence is a keyword match on non-exclusive prose and is confirmed a false positive — that disposition does not reach the recurrence-discipline defect, which is a different object.
P18-013.remedy: Two orders, span unchanged. (a) boundary_rationale: re-splice the Jer.50.5 excerpt from the staged translation at exact case (“Come, and join yourselves to Yahweh in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.”) and pair it with an inline web:Jer.50.5 ref adjacent to the excerpt in the same field. P18-015.challenge_claim: The row places the Jer.50.8 ketiv/qere note on the verse's closing verb while the verse's own bytes put it mid-verse; the ketiv and qere are glossed inside curly double quotes the book reserves for translation text; and at Jer.50.9 the English gloss begins one word earlier than the spliced run.

(a) Replace 'the verse's closing verb carries a ketiv/qere note at Jer.50.8' with a byte-true location — the note stands mid-verse at tokens 6-7 of 11 and the verse's own closing clause carries no note — or splice the ketiv and its qere from source instead of describing their position. (b) Re-set both ketiv/qere glosses in straight quotes; if the translation's own imperative is quoted, quote it at exact case with an inline web:Jer.50.8 ref beside it. (c) Extend the Jer.50.9 splice to open at the first-person pronoun, or re-cut the English gloss to open where the splice opens, so the two extents match. Tests the cure must pass: every located claim in a ketiv/qere verse must be reproducible from that verse's own token sequence, and no curly-quoted run may stand that is not verbatim staged translation text at exact case with its own ref.

P18-016.grounds: The chapter attribution is the SAME defect in both challenges; the excerpt-mechanics point and the refrain-object point are DISTINCT from it and from each other. (b) boundary_rationale: re-splice the Jer.50.13 excerpt at exact case (“Everyone who goes by Babylon will be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.”) and pair it with an inline web:Jer.50.13 ref in the same field. P18-020.challenge_claim: The opening excerpt splices two non-adjacent parts of Jer.50.21 with an ellipsis and presents them inside one curly quotation as if continuous, silently dropping the middle clause — a verbatim violation.
P18-020.grounds: The defect is real but the framing and the severity are both wrong. The paired splice runs tokens 1-8 of 17 and retains עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ (oshb:Jer.50.21, byte tier), the very words the English elides, so the Hebrew extent exceeds the English extent it is offered as glossing. What then does the holding-together work in the row's own prose is the flanking setumah pair, tier-3 and single-witness, which cannot carry it. NEW, named by neither challenge: oshb:Jer.51.26 also closes verse-final with נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, immediately before that imperative onset - the same closure-plus-fresh-onset configuration this tiling treats as a seam one verse-pair earlier, where verse-final נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה at 51:24 is followed by the addressee shift at 51:25. The boundary drawn at Jer.52.12 rests on וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.12, byte tier) - the same month-and-day shape carrying only a prefixed vav and a mid-verse year gloss. The span does clear the weaker shape at 52:5 explicitly and correctly, עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.5, byte tier) being a terminus rather than an onset, which makes the silence over the stronger verse-initial shape at 52:6 an asymmetry inside the same class rather than a uniform decision about it. Test the cure must pass: no categorical claim about dates survives in the row that a dating notice standing inside Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11 falsifies, and every date-shaped verse inside the span is dispositioned per-site with its bytes quoted. A cut at 52:6 is a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work under this remedy.

P20-007.challenge_claim: The onset frame is misdescribed: the verse-initial date reckons by the Judean king's exile, not by a Babylonian king's accession, and the accession reading rests on an ordinal the Hebrew does not carry.
P20-007.grounds: Byte-confirmed. The verse-initial frame reads בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte tier) - thirty-seven years reckoned to the exile of the king of Judah. The Babylonian reckoning is a separate mid-verse element, בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מַלְכֻת֗וֹ (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte tier), and no ordinal token stands with it, so “in the first year of his reign” (web:Jer.52.31) is supplied by the English rendering. Describing the opening frame as dated to a Babylonian king's own accession therefore states of the verse-initial frame what the bytes place mid-verse, and adds a digit only the rendering carries; the same wording is reused as the ground for not folding the notice back into the preceding census, so the defect is load-bearing rather than decorative. The verse also carries two date elements, not one, so a single verse-initial signal does not describe its shape completely. A further defect in the same sentence that the challenge does not name: the interval claim placing this notice decades after the totals just given is not sourceable from the verses cited - the census entries count Nebuchadnezzar's regnal years while this onset counts from a Judean king's exile and from a reign-year phrase carrying no ordinal, so the two reckonings are not commensurable on these bytes; the claim is not shown false, but the only thing that would bridge them is an outside parallel, which is typed-relation metadata and never decides a seam here. The boundary itself is not contested and the rest verifies: the two spellings of the king's name inside 52:31 are byte-real and both belong to the same name form, neither the Jeconiah nor the Coniah form; the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.52.31 and at oshb:Jer.52.32 each stand as a single note in the inventory, so no ordinal ranking between them is asserted or needed; the petuchah at oshb:Jer.52.30 is correctly typed and framed as tier-3 weak, single-witness.
P20-007.remedy: boundary_rationale: restate the onset frame as the bytes carry it - verse-initial, thirty-seven years to the exile of the king of Judah - and name the Babylonian reign-year element as a separate mid-verse element carrying no ordinal; wherever the rendering's first-year wording is relied on, mark it as the English rendering's supplement rather than a byte fact. strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the accession-year ground with one the bytes carry - a fresh verse-initial dated frame on a different reckoning plus a scene change to Babylon - and drop the decades-interval clause unless it can be sourced from within these two witnesses. device_notes: record that this verse carries two date elements, not one. Test the cure must pass: no boundary ground states of a verse-initial frame what the bytes place mid-verse, and no digit or interval survives in the row that only the English rendering or an out-of-book parallel supplies.
